Goal: Implement a 9-card (3×3) Golf variant spike suitable for quick UI/grid experiments.

Why: Tiny rules, deterministic scoring and minimal interactions (flip/swap/discard) make this ideal as a first spike. Good fit for GridContainer (Godot) or Phaser Container.

Core objects:
- Card { rank, suit, faceUp }
- Grid[3][3]
- DrawPile, DiscardPile

Short rules (reference): players lay out 9 cards face-down in a 3×3 grid, reveal some cards, and take turns drawing from the draw pile or top of discard; drawn card may replace a grid card or be discarded; round ends when a player has all cards face-up; scoring: A=1, 2=-2, 3-10=face value, J/Q=10, K=0; three-of-a-kind columns score 0 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_(card_game)).

Resources:
- Wikipedia (rules & variants): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_(card_game)
- Brief rules/variants / BGG thread: https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Golf
- Implementation notes: grid state, explicit discard/draw piles; minimal animations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Work item must include clear rules summary, UI/UX notes, and 1–2 example test cases for scoring.

Goal: Implement Beleaguered Castle as a deterministic, open solitaire spike (all cards face-up).

Why: No hidden state; tableau of 8 piles with simple build-down-in-suit rules; good for drag-and-drop and auto-move logic experiments.

Core objects:
- Foundations (4 aces) built up by suit to Kings
- Tableau: 8 piles (arrays) built down regardless of suit; top card available
- Moves deterministic: move top of pile -> foundation or other pile; empty piles accept any card

Short rules: remove aces to foundation, deal remaining cards into 8 columns to the left/right; build foundations up by suit; tableau builds down regardless of suit; win when all cards are on foundations (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beleaguered_Castle).

Resources:
- Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beleaguered_Castle
- Solitaire reference pages and sample implementations: various open-source solitaire engines

Acceptance criteria:
- Include layout diagram, move rules, and auto-move heuristics; add example winning sequence.

# Intake Brief: 9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)

**Priority: Critical** | **Type: Feature (Epic)** | **Assignee: Map**

> First engine spike: build a playable single-round 9-Card Golf game (human vs. AI) to validate the Tableau Card Engine architecture end-to-end and surface missing abstractions before tackling larger games.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine has a working scaffold (toolchain, project structure, Phaser integration) but zero game logic, card abstractions, or gameplay features. A small, well-scoped spike is needed to validate the engine architecture end-to-end — from card data models through game rules to a playable Phaser UI — and to surface missing framework capabilities before tackling larger games. 9-Card Golf's tiny rule set (flip, swap, discard on a 3x3 grid) makes it the ideal first spike.

## Users

- **Engine developer (primary):** Validates that the engine's modular architecture (card-system, rule-engine, core-engine, ui) can support a real game. Uses the spike to discover which abstractions are missing and which APIs need refinement.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to build a complete card game using the engine modules so I can identify gaps in Card, Deck, Pile, and Grid abstractions before building more complex games."*

- **QA / AI tester:** Uses an AI player to exercise all game paths (random + greedy strategies) and produce reproducible game transcripts for regression testing.
  - *"As a tester, I want an AI opponent that can play complete games automatically so I can validate scoring, turn flow, and edge cases without manual play."*

- **Game designer (future):** Uses the completed spike as a reference implementation and template for building additional example games.
  - *"As a game designer, I want a working reference game that demonstrates how to wire up scenes, rules, and UI so I can quickly scaffold new card games."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Playable single round:** A human player can play a complete single round of 9-Card Golf against 1 AI opponent in a Phaser scene — including initial card reveal, draw/swap/discard turns, and end-of-round scoring.
2. **AI player with two strategies:** An AI player is implemented with both random (valid moves) and greedy (minimize visible score) strategies, selectable at game start or via configuration.
3. **Correct scoring:** Scoring logic correctly implements: A=1, 2=-2, 3-10=face value, J/Q=10, K=0, three-of-a-kind columns=0. Automated unit tests cover at least 3 distinct scoring scenarios (including a column-of-three-of-a-kind case).
4. **Game transcript:** Each completed game produces a JSON transcript recording the full sequence of turns, actions, and resulting board states — sufficient to replay and verify the game.
5. **Visual replay (stretch goal):** A visual replay capability captures a screenshot or canvas snapshot per turn for human review of completed games. This is a stretch goal for this spike — a dedicated dev tool for game log playback and screenshot capture will be tracked separately.

## Constraints

- **First spike — no existing game logic:** All four engine modules (card-system, core-engine, rule-engine, ui) are currently empty stubs (version constants only). Every game-related abstraction must be built from scratch during this spike.
- **Card assets incomplete:** Only 2 placeholder SVGs exist (ace_of_spades.svg, card_back.svg at 140x190px). A full 52-card deck of face assets is needed. Assets must be CC0 or permissively licensed (MIT, Apache 2.0, or similar) per project policy.
- **No assumptions about framework features:** This is the project's first game spike. Do not assume any framework features exist beyond the proven scaffold (Vite, TypeScript, Phaser, Vitest). Missing capabilities must be built or sourced as part of the spike.
- **Single round only:** Scope is limited to one round of play (one deal through to scoring). Multi-round / "9 holes" format is out of scope.
- **1 Human + 1 AI:** Player count is fixed at one human and one AI opponent for this spike.
- **Licensing:** All assets and code must be open and freely available for commercial use per CREDITS.md policy.

## Existing State

- **Toolchain:** Fully operational — Vite 6.1, TypeScript 5.7 (strict mode), Vitest 3.0, Phaser 3.90.0. Dev server on port 3000, production builds to `dist/`.
- **Project structure:** Monorepo layout with `src/` (engine modules) and `example-games/` (game spikes). Path aliases configured (`@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`).
- **Engine modules:** All four modules (`card-system`, `core-engine`, `rule-engine`, `ui`) exist as directories with barrel `index.ts` files exporting only version constants. Zero implementation.
- **Hello-world example:** Working Phaser scene proving SVG asset loading, tween animations, and text rendering. No interactivity or game logic. Establishes card dimensions (140x190px) and scene patterns.
- **Assets:** 2 SVGs (ace of spades face, card back) at 140x190px in `public/assets/cards/`. Attribution in `CREDITS.md`.
- **Tests:** Single smoke test confirming Vitest works. No meaningful game or engine tests.

## Desired Change

Build a playable 9-Card Golf example game at `example-games/golf/` that exercises and populates the engine modules:

- **card-system:** Implement Card type (rank, suit, faceUp), Deck (create, shuffle, draw), and Pile (push, pop, peek) abstractions. Add a Grid[3][3] type (may live locally in the golf game initially).
- **rule-engine:** Implement Golf-specific turn logic (draw from pile or discard, replace grid card or discard drawn card), end-of-round detection (all cards face-up), and scoring rules.
- **core-engine:** Implement minimal game state management and turn sequencing sufficient to drive a 2-player (human + AI) game loop.
- **ui:** Build Phaser scene(s) for the golf game: 3x3 grid layout, draw/discard piles, card flip/swap animations, score display, turn indicators.
- **AI player:** Implement two strategies (random valid move, greedy minimize-score) behind a selectable interface.
- **Recording:** Produce a JSON game transcript per completed game. Per-turn visual snapshots are a stretch goal (see Risks & Assumptions).
- **Card assets:** Source or generate a complete 52-card deck of face SVGs (CC0/permissive) at 140x190px. Update `public/assets/CREDITS.md` with attribution.
- **Tests:** Unit tests for scoring logic (minimum 3 scenarios), turn legality, and deck operations. All tests must pass via `npm test`; build must succeed via `npm run build`.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Scope creep from engine extraction:** Building reusable engine modules alongside a game spike may slow progress. Mitigation: build game-specific implementations first, then extract to shared modules only where the abstraction is clear and stable.
- **Card asset sourcing:** Finding or generating 52 CC0/permissive SVG card faces at consistent quality and dimensions (140x190px) may take non-trivial effort. Mitigation: consider programmatic SVG generation or an existing open-source deck (e.g., the SVG-cards GitHub repo).
- **Visual replay deferred:** Per-turn screenshot capture is a stretch goal for this spike. A dedicated dev tool for game log playback and image capture (using Playwright or similar) will be built as a separate high-priority work item, blocked by this spike. See related work item below.
- **Grid abstraction placement:** Unclear whether Grid[3][3] should live in card-system (reusable) or locally in the golf game. Mitigation: build locally first; extract after a second game validates the abstraction.

### Assumptions
- A standard 52-card deck (no jokers) is sufficient for 9-Card Golf.
- The 9-card variant uses the scoring rules from Wikipedia (A=1, 2=-2, 3-10=face, J/Q=10, K=0, column-of-three=0). No house-rule variants are in scope.
- Phaser 3.90.0's built-in scene management and tween system are sufficient for card flip/swap animations without additional libraries.
- The AI player does not need to be competitive — it only needs to make legal moves to exercise game paths.

## Suggested Next Step

Break CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB into child work items covering: card asset sourcing, card-system implementation, rule-engine (Golf scoring + turn logic), core-engine (game loop + state), UI (Phaser scenes), AI player, game recording, and test suite. Then begin implementation of the first child item per `wl next`.

## Related Work

- **Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN):** High-priority feature to build a Playwright-based dev tool that replays JSON game transcripts and captures per-turn screenshots. Blocked by this spike (requires working game with transcript output).
- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH):** Completed epic that set up the repository structure, toolchain, and empty module stubs. This spike builds directly on that foundation.
- **Wikipedia — Golf (card game):** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_(card_game) — Canonical rules reference.
- **BoardGameGeek — Golf:** https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Golf — Variant rules and community discussion.
- **AGENTS.md:** Project rules, spike-driven development approach, engine architecture, and quality gates.
- **docs/DEVELOPER.md:** Developer setup, build/test commands, and asset management.
- **public/assets/CREDITS.md:** Asset attribution policy and suggested sources (OpenGameArt.org, Kenney.nl, SVG-cards repo).

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (keywords: golf, card, game, spike, scoring, grid, deck, phaser) and repository files. No duplicate work items found.

### Worklog items

- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the repository structure, Vite/TypeScript/Phaser toolchain, hello-world example, and empty engine module stubs. This spike is a direct dependency — it provides the foundation (build tooling, directory layout, card asset pipeline patterns) that the Golf spike will build on. The hello-world scene patterns (SVG loading at 140x190px, Phaser.Scene subclass, game config) serve as templates for the Golf scene implementation.

- **Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN)** [blocked by this item]: High-priority feature to build a Playwright-based CLI tool that replays JSON game transcripts and captures per-turn screenshots. Directly blocked by this spike — it requires a working game producing JSON transcripts. The transcript format defined by this Golf spike will become the initial schema for the replay tool.

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [blocked by this item]: Open solitaire spike with deterministic, all-face-up gameplay. Blocked by this spike because it will reuse Card, Deck, and Pile abstractions built here. Its tableau/foundation model will exercise different engine patterns (build-up-by-suit vs. Golf's grid/scoring), providing a second validation point for engine module APIs.

- **Sushi Go! (CG-0MLSDWSCG154TUEL)**, **Splendor (CG-0MLSDX4B91DG6S1A)**, **Lost Cities (CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL)**, **The Mind (CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9)**, **Coloretto (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)** [all blocked]: Five additional game spikes at idea stage. All will consume the card-system and core-engine modules first built by this Golf spike. Not directly related but will benefit from abstractions validated here.

- **Add pre-commit hook to enforce doc updates (CG-0MLSHQMDY1H0I2B7)** [open]: Infrastructure task to add doc-update enforcement. Not directly related to this spike but the Golf spike should comply with the doc-update policy when making infrastructure changes.

- **Rename project to Tableau Card Engine (CG-0MLSIULHH0Y6I3DV)** [completed]: Branding rename already applied. The Golf spike should use "Tableau Card Engine" / "TCE" naming consistently.

### Repository files

- **`example-games/hello-world/`**: Establishes the patterns this spike should follow — `main.ts` entry point, `scenes/` directory with Phaser.Scene subclass, SVG asset loading via `this.load.svg()` with explicit dimensions, game config with scale mode and parent container.

- **`src/card-system/index.ts`**: Empty stub (exports only `CARD_SYSTEM_VERSION`). This spike must populate it with Card, Deck, and Pile abstractions.

- **`src/core-engine/index.ts`**: Empty stub (exports only `ENGINE_VERSION`). This spike must add minimal game state management and turn sequencing.

- **`src/rule-engine/index.ts`**: Empty stub (exports only `RULE_ENGINE_VERSION`). This spike must add Golf-specific turn logic and scoring.

- **`src/ui/index.ts`**: Empty stub (exports only `UI_VERSION`). This spike must add Phaser scene components for the Golf game.

- **`public/assets/cards/`**: Contains 2 placeholder SVGs (ace_of_spades.svg, card_back.svg) at 140x190px establishing the card asset format. This spike must source or generate the remaining 51 card faces.

- **`public/assets/CREDITS.md`**: Documents asset attribution policy and suggests sources (OpenGameArt.org, Kenney.nl, SVG-cards GitHub repo). Must be updated when new card assets are added.

- **`tests/smoke.test.ts`**: Trivial Vitest smoke test. This spike must add meaningful tests for scoring logic, turn legality, and deck operations alongside this existing test.

# Intake Brief: Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Epic** | **Assignee: Map**

> Second engine spike: build a playable Beleaguered Castle solitaire game to validate single-player support, drag-and-drop interaction, undo/redo, and auto-move mechanics in the Tableau Card Engine.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine currently supports only multi-player games (the core-engine requires 2+ players) and uses click-only input. A single-player solitaire game is needed to validate and extend the engine for: single-player GameState, drag-and-drop card interaction, undo/redo state management, and auto-move heuristics. Beleaguered Castle's fully deterministic, open-information rules (all cards face-up) make it an ideal spike for these features without the complexity of hidden state.

## Users

- **Engine developer (primary):** Validates that the engine's modular architecture can support single-player games, drag-and-drop input, undo/redo, and auto-move. Uses the spike to extend core-engine for 1-player support and extract reusable patterns.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to build a single-player solitaire game using the engine modules so I can identify gaps in single-player support, input handling, and state history management."*

- **Solitaire player:** Plays Beleaguered Castle with modern digital solitaire UX: drag cards or click-to-move, undo/redo mistakes, and watch cards auto-move to foundations when safe.
  - *"As a player, I want to play Beleaguered Castle with both drag-and-drop and click-to-move input, full undo/redo, and auto-move to foundations so the game feels polished and responsive."*

- **Game designer (future):** Uses the completed spike as a reference for building other solitaire-style games using the engine's new single-player, drag-and-drop, and undo/redo capabilities.
  - *"As a game designer, I want a working solitaire reference game that demonstrates drag-and-drop, undo/redo, and auto-move so I can quickly scaffold similar card games."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Playable classic Beleaguered Castle:** A player can play a complete game of Beleaguered Castle (classic deal: aces pre-placed on foundations, 48 cards dealt into 8 columns of 6) in a Phaser scene from deal to win or loss.
2. **Dual input methods:** Cards can be moved via both drag-and-drop (drag from tableau pile to foundation or another tableau pile) and click-to-select/click-to-place. Invalid moves snap the card back / are rejected.
3. **Full undo/redo:** A reusable undo/redo module in `src/core-engine/` supports unlimited undo/redo steps. The player can step backward and forward through their entire move history.
4. **Auto-move to foundations + auto-complete:** Cards are automatically moved to foundations when safe to play (no tableau pile needs the card as a build target). When the remaining game is trivially winnable, auto-complete plays all remaining moves to completion.
5. **Win and no-moves detection:** The game detects when the player wins (all cards on foundations) and when no legal moves remain (game over / stuck).
6. **New game / restart:** The player can start a new game (fresh shuffle) or restart the current deal at any time via a UI button.
7. **Single-player core-engine support:** `src/core-engine/` GameState is modified to allow 1 player, enabling all future solitaire games to use the shared engine.
8. **JSON game transcript:** Each completed game produces a JSON transcript compatible with the existing Visual Replay Dev Tool.
9. **Test coverage:** Unit tests cover: deal logic, move legality (valid and invalid moves), foundation build-up rules, win detection, no-moves detection, undo/redo operations, auto-move heuristics, and scoring (if applicable). All tests pass via `npm test`; build succeeds via `npm run build`.

## Constraints

- **Classic deal only:** This work item covers the classic Beleaguered Castle deal (aces pre-placed on foundations, 48 cards into 8 columns of 6). The Citadel variant (all 52 cards in tableau) is tracked separately as CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV.
- **Single-player only:** No AI opponent or solver. The player makes all decisions.
- **Card assets already available:** A full 52-card SVG deck at 140x190px exists in `public/assets/cards/` (CC0 licensed). No new art assets are needed.
- **Rule engine still a stub:** The rule engine (`src/rule-engine/`) remains an empty stub. Beleaguered Castle rules should be built locally in the game first; extraction to the rule engine is out of scope unless a clear reusable pattern emerges.
- **Licensing:** All code and assets must be open and freely available for commercial use per project policy.
- **Layout:** Foundations across the top, 8 tableau columns below (digital solitaire convention, not the traditional center-foundations layout).

## Existing State

- **Card system (src/card-system/):** Mature. Card, Deck, Pile types with full test coverage. Pile supports LIFO push/pop/peek operations suitable for foundations and tableau columns.
- **Core engine (src/core-engine/):** Functional. GameState<T> and TurnSequencer, but requires 2+ players. Must be modified for single-player support.
- **Rule engine (src/rule-engine/):** Empty stub (version constant only).
- **UI (src/ui/):** HelpPanel and HelpButton components available. No drag-and-drop, card sprite, or game-play UI components exist.
- **Golf example game (example-games/golf/):** Completed first spike. Establishes patterns for: scene structure, game logic separation (rules/scoring as pure functions), AI strategies, game transcripts, browser tests with Phaser, and help panel integration.
- **Card assets:** 52 SVG card faces + card back at 140x190px in `public/assets/cards/`. CC0 licensed from saulspatz/SVGCards.
- **No solitaire-specific code exists:** No foundation logic, tableau column logic, drag-and-drop, auto-move, or undo/redo anywhere in the codebase.

## Desired Change

Build a playable Beleaguered Castle example game at `example-games/beleaguered-castle/` that introduces single-player, drag-and-drop, undo/redo, and auto-move capabilities:

- **core-engine (single-player):** Modify `createGameState()` to accept 1 player. Ensure TurnSequencer works correctly for single-player (turn "advancement" is a no-op or simply increments the move counter).
- **core-engine (undo/redo):** Build a reusable `UndoRedoManager` module in `src/core-engine/` that maintains a history stack of game states and supports unlimited undo/redo.
- **Game logic (example-games/beleaguered-castle/):**
  - Deal module: shuffle deck, remove aces to foundations, deal 48 cards into 8 columns of 6 (all face-up).
  - Move rules: move top card of any tableau column to a foundation (if next in suit sequence) or to another tableau column (if one rank lower, regardless of suit). Empty columns accept any card.
  - Win detection: all 52 cards on foundations.
  - No-moves detection: no legal moves remain across all tableau columns.
  - Auto-move: automatically move cards to foundations when safe (no tableau column needs the card). Auto-complete when trivially solvable.
- **Phaser UI (example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/):**
  - Layout: 4 foundation piles across the top, 8 tableau columns below.
  - Dual input: drag-and-drop cards between piles, or click-to-select then click-to-place.
  - Visual feedback: highlight valid drop targets, snap-back for invalid moves, card flip animations for foundation placement.
  - Undo/redo buttons and keyboard shortcuts.
  - Win/loss overlays.
  - Help panel with game rules (using reusable HelpPanel component).
- **Game transcript:** Produce a JSON transcript per completed game, compatible with the Visual Replay Dev Tool.
- **Tests:** Unit tests for deal logic, move legality, foundation rules, win/no-moves detection, undo/redo, and auto-move. Browser tests for Phaser rendering and interaction. All tests pass via `npm test`; build succeeds via `npm run build`.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Drag-and-drop complexity:** Implementing reliable drag-and-drop with Phaser (setDraggable, drag zones, drop zones, snap-back) is significantly more complex than click input. May require substantial iteration on hit detection and visual feedback.
- **Undo/redo state size:** Storing full game state snapshots for unlimited undo/redo could consume significant memory for long games. Mitigation: use a command pattern (store moves, not states) or delta-based approach to minimize memory usage.
- **Auto-move correctness:** Determining whether a card is "safe" to auto-move to a foundation requires checking whether any tableau column still needs the card as a build target. The heuristic must be conservative to avoid auto-moving cards that the player might want to keep available for tableau building. Mitigation: start with a simple safe-move heuristic and iterate.
- **Auto-complete detection:** Determining when the game is "trivially winnable" is non-trivial (requires checking that all remaining tableau cards can be played to foundations in some order). Mitigation: use a simple heuristic (e.g., all tableau cards are in ascending order within their columns) rather than a full solver.
- **Core-engine single-player change scope:** Modifying GameState to allow 1 player may have ripple effects on TurnSequencer and any code that assumes 2+ players. Mitigation: make the change backward-compatible and verify all existing Golf tests still pass.
- **Low win rate:** Beleaguered Castle has a relatively low win rate (~30% of random deals are solvable). Players may encounter many unwinnable deals. Mitigation: the no-moves detection will inform the player when they are stuck, and new-game/restart options allow quick recovery.
- **Undo/redo interaction with auto-move:** Undoing a move that triggered one or more auto-moves must correctly undo the entire chain (auto-moves + player move). Failure to do so would leave the game in an inconsistent state. Mitigation: treat auto-move chains as part of the triggering move in the undo history.

### Assumptions
- A standard 52-card deck (no jokers) is used.
- Beleaguered Castle uses the classic rules from Wikipedia: aces pre-placed on foundations, build foundations up by suit (A to K), build tableau columns down regardless of suit, only top card of each column is available, empty columns accept any card.
- Phaser 3.90.0's built-in drag-and-drop support (setDraggable, drag events, drop zones) is sufficient without additional libraries.
- The undo/redo module does not need to support branching history (tree-based undo); a simple linear stack is sufficient.
- The game does not need a solver or hint system for this spike.
- The JSON transcript format can follow the same general structure as the Golf transcript, adapted for solitaire moves.

## Suggested Next Step

Break CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB into child work items covering: core-engine single-player support, undo/redo module, Beleaguered Castle game logic (deal, rules, win/loss detection), auto-move heuristics, Phaser UI (layout, drag-and-drop, click-to-move, visual feedback), game transcript recording, help panel integration, and test suite. Then begin implementation per `wl next`.

## Related Work

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: First game spike. Provides reference patterns for scene structure, game logic separation, AI strategies, game transcripts, and test structure. Beleaguered Castle follows the same architectural patterns.
- **Card System Engine Module (CG-0MLSPHOWY1HSCIDX)** [completed]: Card, Deck, Pile types that Beleaguered Castle will reuse directly.
- **Core Engine Turn Sequencer (CG-0MLSPHU1C02RAGE0)** [completed]: GameState and TurnSequencer that must be modified for single-player support.
- **Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN)** [completed]: JSON transcript replay tool. Beleaguered Castle should produce compatible transcripts.
- **Help Screen with Game Rules (CG-0MLT0PM000TQRIXT)** [completed]: Reusable HelpPanel and HelpButton components to integrate into Beleaguered Castle.
- **Citadel variant option (CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV)** [open]: Follow-on work item for adding the Citadel variant deal to Beleaguered Castle.
- **Wikipedia -- Beleaguered Castle:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beleaguered_Castle -- Canonical rules reference.
- **AGENTS.md:** Project rules, spike-driven development approach, engine architecture, and quality gates.
- **docs/DEVELOPER.md:** Developer setup, build/test commands, adding example games, and asset management.

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (keywords: solitaire, foundation, tableau, drag-and-drop, undo, auto-move, single-player, card, game, engine, phaser) and repository files. No duplicate work items found.

### Worklog items

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: The primary reference implementation. Its game logic architecture (pure rule functions separated from Phaser scene, game transcript recording, browser tests with headless Chromium) establishes the patterns Beleaguered Castle should follow. Key differences: Golf is multi-player with AI; Beleaguered Castle is single-player with undo/redo and drag-and-drop.

- **Card System Engine Module (CG-0MLSPHOWY1HSCIDX)** [completed]: Provides Card, Deck, and Pile types. The Pile class (LIFO push/pop/peek) is directly suitable for both foundation piles (build up by suit) and tableau columns (build down regardless of suit). No modifications to card-system are expected.

- **Core Engine Turn Sequencer (CG-0MLSPHU1C02RAGE0)** [completed]: Provides GameState<T> and TurnSequencer. Currently enforces a minimum of 2 players in `createGameState()` -- this constraint must be relaxed to support single-player solitaire. The TurnSequencer's `advanceTurn()` rotation logic will need adaptation for single-player (move counter only).

- **Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN)** [open]: JSON transcript replay tool. Beleaguered Castle should produce transcripts in a compatible format. The solitaire transcript schema will differ from Golf's (single-player moves, auto-moves, undo/redo events) but should share the same envelope structure.

- **Help Screen with Game Rules (CG-0MLT0PM000TQRIXT)** [completed]: Reusable HelpPanel and HelpButton components in `src/ui/`. Beleaguered Castle should integrate these with game-specific help content describing the deal, move rules, undo/redo shortcuts, and auto-move behavior.

- **Card Asset Pipeline (CG-0MLSPHIDD19PBDOZ)** [completed]: The full 52-card SVG deck is already available at `public/assets/cards/` (CC0 licensed, 140x190px). No new assets needed for Beleaguered Castle.

- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the repository structure, toolchain (Vite, TypeScript, Phaser, Vitest), and path aliases. Beleaguered Castle builds on this foundation.

- **Citadel variant option (CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV)** [open]: Created during this intake. Follow-on work to add a Citadel deal variant (all 52 cards in tableau, no aces pre-placed) as a selectable option within the Beleaguered Castle game.

- **Coloretto (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)** [blocked]: Set-building tableau game. While not directly related, it is another planned game spike that will benefit from the drag-and-drop and single-player engine features built by this spike.

### Repository files

- **`example-games/golf/`**: Full reference implementation. Key files to study: `GolfGame.ts` (game orchestration pattern), `GolfRules.ts` (pure rule functions), `GolfScoring.ts` (scoring logic), `GameTranscript.ts` (transcript recording), `scenes/GolfScene.ts` (Phaser scene with state-machine-driven UI flow).

- **`src/card-system/Pile.ts`**: LIFO stack abstraction documented as suitable for "draw piles, discard piles, foundations, and any other ordered collection of cards." Beleaguered Castle will use Pile instances for both the 4 foundations and 8 tableau columns.

- **`src/core-engine/GameState.ts`**: The `createGameState()` function at line 48 enforces `players.length >= 2`. This validation must be changed to `>= 1` for single-player support, with existing tests verified to still pass.

- **`src/core-engine/TurnSequencer.ts`**: The `advanceTurn()` function uses modular arithmetic (`(currentPlayerIndex + 1) % players.length`) which would work correctly for a single player (always index 0). The main concern is whether consumers assume multi-player behavior.

- **`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`** and **`src/ui/HelpButton.ts`**: Reusable UI components for in-game help. Already integrated in the Golf game via `help-content.json`. Beleaguered Castle should follow the same pattern with its own help content file.

- **`public/assets/cards/`**: 52 SVG card faces + card back, all at 140x190px. File naming convention: `{rank}_of_{suit}.svg`. All assets are CC0 licensed per `CREDITS.md`.

- **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`**: Section "Adding a New Example Game" describes the steps for creating a new game under `example-games/`. Beleaguered Castle should follow this guide.

Goal: Implement Sushi Go! (tableau drafting) spike -- drafting mechanics + public scoring.

## User Stories

As a player, I want to play a simplified Sushi Go!-style card drafting game against AI opponents so I can experience drafting mechanics in the Tableau Card Engine.

As an engine developer, I want to build a drafting game to validate and exercise Hand, Tableau, and ScoreCalculator abstractions that differ from the existing Golf (grid) and Beleaguered Castle (solitaire) patterns.

## Game Rules (Simplified Sushi Go!)

- 2 players (1 human + 1 AI), 3 rounds
- Card types: Tempura (2-set=5pts), Sashimi (3-set=10pts), Dumpling (1=1,2=3,3=6,4=10,5+=15pts), Nigiri (1/2/3pts), Wasabi (next nigiri x3), Maki Rolls (1/2/3 icons, most=6pts, 2nd=3pts), Pudding (most=+6pts, fewest=-6pts end of game)
- Each round: deal cards to each player (10 cards for 2 players), pick one simultaneously, pass hand left, repeat until all cards picked
- Score at end of each round (except Pudding scored at game end)
- Highest total score after 3 rounds wins

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Game logic is implemented as pure TypeScript (no Phaser dependencies) with separate files for card types, scoring, drafting, and game orchestration
2. All 7 card types are implemented with correct scoring rules
3. Drafting mechanic (pick-and-pass) works correctly for 2 players over 3 rounds
4. AI opponent makes legal moves (random strategy minimum, greedy stretch)
5. Phaser scene renders the game: player hand, tableau, opponent tableau, scoring
6. Game is registered in the game selector (main.ts)
7. Unit tests cover all scoring rules (each card type), drafting mechanics, and round flow
8. npm test passes and npm run build succeeds
9. Help panel with rules is included
10. Sound effects and settings panel are integrated

## Architecture

- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoCards.ts -- card type definitions and deck creation
- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.ts -- scoring logic per card type
- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoGame.ts -- game orchestration (rounds, drafting, turn flow)
- example-games/sushi-go/AiStrategy.ts -- AI player strategies
- example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts -- Phaser scene
- example-games/sushi-go/main.ts -- standalone entry point
- example-games/sushi-go/help-content.json -- help text

## Resources

- Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sushi_Go!
- Existing example games (Golf, Beleaguered Castle) as patterns

# Splendor (Engine-Building) Spike

## Goal
Implement a playable single-player Splendor spike (human vs 1 AI) that exercises the Tableau Card Engine, focusing on card market, gem token pool, noble tiles, and purchase mechanics.

## User Stories

**As a player,** I want to collect gem tokens, reserve development cards, and purchase development cards using my tokens and card bonuses so that I can accumulate prestige points and win the game.

**As a player,** I want nobles to automatically visit me when I meet their requirements so that I earn bonus prestige points.

**As an engine developer,** I want a working Splendor reference implementation that validates custom card types, token-based resource management, and market/tableau mechanics so I can identify engine gaps and reusable patterns.

## Game Rules (from official Splendor rules)

### Components
- **40 gem tokens:** 7 each of emerald, sapphire, ruby, diamond, onyx + 5 gold (wild)
- **90 development cards:** across 3 tiers (I, II, III), each with gem cost, gem bonus, and optional prestige points
- **10 noble tiles:** each with gem bonus requirements and 3 prestige points

### Setup (2 players)
- 4 tokens of each gem color (not 7) + 5 gold tokens
- n+1 = 3 noble tiles dealt face up
- 4 cards from each tier dealt face up in a market row

### Turn Actions (one per turn)
1. **Take 3 different gem tokens** from the supply
2. **Take 2 same-color gem tokens** (only if >= 4 of that color remain before taking)
3. **Reserve 1 development card** (from market or top of a tier deck) and take 1 gold token
4. **Purchase 1 development card** (from market or reserved cards) by paying gem cost minus card bonuses; spent gems return to supply

### After-Turn Checks
- If player has >= 10 gems, must return excess to the supply
- Noble visit: if a players card bonuses meet a nobles requirements, the noble visits (player takes the tile)

### End of Game
- When any player reaches 15+ prestige points, finish the current round (each player takes equal turns)
- Player with most prestige wins; ties broken by fewest purchased cards

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Game logic is pure TypeScript with no Phaser dependency (fully testable)
2. All 90 development cards defined with tier, gem cost, gem bonus, and prestige points (matching official distribution)
3. All 10 noble tiles defined with gem bonus requirements and prestige points
4. Gem token supply correctly initialized for 2 players (4 of each color + 5 gold)
5. All 4 turn actions implemented and validated (take 3 different, take 2 same, reserve, purchase)
6. Card bonus discounts correctly reduce purchase costs
7. Noble visits triggered automatically when requirements met
8. 10-gem hand limit enforced with discard mechanic
9. End-game detection at 15+ prestige with round completion
10. Tiebreaker scoring (fewest purchased cards) implemented
11. AI opponent with at least greedy strategy making legal moves
12. Phaser scene with card market display (3 tiers x 4 visible cards), gem token supply, player tableau, and turn action UI
13. Game registered in Game Selector landing page
14. Help panel with game rules
15. Sound effects for key actions (token take, card purchase, noble visit)
16. Unit tests for: card/token definitions, all 4 turn actions, scoring, noble visits, end-game detection, AI strategy
17. npm test passes and npm run build succeeds
18. Standalone main.ts entry point + createSplendorGame factory

## Technical Approach
- Follow Sushi Go pattern: custom types (not card-system rank/suit), pure game logic, separate scene
- Directory: example-games/splendor/ with scenes/, tests in tests/splendor/
- Use GameEventEmitter, PhaserEventBridge, SoundManager from core-engine
- Use HelpPanel, SettingsPanel, overlay system, scene header from ui module
- Cards rendered as colored rectangles with text (no sprite assets needed)

## Resources
- Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splendor_(board_game)
- Rulebook: https://www.spacecowboys.fr/images/jeux/splendor/rules_splendor_en.pdf

# Intake Brief: Lost Cities (2-Player Lanes) — CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature (Epic)** | **Assignee: Map**

> Build a playable Lost Cities card game (human vs. AI, full 3-round match) to validate the engine's support for 2-player hidden-information games with per-color expedition lanes, ascending-play rules, and multi-round cumulative scoring.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine has been validated with grid-based (Golf), solitaire (Beleaguered Castle), drafting (Sushi Go!), and resource-based (Splendor) game patterns but has not yet tackled a 2-player hidden-information game with per-color lanes and ascending-play constraints. Lost Cities introduces expedition lanes, investment/wager multipliers, multi-round cumulative scoring, and discard-pile strategy — mechanics not yet exercised by any existing spike. Implementing Lost Cities will validate the engine's ability to support lane-based card placement, hidden hands, and multi-round match structure.

## Users

- **Engine developer (primary):** Validates that the engine modules (card-system, core-engine, ui) support lane-based card placement, hidden-information games, custom (non-standard) card types, and multi-round match state.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to build a lane-based 2-player card game so I can identify gaps in the engine's support for ascending-play constraints, per-color discard piles, and multi-round scoring."*

- **Player (secondary):** Plays Lost Cities against an AI opponent in the browser with smooth animations and clear visual feedback.
  - *"As a player, I want to play a full 3-round match of Lost Cities against an AI opponent, seeing my hand, expedition lanes, discard piles, and cumulative scores, so I can enjoy the game digitally."*

- **QA / AI tester:** Uses AI-vs-AI matches to exercise all game paths and produce reproducible transcripts for regression testing.
  - *"As a tester, I want AI opponents that can play complete matches automatically so I can validate scoring, turn flow, and edge cases without manual play."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Full 3-round match:** A human player can play a complete 3-round Lost Cities match against 1 AI opponent in a Phaser scene — including dealing, playing/discarding, drawing, scoring per round, and cumulative match scoring.
2. **Correct scoring:** Scoring logic implements the standard Lost Cities rules: -20 base per started expedition, sum of card values, investment multiplier (x2/x3/x4), and 8+ card expedition bonus (+20). At least 4 scoring unit tests covering: empty expedition (0 points), basic expedition, investment-multiplied expedition, and 8-card bonus.
3. **AI player with two strategies:** Random (valid moves) and greedy (avoids giving opponent useful discards, prefers high-value expeditions) strategies are implemented. A child work item is created for a more advanced heuristic strategy.
4. **Custom card assets:** A script generates 60 SVG card images (5 colors x 12 cards: 3 investments + ranks 2-10) plus a card back, at the project's standard dimensions. SVGs load correctly in Phaser.
5. **Game transcript:** Each completed match produces a JSON transcript capturing all rounds, turns, actions, and board states — sufficient for the Visual Replay Dev Tool.
6. **Playable from game selector:** Lost Cities is selectable from the main game selector, launches without errors, and a complete 3-round match can be played start-to-finish via `npm run dev`.

## Constraints

- **Custom card type required:** Lost Cities uses 5 expedition colors (yellow, blue, white, green, red) with ranks 2-10 plus 3 investment/wager cards per color (60 cards total). This does not map to the standard 52-card deck. A custom `LostCitiesCard` type must be defined.
- **Hidden information:** The human player's hand is displayed face-up; the AI's hand is hidden. AI knows its own hand but not the opponent's.
- **Spike-driven development:** Game-specific modules (cards, rules, scoring, AI) live locally in `example-games/lost-cities/` initially. Reusable abstractions are extracted to engine modules only after a second game validates them.
- **Human vs. AI only (this spike):** Player count is fixed at one human and one AI opponent. The architecture should support local 2-player addition in a follow-up but this spike does not implement it.
- **Licensing:** All generated assets and code must be open and freely available for commercial use per CREDITS.md policy.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` must pass and `npm run build` must succeed.

## Existing State

- **Engine modules fully populated:** card-system (Card, Deck, Pile), core-engine (GameState, TurnSequencer, GameEventEmitter, PhaserEventBridge, SoundManager, UndoRedoManager, TranscriptStore), and ui (CardTextureHelpers, SceneHeader, Overlay, HelpPanel, SettingsPanel) are all implemented and battle-tested across 4 example games.
- **4 existing example games:** Golf (2-player grid), Beleaguered Castle (solitaire), Sushi Go! (drafting), Splendor (resource engine). All provide patterns for game logic modules, scenes, AI strategies, and transcript recording.
- **Custom card precedent:** Sushi Go! and Splendor both define custom card types and render them procedurally, providing a direct pattern for Lost Cities' non-standard deck.
- **Game selector:** Root `main.ts` manages game routing. Adding Lost Cities requires importing the scene and adding a `GameEntry` to the `GAMES` array.
- **Card asset pipeline:** 52 standard SVGs exist at 140x190px. Lost Cities requires 60 custom SVGs (5 colors x 12 cards + back) generated by a script.
- **Test infrastructure:** Vitest with unit + browser test projects, path aliases, deterministic RNG helpers. ~200+ existing tests across engine and games.

## Desired Change

Build a playable Lost Cities example game at `example-games/lost-cities/` following established patterns:

- **Card type:** Define `LostCitiesCard` (color/expedition, rank or investment, faceUp) and a `createLostCitiesDeck()` factory (60 cards: 5 colors x 3 investments + ranks 2-10).
- **Rules module:** Implement turn logic (play to expedition lane or discard, then draw from stock or any discard pile), ascending-play validation (investments first, then ascending rank order), and round-end detection (draw pile exhausted).
- **Scoring module:** Implement standard scoring (-20 base, sum of values, investment multiplier, 8-card bonus) with per-expedition and per-round aggregation.
- **Match state:** Track 3-round match with cumulative scoring. Each round resets expeditions and deals a fresh deck.
- **AI player:** Random strategy (legal moves) and greedy strategy (avoid discarding cards useful to opponent, prefer extending committed expeditions).
- **Scene:** Phaser scene showing human player's hand, both players' expedition lanes (5 colors each), 5 discard piles (one per color), draw pile, score display, and turn/round indicators. Card play animations for lane placement, discard, and draw.
- **Card asset generator:** Script to generate 60+1 SVG card images with colored backgrounds and rank/investment text.
- **Transcript recording:** JSON transcripts per completed match, following established patterns.
- **Tests:** Unit tests for scoring (4+ scenarios), turn legality, deck creation, and integration test (AI-vs-AI complete match).
- **Routing:** Add Lost Cities to the game selector in root `main.ts`.
- **Documentation:** Update docs/DEVELOPER.md and README.md with the new game entry.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep:** Multi-round match state, custom assets, and AI strategy add complexity beyond previous single-round spikes. **Mitigation:** Record additional feature ideas (heuristic AI, local 2P, tournament mode) as separate work items rather than expanding this spike.
- **Custom SVG generation quality:** Programmatically generated card SVGs may not look polished enough for a good player experience. **Mitigation:** Start with functional but simple designs (colored rectangles with rank text); visual refinement can be a follow-up work item.
- **Hidden-information AI fairness:** Ensuring the greedy AI does not "cheat" by accessing the opponent's hand or the draw pile order requires careful encapsulation. **Mitigation:** Pass AI only a view of visible game state (own hand, expedition lanes, discard tops, draw pile size).
- **Multi-round state management:** The engine's current GameState/TurnSequencer is round-based. Managing a 3-round match with inter-round state (cumulative scores, round transitions) may require match-level wrapper logic. **Mitigation:** Build match wrapper locally in the game module; extract to engine only if a second game needs it.
- **Turn two-phase complexity:** Each Lost Cities turn has two mandatory phases (play/discard, then draw) unlike simpler single-action turns in Golf. Input handling and UI state must track which phase the player is in. **Mitigation:** Model turn phases explicitly in game state; existing Splendor's multi-step turns provide a pattern.
- **Regression risk to existing games:** Adding a new game and potentially modifying shared engine modules could break existing example games. **Mitigation:** Run the full test suite (`npm test`) and build (`npm run build`) before every commit; do not modify shared modules without verifying all games still work.

### Assumptions

- The 5 expedition colors are: yellow, blue, white, green, red (matching the standard Lost Cities board game).
- Standard scoring rules from Wikipedia are authoritative: -20 base per started expedition, card values summed, investment cards multiply the total (1=x2, 2=x3, 3=x4), 8+ cards = +20 bonus.
- Each player holds 8 cards in hand at all times (draw after play/discard maintains hand size).
- Round ends when the draw pile is exhausted. Each other player does NOT get a final turn (unlike Golf).
- The greedy AI strategy does not need to be competitive — it needs to demonstrate informed decision-making (discard awareness) for testing purposes.
- Phaser 3.90.0's tween system is sufficient for lane-placement animations.

## Suggested Next Step

Break CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL into child work items covering: SVG card asset generator, Lost Cities card type and deck, rules module (turn logic + ascending play), scoring module, match state management, AI player (random + greedy), Phaser scene, transcript recording, integration tests, and documentation updates. Then begin implementation per `wl next`.

## Related Work

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: First 2-player spike. Established card-system, core-engine, and game architecture patterns that Lost Cities will reuse.
- **Splendor (CG-0MLSDX4B91DG6S1A)** [completed]: Custom card type reference. Demonstrates how to define non-standard card data and render procedurally.
- **Sushi Go! (CG-0MLSDWSCG154TUEL)** [completed]: Custom card type and procedural rendering. Similar pattern for Lost Cities' custom deck.
- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [completed]: Lane-based layout (tableau columns). Relevant for expedition lane rendering patterns.
- **Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN)** [open]: Will consume Lost Cities transcripts. Transcript format should be compatible.
- **Game-Agnostic Replay Adapter Pattern (CG-0MLTFUL061DWDGA2)** [open]: Relevant for transcript recording design.
- **Wikipedia — Lost Cities:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Cities — Canonical rules reference.
- **BoardGameGeek — Lost Cities:** https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/2349/lost-cities — Community rules and variants.
- **AGENTS.md:** Project rules, spike-driven development approach, engine architecture, and quality gates.
- **docs/DEVELOPER.md:** Developer setup, build/test commands, and asset management.

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (keywords: lost cities, expedition, lanes, ascending, discard, 2-player, investment, wager, multi-round, hidden information, custom card, scoring, phaser, transcript) and repository files. Items already listed in the manual "Related Work" section above are not repeated unless new relevance context is added.

### Worklog items

- **The Mind — open-hand variant (CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9)** [blocked]: Another game spike featuring ascending-play rules on a shared pile. Lost Cities' per-color ascending-play constraint is a related mechanic; implementation patterns for enforcing ascending order in one game may inform the other.

- **Coloretto — set-building tableau (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)** [blocked]: Set-collection game with per-player color scoring and row-based card placement. The per-color lane structure and color-based scoring parallel Lost Cities' expedition lanes. Patterns for color-grouped placement UI may be reusable.

- **Game Selector Index Page (CG-0MLTRTAWY0X0CSY4)** [completed]: Lost Cities must be added to the game selector in `main.ts`. The `GameEntry` interface and `GAMES` array in `main.ts:24` define the registration pattern.

- **Game-Agnostic Replay Adapter Pattern (CG-0MLTFUL061DWDGA2)** [open]: Lost Cities will need a replay adapter for transcript playback. If this pattern is implemented before Lost Cities, the adapter interface should be followed; if not, Lost Cities' transcript format should remain compatible for later adaptation.

- **Core Engine Event System (CG-0MLTFSAOM1W4UKI8)** [completed]: Provides `GameEventEmitter` and `PhaserEventBridge` that Lost Cities should use for game event dispatch and UI synchronization, following the pattern established by Golf and refined by later games.

- **Transcript Browser Storage Auto-Save (CG-0MLTFQZ6G09TVLDL)** [completed]: Provides `TranscriptStore` for browser-based transcript persistence. Lost Cities' multi-round match transcripts should use this store, though the larger transcript size (3 rounds vs. single round) should be considered.

- **Migrate canvas from 800x600 to 1280x720 (CG-0MLVOT2VY0DG9VLF)** [completed]: Canvas is now 1280x720. Lost Cities' scene layout (10 expedition lanes, 5 discard piles, hand, draw pile, scores) should be designed for this resolution.

- **Deploy card games to GitHub Pages (CG-0MLTRXRKK1Q50Z0M)** [completed]: CI/CD pipeline deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main. Lost Cities will be automatically deployed once merged, no additional CI work needed.

### Repository files

- **`example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoCards.ts`**: Defines custom `SushiGoCard` type and `createSushiGoDeck()` factory for a non-standard deck. This is the closest pattern for Lost Cities' `LostCitiesCard` type and `createLostCitiesDeck()` factory (60 custom cards with color/rank/investment attributes).

- **`example-games/splendor/SplendorCards.ts`**: Defines `DevelopmentCard`, `Noble`, and `GemColor` types for another non-standard card game. Demonstrates how to model game-specific card attributes (cost, points, gem bonus) beyond standard rank/suit, relevant for Lost Cities' investment/wager cards.

- **`example-games/splendor/AiStrategy.ts`** and **`example-games/sushi-go/AiStrategy.ts`**: AI strategy implementations with random and greedy/heuristic variants. Lost Cities' AI (random + greedy discard-aware) should follow the same interface pattern.

- **`src/card-system/Pile.ts`**: Pile abstraction used for draw piles and discard piles. Lost Cities needs 5 per-color discard piles plus a shared draw pile — all using this abstraction.

- **`src/core-engine/TurnSequencer.ts`**: Turn management for 2-player games. Lost Cities' two-phase turn (play/discard, then draw) is more complex than Golf's single-action turn but can build on the same sequencer with phase tracking.

- **`src/core-engine/TranscriptStore.ts`**: Browser-based transcript persistence. Lost Cities' 3-round match transcripts will use this for auto-save, following the pattern established by Golf and Beleaguered Castle.

- **`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`**: Reusable scene header component with title, help button, settings button, and menu button. Lost Cities' scene should use `createSceneHeader()` for consistent UI.

- **`main.ts`**: Game selector registration. Lost Cities must import its scene and add a `GameEntry` to the `GAMES` array (line 24) and register the scene in the Phaser config (line 60).

# Intake Brief: The Mind (CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature (Epic)** | **Assignee: Map**

> Implement a real-time cooperative card game where a human and an AI partner must play numbered cards (1-100) onto a shared ascending pile by timing their plays — without communication — across 8 levels of increasing difficulty with a shared lives system.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine has no cooperative game and no real-time gameplay mechanic. The Mind introduces both: players must independently decide WHEN to play cards based on intuition about card values relative to the 1-100 range. This spike validates the engine's ability to support cooperative win/loss conditions, real-time AI timing heuristics, custom (non-standard-deck) card types, and level progression — all novel capabilities not exercised by the existing 5 example games.

## Users

- **Engine developer:** Validates the engine's ability to handle cooperative games, real-time AI decisions, custom card types (numbers 1-100 instead of standard playing cards), and multi-level progression — patterns not tested by any existing spike.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to build a cooperative real-time game to discover what engine abstractions are missing for non-competitive, non-turn-based gameplay."*

- **Player (casual):** Experiences a cooperative card game where the challenge is reading the AI partner's timing and coordinating plays without explicit communication.
  - *"As a player, I want to play The Mind cooperatively with an AI partner, feeling the tension of deciding when to play my cards and hoping my partner plays theirs at the right moment."*

- **QA / AI tester:** Uses AI-vs-AI games (both sides automated) to exercise all game paths and produce timestamped transcripts for regression testing of timing logic.
  - *"As a tester, I want to run automated games to verify that the AI timing model produces legal play sequences and that the lives/level system works correctly."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Playable 8-level game:** A human player can play a complete game of The Mind with 1 AI partner across 8 levels (Level 1 = 1 card each, Level 8 = 8 cards each) in a Phaser scene, with real-time gameplay where both players independently decide when to play.
2. **AI timing model:** An AI partner uses a linear proportional timing heuristic (delay proportional to card value relative to 1-100 range, with random jitter) to decide when to play cards. The AI architecture is extensible to support more sophisticated timing models later.
3. **Lives system:** The team starts with 2 lives (per the original 2-player rules). When a card is played while any player holds a lower unplayed card, a life is lost and all lower cards held by either player are discarded. The game ends when lives reach zero (loss) or all 8 levels are cleared (win). Bonus lives may be earned at specific levels (to be confirmed during planning -- the original game awards a bonus life at levels 3 and 6 for 2 players).
4. **Custom card type:** Cards are numbered 1-100 using a custom `MindCard` type (not the standard rank/suit Card type), leveraging the generic `Pile<T>` from card-system.
5. **Timestamped game transcript:** Each completed game produces a JSON transcript recording timestamps, card values, player identity, pile state, lives remaining, and level progression — consistent with the engine's `TranscriptRecorderBase<T>` pattern.

## Constraints

- **2 players only (1 human + 1 AI):** Consistent with other example game spikes. Multi-player support is out of scope.
- **No shuriken/throwing star mechanic:** The cooperative "pause and discard lowest" mechanic is deferred to a follow-up work item to keep scope manageable.
- **Custom card assets needed:** Cards are numbered 1-100 and do not use the standard 52-card deck SVGs. Simple rendered text or minimal SVG cards showing the number are sufficient for the spike.
- **Click-to-play interaction:** The human plays a card by clicking it from their hand. Drag-to-play is out of scope for the initial spike.
- **Independent of refactor epic:** This spike should use the engine modules as they currently are. If the refactor epic (CG-0MLX8SR0E1S709OW) completes first, imports can be adjusted, but this work is not blocked by it.
- **Reuse engine, extend locally:** Use core-engine's GameState, GameEventEmitter, TranscriptRecorderBase, and seeded RNG. Use ai module's AiPlayer and AiStrategyBase. Build game-specific logic (timing model, cooperative state, level progression) locally in `example-games/the-mind/`.
- **Licensing:** All assets and code must be open and freely available for commercial use per project policy.

## Existing State

- **Engine modules populated:** card-system (Card, Deck, Pile<T>, shuffle), core-engine (GameState, TurnSequencer, GameEventEmitter, TranscriptRecorderBase, seeded RNG, SoundManager), rule-engine (LegalityResult), ai (AiStrategyBase, AiPlayer, pickRandom, pickBest), ui (GameSelectorScene, overlays, scene headers, card texture helpers).
- **5 example games complete:** Golf (grid/scoring), Beleaguered Castle (solitaire/undo-redo), Sushi Go (drafting), Splendor (engine-building/tokens), Lost Cities (ascending-play/expeditions). All are competitive or solo — no cooperative game exists.
- **Ascending-play precedent:** Lost Cities enforces ascending card order on expedition lanes, providing a partial mechanical parallel.
- **No real-time gameplay:** All existing games are turn-based. The Mind will be the first game with real-time decision-making.
- **Custom card type support:** Pile<T> is already generic, but Deck operations are currently Card-specific. The Mind will need a simple deck factory for numbered cards.
- **Game selector:** Root `main.ts` has a game catalogue with 5 entries. The Mind must be added as entry 6.

## Desired Change

Build a playable The Mind example game at `example-games/the-mind/` that introduces cooperative and real-time gameplay to the engine:

- **Custom card type:** Define `MindCard` type (numeric value 1-100, faceUp boolean). Implement a deck factory that creates and shuffles the 100-card deck using the seeded RNG.
- **Game state:** Implement `TheMindGameState` tracking: shared pile (ascending), each player's hand (hidden from each other), current level (1-8), lives remaining, and level completion status.
- **Real-time play:** Both players (human and AI) can play a card at any moment — there are no turns. The human clicks a card; the AI uses a timing heuristic to decide when to play.
- **AI timing model:** Linear proportional delay: `delay = (cardValue / 100) * baseDuration + randomJitter`. The base duration and jitter are configurable. Architecture allows swapping in more sophisticated models later.
- **Lives and penalty:** When a card is played and any player holds a lower unplayed card, a life is lost and all such lower cards are discarded from play. Visual and audio feedback for life loss.
- **Level progression:** Level 1 starts with 1 card per player. Each cleared level deals one more card per player (Level 2 = 2 cards, etc.). Team wins after clearing Level 8.
- **UI:** Phaser scene showing: human's hand (face-up, clickable), AI's hand (face-down, card count visible), shared pile (last played card and count), lives display, level indicator, win/loss overlay.
- **Transcript recording:** Use TranscriptRecorderBase to record timestamped events: card plays, life losses, level completions, game outcome.
- **Game selector integration:** Add The Mind to the root game catalogue in `main.ts`.
- **Tests:** Unit tests for card type/deck, timing model, lives/penalty logic, level progression. Integration test running an AI-vs-AI game to completion.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Scope creep:** The Mind introduces multiple novel capabilities (cooperative play, real-time AI, custom cards, level progression). Mitigation: build all game-specific logic locally in `example-games/the-mind/`; record opportunities for additional features (shuriken mechanic, multi-player support, advanced AI models) and engine extraction (cooperative abstractions) as separate work items linked to CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9 rather than expanding this spike.
- **Real-time timing hard to test deterministically:** AI timing introduces non-deterministic delays (jitter). Mitigation: use seeded RNG for jitter in tests; separate timing logic from Phaser's update loop for unit testability.
- **Custom card rendering:** 100 numbered cards need visual representation. Mitigation: render card numbers as text on a generic card background using Phaser's text rendering -- no external SVG assets needed.
- **AI timing feels robotic:** A linear delay model may produce predictable behavior. Mitigation: start with linear + jitter; tune during playtesting; extensible architecture allows swapping in better models later.
- **TurnSequencer mismatch:** The engine's TurnSequencer assumes alternating turns, but The Mind has simultaneous play. Mitigation: use GameState for shared state but bypass TurnSequencer; implement real-time play handling locally.
- **Regression risk:** Adding a sixth game to the game selector could break existing games. Mitigation: run full test suite (`npm test`) and verify all games load after integration.
- **Browser performance:** Continuous timer-based AI decisions and pile updates may affect frame rate. Mitigation: use Phaser's built-in timer events; profile on target browsers during development.

### Assumptions
- Phaser's `time.addEvent()` or scene `update()` loop provides sufficient precision for the AI timing model (millisecond-level delays).
- The generic `Pile<T>` from card-system can be used for the shared ascending pile with `MindCard` as the type parameter.
- 8 levels for 2 players (matching the original game's 2-player level count) provides sufficient game length for a satisfying experience.
- The AI does not need to be "good" at the game — it needs to produce plausible timing behavior and legal plays for testing and demonstration purposes.
- Card backs for the AI's hidden hand can use the existing `card_back.svg` asset.

## Related Work

- **Refactor common game utilities into core engine (CG-0MLX8SR0E1S709OW)** [open, plan_complete]: Extracting shared utilities. Not a blocker, but The Mind may benefit from cleaned-up APIs if the refactor completes first. Mentions cooperative game types as a future consideration for AI interfaces.
- **Coloretto (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)** [blocked, idea]: Another planned game spike. Not directly related but both are pending future games.
- **Lost Cities (CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL)** [completed]: Uses ascending-play mechanics on expedition lanes — closest mechanical parallel to The Mind's ascending pile.
- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: First game spike that established engine architecture patterns and set the template for spike development.
- **Wikipedia — The Mind:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mind — Rules reference.
- **BoardGameGeek — The Mind:** https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/244992/the-mind — Community discussion and variant rules.
- **AGENTS.md:** Project rules, spike-driven development approach, and quality gates.
- **docs/DEVELOPER.md:** Developer setup, build/test commands, asset management.

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (39 items) and repository files for keywords: cooperative, real-time, ascending, timing, level progression, custom card, AI strategy, transcript, game selector. Conservative filtering applied -- only items and files with clear, direct relevance to The Mind's implementation are included.

### Worklog items

- **AI Strategy module -- src/ai (CG-0MLYGKHJH1PVJJ95)** [completed]: Created the shared `src/ai/` module with `AiStrategyBase`, `AiPlayer<TStrategy>`, `pickRandom<T>()`, and `pickBest<T>()`. The Mind's AI timing strategy must extend `AiStrategyBase` and wrap it in an `AiPlayer` instance, following the same pattern used by Golf, Splendor, Sushi Go, and Lost Cities.

- **Refactor common game utilities into core engine (CG-0MLX8SR0E1S709OW)** [open, plan_complete]: Active refactoring epic that generalizes the card-system for custom card types and consolidates AI strategy patterns. Directly relevant because (a) the generic `Pile<T>` and potential generic `Deck<T>` work enables `MindCard` usage, (b) the AI strategy interface may evolve to accommodate cooperative/real-time patterns introduced by The Mind, and (c) the description explicitly notes cooperative game types as a future consideration for AI interfaces.

- **Lost Cities (CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL)** [completed]: Closest mechanical parallel. Implements ascending-play enforcement on expedition lanes (`LostCitiesRules.ts`), a custom card type (`LostCitiesCard` with color and investment properties), game-specific AI strategies extending `AiStrategyBase`, and a game transcript recorder extending `TranscriptRecorderBase<T>`. The Mind should follow the same structural patterns for its custom card type, AI strategy, and transcript recording.

- **Ensure all games output game transcripts for the replay tool (CG-0MLZJ1VL20F52WP2)** [open, idea]: Requires every example game to produce transcripts compatible with the replay tool. The Mind must implement `TranscriptRecorderBase<T>` to satisfy this requirement. Coordination needed to ensure The Mind's timestamp-based transcript format (real-time events rather than turn-based snapshots) is compatible with the replay tool's expectations.

- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the project structure, Vite + TypeScript + Vitest toolchain, and example-game directory layout that The Mind must follow. The Mind's `example-games/the-mind/` directory, entry point, and scene structure should mirror the patterns established here.

- **Deploy card games to GitHub Pages (CG-0MLTRXRKK1Q50Z0M)** [completed]: Established the GitHub Actions deployment pipeline and game selector integration pattern. The Mind must be added to the game catalogue in `main.ts` and registered in the Phaser scene list to appear on the deployed site.

### Repository files

- **`src/card-system/Pile.ts`**: Generic `Pile<T>` class (line 17) that The Mind will use directly with `MindCard` as the type parameter for the shared ascending pile. Already supports push, pop, peek, isEmpty, size, and toArray operations needed for pile management.

- **`src/ai/AiStrategy.ts`**: Defines `AiStrategyBase` interface (line 28) and `AiPlayer<TStrategy>` wrapper class (line 54) that The Mind's AI timing strategy must extend. The existing interface is turn-based (strategy returns an action); The Mind will need to adapt this for real-time timing decisions.

- **`src/core-engine/TranscriptRecorder.ts`**: Abstract `TranscriptRecorderBase<T>` class (line 92) that The Mind must extend for its game transcript. The base class provides timestamped recording infrastructure; The Mind's recorder will need to capture real-time events (card plays with timestamps, life losses, level transitions) rather than turn-based snapshots.

- **`main.ts`**: The unified entry point containing the game catalogue array (line 25) and Phaser scene registration (line 67). The Mind must add a `GameEntry` to the `GAMES` array and register its scene class here.

- **`example-games/lost-cities/LostCitiesRules.ts`**: Reference implementation of ascending-play validation (lines 105-148). The Mind's pile validation logic (checking that played cards are higher than the pile top) can follow a similar pattern, though simplified since The Mind uses a single shared pile rather than per-color expedition lanes.

- **`example-games/lost-cities/AiStrategy.ts`**: Reference implementation of game-specific AI strategies extending `AiStrategyBase` with custom decision methods. The Mind's timing-based AI strategy should follow the same structural approach (extend base, define game-specific methods) while replacing action selection with timing heuristics.

- **`example-games/lost-cities/GameTranscript.ts`**: Reference implementation of a game-specific transcript recorder extending `TranscriptRecorderBase<T>` (line 233 onwards). The Mind's recorder should follow this pattern but capture real-time timestamps and cooperative events instead of turn-based actions.

- **`src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`**: The `GameEntry` type (line 28) and `GameSelectorScene` class used by the game catalogue. The Mind's scene must be compatible with this system and navigable from the selector.

## Suggested Next Step

Break CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9 into child work items covering: custom card type and deck factory, game state and cooperative mechanics (lives/penalty/level progression), AI timing model, Phaser UI scene, transcript recording, game selector integration, and test suite. Create a separate sibling work item for the shuriken/throwing star mechanic (tagged `discovered-from:CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9`). Then begin implementation of the first child item per `wl next`.
