# Intake Brief: Coloretto (Set-Building Tableau) — CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature (Epic)** | **Assignee: Map**

> Implement a playable Coloretto game (human vs. 1–4 AI) with the set-building / "take-a-row" card mechanic, multi-round cumulative scoring, and reusable engine patterns for set-collection games.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine has seven completed game spikes (Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Splendor, Lost Cities, The Mind, Feudalism, Main Street) but no game that exercises the **set-building / set-collection tableau mechanic** with the "take-a-row" action pattern. Coloretto's simple row-placement mechanic and per-player color scoring fills this gap, validating the engine for set-collection games and extracting reusable patterns for future games with similar mechanics (row-based drafting, set-collection scoring, multiple-round accumulation).

## Users

- **Player (primary):** Plays Coloretto against 1–4 AI opponents across multiple rounds, collecting color sets by taking rows from a shared tableau and scoring positively for selected colors and negatively for others.
  - *"As a player, I want to play a complete game of Coloretto against AI opponents so I can experience the take-a-row mechanic and set-collection scoring with multiple rounds."*

- **Engine developer:** Validates the engine's ability to support row-based intermediate holding zones, per-player set collection, and set-collection scoring with positive/negative selection.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to build a Coloretto spike to exercise row/tableau mechanics and multi-round cumulative scoring, extracting reusable patterns for future set-collection games."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Playable Coloretto (simplified rules):** 1 human player can play a complete multi-round game of Coloretto against 1–4 AI opponents. The simplified rules include: standard chameleon deck (7 colors, single/double chameleon cards per color), Last Round trigger card, row placement (max 3 cards per row) and take-a-row actions, multi-round play with cumulative scoring.

2. **Correct scoring:** At the end of each round, each player selects 3 colors to score positively (if they have cards in at least 3 colors; otherwise all colors are positive). Scoring uses the canonical table: 1 card = 1pt, 2 = 3, 3 = 6, 4 = 10, 5 = 15, 6+ = 21. Players with fewer than 3 colors score all colors positively. Cumulative total across rounds determines the winner.

3. **Game logic is pure TypeScript:** All game logic (card definitions, deck, rows, scoring, turn flow, round management) is implemented as pure TypeScript with no Phaser dependencies, following the pattern established by Sushi Go!, Splendor, and other completed games.

4. **AI opponent with basic heuristic:** AI players make legal moves with a basic heuristic strategy (e.g., prefers rows containing colors already in its collection, avoids giving strong rows to opponents). At minimum, a random strategy is also available.

5. **Full UX integration:** Phaser scene renders the shared rows, per-player collections, score display, turn indicators, and round/game-end overlays. The game is registered in the Game Selector landing page. Help panel with rules is included.

6. **Sound effects and settings panel:** Basic sound effects for key actions (card placement, row take, scoring) integrated via the existing GameEventEmitter / SoundManager infrastructure. SettingsPanel with mute/volume controls is included.

7. **Game transcript:** Each completed game produces a JSON transcript recording the sequence of turns, row states, and final scores.

8. **Test coverage:** Unit tests cover: deck composition (7 colors, correct card counts per color, Last Round card), row placement rules (max 3 cards per row, cannot place on a full row), take-a-row mechanics, scoring algorithm (all scoring buckets), multi-round accumulation, AI strategy (basic heuristic), and win/loss detection. All tests pass via `npm test`; build succeeds via `npm run build`.

9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Simplified deck for initial spike:** The initial implementation uses only standard chameleon cards (7 colors, single/double chameleon cards per color, plus the Last Round card). Joker cards (wild chameleons) and +2 bonus point cards are tracked as a separate follow-on work item (CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39).
- **Multi-round play:** The full multi-round format is implemented from the start (not deferred). Number of rounds follows the canonical Coloretto rules based on player count: 3 rounds for 5 players, 4 rounds for 4 players, 5 rounds for 3 players, and 7 rounds for 2 players.
- **Row count per player count:** Follows canonical rules — 3 rows for 2-3 players, 4 rows for 4 players, 5 rows for 5 players.
- **No card sprite assets needed:** Cards rendered as colored rectangles with text (chameleon count + color name), following the pattern from Sushi Go! and Splendor where custom card types don't reuse the standard 52-card SVG deck.
- **Player count:** 1 human + 1-4 AI opponents (2-5 total players), matching the original game's player range.
- **Licensing:** All code and assets must be open and freely available for commercial use per project policy.

## Existing State

- **Engine infrastructure:** Mature — GameState, TurnSequencer (multi-player), Card/Deck/Pile abstractions, GameEventEmitter, SoundManager, SettingsPanel, HelpPanel, and game selector all exist and are proven across 7+ games.
- **Existing game patterns:** Sushi Go! (drafting) and Splendor (engine-building) provide the closest architectural reference for Coloretto — custom card types, pure game logic, multi-player AI, game transcript recording.
- **No set-building / row-mechanic code exists:** No row abstraction, no "choose positive colors at scoring time" mechanic, and no per-color set scoring with positive/negative selection exists anywhere in the codebase.
- **Coloretto follow-on work item created:** CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39 tracks full rules expansion (jokers, +2 cards).

## Desired Change

Build a playable Coloretto example game at `example-games/coloretto/`:

- **Directory structure:** `example-games/coloretto/` with:
  - `ColorettoCards.ts` — card type definitions (colors, chameleon counts, Last Round trigger)
  - `ColorettoGame.ts` — game orchestration (round management, deal, row management, turn flow)
  - `ColorettoScoring.ts` — scoring logic (per-color point table, positive/negative selection, cumulative multi-round scoring)
  - `ColorettoAis.ts` — AI strategies (basic heuristic + random)
  - `scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — Phaser scene
  - `createColorettoGame.ts` — Phaser game config factory
  - `help-content.json` — rules and controls
  - `main.ts` — standalone entry and game selector registration

- **Game objects:**
  - **Deck:** Custom deck of colored chameleon cards + Last Round trigger card.
  - **Rows:** N shared rows (3-5 depending on player count), each accepting up to 3 cards face-up.
  - **Player collections:** Per-player set of collected cards (from rows they've taken).
  - **Round counter:** Tracks current round; handles Last Round trigger.

- **Turn flow:**
  1. Draw top card of deck → place face-up onto any non-full row.
  2. Instead of placing, a player may take an entire row (all cards in it) into their collection — then they sit out until the round ends.
  3. Continue until all players have taken a row or the Last Round card appears, then one final round of play.
  4. Score each round, accumulate across rounds, determine overall winner.

- **Scoring (canonical table):**
  - 1 card = 1pt, 2 = 3, 3 = 6, 4 = 10, 5 = 15, 6+ = 21
  - Each player selects 3 colors to score positively; all others score negatively
  - If player has < 3 colors in their collection, all score positively
  - Cumulative across rounds

- **Tests:**
  - Unit: deck composition, row placement rules, take-a-row, scoring (each bucket), multi-round accumulation, AI behavior
  - All pass via `npm test`; `npm run build` succeeds

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep (full rules expansion deferred):** There is a natural inclination to implement the full Coloretto deck (jokers, +2 cards) during the initial spike. **Mitigation:** record the full rules expansion as a separate child work item (CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39) to be implemented after the initial spike is complete. Additional feature opportunities discovered during implementation should also be tracked as separate work items rather than expanding the current scope.
- **Multi-round UX complexity:** Managing multi-round display (round transitions, cumulative score display, final winner) adds UI complexity beyond single-round games like Golf. **Mitigation:** follow the Sushi Go! pattern for multi-round play, which already implements round transitions and cumulative scoring.
- **AI heuristic quality:** A basic heuristic that prefers colors already in the player's collection may be too predictable or weak. **Mitigation:** start simple; the architecture supports adding more sophisticated strategies later without changing the game logic.
- **Row display with 5 players:** Displaying up to 5 rows simultaneously with per-player collections may be visually crowded in a 1280px viewport. **Mitigation:** design the layout early with flexibility for variable row counts; compact card rendering (colored rectangles with text) keeps visual density manageable.

### Assumptions

- Cards are rendered as colored rectangles with chameleon count text (no card sprite assets needed), following the Sushi Go! and Splendor pattern.
- The existing TurnSequencer supports 2-5 players correctly (already proven with Golf for 2 players; should work for N players).
- The existing GameEventEmitter, SoundManager, HelpPanel, and SettingsPanel components are reusable without significant modification.
- Multi-round management follows the Sushi Go! pattern (per-round state, round transitions, cumulative score tracking).
- Players are eliminated from action within a round once they take a row (they sit out), which is unique to Coloretto's turn flow.

## Related Work

- **Coloretto full rules expansion (CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39)** [open, child]: Follow-on work item for joker cards, +2 bonus cards, and full deck. Created during this intake as a deferred scope item.
- **Sushi Go! (CG-0MLSDWSCG154TUEL)** [completed]: Closest architectural reference — multi-round play, drafting/passing mechanics, custom card types, pure game logic, multi-player AI. Coloretto's round management and scoring patterns follow Sushi Go!'s architecture.
- **Splendor (CG-0MLSDX4B91DG6S1A)** [completed]: Reference for multi-player game architecture, AI strategies, and game transcript recording. Provides patterns for game state management with 2+ players.
- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: Foundational first spike that established the project's architectural patterns (pure game logic, AI, transcript, Phaser UI).
- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the repository structure, toolchain, and path aliases that Coloretto builds on.
- **Wikipedia — Coloretto:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloretto — Canonical rules reference.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Player count — 2 players only (1 human + 1 AI), full 2-5 players (1 human + up to 4 AI), or 2-4 players?" — Answer (user): **B — Full 2-5 players (1 human + up to 4 AI).** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Game scope — full rules (jokers, +2 cards, Last Round) or simplified (standard cards + Last Round only)?" — Answer (user): **Start with B (simplified — standard cards + Last Round only), create follow-on work item for full rules.** Source: interactive reply. The follow-on item was created as CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39 (child of this work item).
- Q: "Number of rounds — single round (one deal → scoring → done) or multiple rounds with cumulative scoring?" — Answer (user): **B — Multiple rounds with cumulative scoring (full original game).** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "AI sophistication — random only, random + basic heuristic, or random + greedy?" — Answer (user): **B — Random + basic heuristic (prefers rows with colors it already has).** Source: interactive reply.

## Key Files

- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoCards.ts` — New: card type definitions (colors, chameleon counts, Last Round trigger).
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoGame.ts` — New: game orchestration (round management, deal, row management, turn flow).
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoScoring.ts` — New: scoring logic (per-color point table, positive/negative selection, cumulative multi-round scoring).
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts` — New: AI strategies (basic heuristic + random).
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — New: Phaser scene.
- `example-games/coloretto/createColorettoGame.ts` — New: Phaser game config factory.
- `example-games/coloretto/main.ts` — New: standalone entry and game selector registration.
- `src/core-engine/TurnSequencer.ts` — Existing multi-player turn sequencer to reuse.
- `src/ui/` — Reusable UI components (OverlayManager, HelpPanel, SettingsPanel).

# Scaffold Card Game Engine Project

> **Headline**: Set up the Card Game Spikes repository with Phaser 3.x, TypeScript, Vite, and Vitest as a flat monorepo, unblocking all 7 planned game spikes.

## Problem Statement

The Card Game Spikes project is a completely greenfield repository with no source code, build tooling, or directory structure. All 7 planned example game spikes (9-Card Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Splendor, Lost Cities, The Mind, Coloretto) are blocked until a working project foundation is in place. A properly scaffolded project with build, test, and dev-server tooling is required before any game development can begin.

## Users

- **Game developers (internal)**: Agents and contributors who will implement the example card games and extract reusable engine components.
  - *As a game developer, I want to run a single command to start a dev server with hot-reload so I can iterate quickly on game code.*
  - *As a game developer, I want TypeScript configured with strict mode so I catch type errors early.*
  - *As a game developer, I want a clear directory structure so I know where to put shared engine code vs. game-specific code.*
- **Engine consumers (future)**: Developers who will reuse extracted engine modules for their own card games.
  - *As an engine consumer, I want shared modules (core-engine, card-system, rule-engine) organized in a discoverable way so I can import only what I need.*

## Success Criteria

1. Running `npm install && npm run dev` starts a Vite dev server that renders a minimal Phaser 3.x "hello world" scene in the browser (a card sprite or text on a colored background).
2. Running `npm test` executes Vitest and at least one passing unit test completes successfully.
3. Running `npm run build` produces a production bundle in a `dist/` directory without errors.
4. The directory structure includes clearly separated areas for shared engine modules (`src/core-engine/`, `src/card-system/`, `src/rule-engine/`, `src/ui/`) and example games (`example-games/`), with each example game having its own entry point and scene(s).
5. A git repository is initialized with a proper `.gitignore` (covering `node_modules/`, `dist/`, IDE files, OS files) and an initial commit containing the full scaffold.

## Constraints

- **Phaser 3.x (latest stable, currently 3.90.0)**: The AGENTS.md originally specified "Phaser 4" but this does not exist as a stable release. Phaser 3.x is the current community standard.
- **Vite**: Replaces Webpack as specified in AGENTS.md. Vite is officially supported by Phaser's project scaffolder and offers faster dev builds and HMR.
- **Vitest**: Replaces Jest as specified in AGENTS.md. Vitest integrates natively with Vite, uses the same API as Jest, and avoids ESM/CJS compatibility friction.
- **TypeScript**: Strict mode, targeting modern browsers (ES2020+).
- **Flat monorepo**: Single `package.json` at root. Shared engine code in `src/` subdirectories, example games in `example-games/` with their own scenes and entry points. No npm workspaces for now.
- **Open-source licensing**: All dependencies and assets must be permissively licensed (MIT, Apache 2.0, CC0, etc.) and suitable for commercial use.
- **AGENTS.md must be updated** to reflect the actual tech stack decisions (Phaser 3.x, Vite, Vitest, flat monorepo structure).

## Existing State

- The repository contains only `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore` (minimal, Worklog-focused), and `.worklog/` data.
- No git repository is initialized (no `.git/` directory).
- No `package.json`, no TypeScript config, no build tooling, no source files, no tests.
- 7 game spike work items exist in Worklog, all at "idea" stage, all blocked pending scaffolding.

## Desired Change

After this work item is completed, the repository will contain:

- **Git repository**: Initialized with a proper `.gitignore` and initial commit.
- **`package.json`**: With Phaser 3.x, TypeScript, Vite, and Vitest as dependencies; scripts for `dev`, `build`, `test`, and `preview`.
- **`tsconfig.json`**: Strict TypeScript configuration targeting ES2020, with Phaser type definitions.
- **`vite.config.ts`**: Configured for Phaser 3.x development with dev server and production build.
- **Directory structure**:
  ```
  cardGameSpikes/
  ├── src/
  │   ├── core-engine/       # Game loop, state management, rendering helpers
  │   ├── card-system/       # Card definitions, deck, hand, pile abstractions
  │   ├── rule-engine/       # Rule definitions, validation, turn logic
  │   └── ui/                # Reusable UI components (buttons, menus, overlays)
  ├── example-games/
  │   └── hello-world/       # Minimal Phaser scene proving toolchain works
  │       ├── scenes/
  │       └── main.ts
  ├── public/                # Static assets (HTML, images, fonts)
  ├── tests/                 # Vitest test files
  ├── dist/                  # Production build output (gitignored)
  ├── AGENTS.md              # Updated with actual tech stack
  ├── package.json
  ├── tsconfig.json
  ├── vite.config.ts
  └── .gitignore             # Comprehensive Node.js/TS/Vite ignores
  ```
- **Hello-world scene**: A minimal Phaser 3.x scene that renders on screen, proving Vite + Phaser + TypeScript integration works end-to-end.
- **One passing Vitest test**: Demonstrating the test framework is wired up correctly.
- **Updated AGENTS.md**: Reflecting Phaser 3.x, Vite, Vitest, and the actual directory structure.

## Related Work

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** - First game spike, directly unblocked by this scaffolding.
- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** - Solitaire spike, blocked.
- **Sushi Go! (CG-0MLSDWSCG154TUEL)** - Drafting game spike, blocked.
- **Splendor (CG-0MLSDX4B91DG6S1A)** - Engine-building game spike, blocked.
- **Lost Cities (CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL)** - 2-player lanes spike, blocked.
- **The Mind (CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9)** - Open-hand variant spike, blocked.
- **Coloretto (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)** - Set-building tableau spike, blocked.
- **Official Phaser Webpack-TS template** (https://github.com/phaserjs/template-webpack-ts) - Reference for Phaser + TypeScript project structure.
- **Phaser `create-phaser-game` CLI** - Official scaffolder supporting Vite + TypeScript templates.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Phaser 3.x may not work seamlessly with Vite out of the box (e.g., global `Phaser` variable, canvas/WebGL initialization). *Mitigation*: The official `create-phaser-game` CLI has a Vite template, so this path is well-trodden.
- **Risk**: The flat monorepo approach may not scale if engine modules need independent versioning later. *Mitigation*: Acceptable for a spike-driven project; migration to workspaces can be done later without major refactoring.
- **Assumption**: Phaser 3.x TypeScript definitions are up-to-date and compatible with strict mode (they are shipped in the `phaser` npm package under `types/`).
- **Assumption**: A single Vite entry point can serve multiple example games. If not, a per-game Vite config or multi-page setup may be needed (discoverable during first game spike implementation).
- **Assumption**: No CI/CD pipeline is needed in this scaffolding phase; local `npm test` and `npm run build` are sufficient validation.

## Suggested Next Step

Break this epic into child work items for implementation: (1) git init + .gitignore, (2) package.json + Vite + TypeScript config, (3) directory structure + placeholder modules, (4) hello-world Phaser scene, (5) Vitest setup + first test, (6) AGENTS.md update. Then implement starting from work item CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH.

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (keyword: scaffold, setup, phaser, card game) and repository files. No duplicate or prior scaffolding work items found.

- **AGENTS.md** (`/AGENTS.md`): The project charter defining the vision, directory structure, and tech stack for the Card Game Engine. This scaffolding work item directly implements the foundational setup described in AGENTS.md, with agreed deviations (Phaser 3.x instead of 4, Vite instead of Webpack, Vitest instead of Jest).
- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)**: The first and highest-priority game spike. It is directly unblocked by this scaffolding and will be the first consumer of the project structure, Phaser integration, and test framework established here. Its description references `Phaser Container` which validates the need for a working Phaser setup.
- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)**, **Sushi Go! (CG-0MLSDWSCG154TUEL)**, **Splendor (CG-0MLSDX4B91DG6S1A)**, **Lost Cities (CG-0MLSDXELC06VESJL)**, **The Mind (CG-0MLSDXNMM1R2IMT9)**, **Coloretto (CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38)**: All 6 remaining game spikes are blocked pending scaffolding. # Intake Brief: Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool (CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Playwright-driven dev tool that replays JSON game transcripts, captures per-turn screenshots, and supports live browser takeover for interactive bug reproduction.

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine produces JSON game transcripts capturing every turn, but there is no way to visually replay a recorded game. Developers debugging game logic or UI issues must manually play through games to reproduce bugs, and there is no automated way to generate screenshots or videos of completed games for visual verification, regression testing, or documentation.

## Users

- **Engine developer:** Needs to visually verify that game state rendering matches expected behavior across all turns, catch rendering bugs, and reproduce reported visual issues without manual play.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want to replay a recorded game transcript and see per-turn screenshots so I can verify rendering correctness and visually debug game state issues."*

- **QA / tester:** Needs to generate reproducible visual evidence of bugs and regressions by replaying specific game transcripts that trigger known issues.
  - *"As a QA tester, I want to replay a game transcript that reproduces a bug, pause at the problematic turn, and take over interactively to investigate the issue in a live browser."*

- **Game designer:** Needs to review complete game playthroughs visually without playing them, for tuning game feel, animations, and UI layout.
  - *"As a game designer, I want to watch a recorded game play back visually so I can evaluate the game's visual presentation and identify UI improvements."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Screenshot capture:** Running `npm run replay -- data/transcripts/golf/game-001.json --output data/screenshots/golf/game-001/` replays the transcript in a headless Playwright browser and produces a PNG screenshot after each turn, saved to the specified output directory.
2. **Transcript auto-save:** Games automatically save completed transcripts to browser storage (IndexedDB preferred, localStorage fallback) with a rolling window of the last 10 games. A CLI script (`npm run transcripts:export -- golf`) extracts transcripts from browser storage to `data/transcripts/golf/` on disk. An in-game export button also allows manual JSON download.
3. **Partial replay with takeover:** The replay tool supports `--stop-at <turn>` (e.g., `npm run replay -- transcript.json --stop-at 12`) which pauses replay at the specified turn and keeps the browser open in non-headless mode, allowing the developer to take manual control and play from that point.
4. **Engine event system:** The core engine module (`src/core-engine/`) emits standardized events (`turn-started`, `turn-completed`, `animation-complete`, `state-settled`, `game-ended`) that the replay tool listens for to ensure precise timing between turns.
5. **Golf game support:** The tool works with the existing 9-Card Golf transcript format (version 1) as the initial supported game, with architecture designed to support additional games without major refactoring.
6. **Documentation:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` is updated with usage instructions for the replay tool, transcript auto-save/export, and the engine event system.

## Constraints

- **Canvas-based rendering:** Phaser renders to a WebGL/Canvas element, not DOM. Playwright cannot use CSS selectors for game elements. The tool must use coordinate-based clicking or the game must expose hit area information for reliable interaction.
- **Browser storage for persistence:** Transcripts are saved to localStorage/IndexedDB since the game runs in a browser and the Vite dev server does not natively support disk writes. A separate CLI step is needed to extract transcripts to disk files.
- **Playwright dependency:** Playwright is already a devDependency (^1.58.2) used for Vitest browser tests. The replay tool must not conflict with the existing test configuration.
- **Existing transcript schema:** The tool must consume the existing `GameTranscript` format (version 1) defined in `example-games/golf/GameTranscript.ts`. Changes to the schema should be backward-compatible.
- **Video capture is a stretch goal:** Per-turn PNG screenshots are the primary output. Stitching screenshots into a video or recording continuous video is deferred to a follow-up enhancement.
- **Licensing:** All new dependencies must be permissively licensed (MIT, Apache 2.0, CC0, or similar).

## Existing State

- **Transcript system:** A well-tested `TranscriptRecorder` class exists in `example-games/golf/GameTranscript.ts` that captures complete board state per turn (player grids, discard pile, stock count, scores). The transcript is currently held in-memory only and used for the end-of-game results screen.
- **Transcript format:** Version 1 schema is defined as TypeScript interfaces (`GameTranscript`, `TurnRecord`, `BoardSnapshot`, `CardSnapshot`, `GameResults`). Comprehensive unit and integration tests validate transcript correctness and JSON round-trip serialization.
- **Playwright integration:** Already installed as a devDependency and configured as the Vitest browser test provider (headless Chromium). Browser tests exist for Golf UI interactions (`tests/golf/GolfInteraction.browser.test.ts`).
- **No replay tool:** No replay, playback, or screenshot capture functionality exists. No dev tools infrastructure exists. No `tools/` directory.
- **No transcript persistence:** Transcripts are not saved to disk or browser storage. They exist only in-memory during a game session.
- **No engine event system:** The core engine does not emit events for turn lifecycle or animation timing. The Golf scene manages its own animation callbacks internally.

## Desired Change

Build a developer replay tool with these capabilities:

### Transcript Persistence (child task)
- Implement auto-save of completed game transcripts to browser storage (localStorage or IndexedDB) after each game.
- Maintain a rolling window of the last 10 transcripts per game.
- Add an in-game export button that downloads the current transcript as a JSON file.
- Create a CLI extraction script (`npm run transcripts:export`) that uses Playwright to connect to the game, read transcripts from browser storage, and write them as JSON files to `data/transcripts/<game>/`.
- Add `data/` to `.gitignore`.

### Core Engine Event System (child task)
- Add a standardized event emitter to the core engine module (`src/core-engine/`) that games can use to signal turn lifecycle events.
- Define events: `turn-started`, `turn-completed`, `animation-complete`, `state-settled`, `game-ended`.
- Integrate the event system into the Golf scene so it emits these events at appropriate points.
- Design for reuse across all example games.

### Replay Tool (primary deliverable)
- Create an npm script entry point (`npm run replay`) that accepts a transcript JSON file path and replays it.
- Use Playwright to launch the game in a headless browser, then drive it through recorded turns using coordinate-based UI automation.
- Use core engine events to synchronize between turns (wait for `state-settled` before capturing screenshots and advancing).
- Capture a PNG screenshot of the Phaser canvas after each turn, saved to a configurable output directory (default: `data/screenshots/<game>/<timestamp>/`).
- Support `--stop-at <turn>` to pause at a specific turn, switch to non-headless mode, and hand the browser off to the developer for interactive takeover.
- Produce a summary report (JSON) listing turns replayed, screenshot paths, and any errors encountered.
- Design the tool architecture to be game-agnostic where possible, with game-specific adapters for translating transcript moves into UI interactions.

### Documentation
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with usage instructions for the replay tool, transcript export, and the engine event system.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Canvas interaction reliability:** Coordinate-based clicking on Phaser canvas elements may be fragile if game layout changes or window size varies. Mitigation: use the engine event system and game-exposed hit area data to improve targeting; pin viewport dimensions during replay.
- **Animation timing:** Replaying turns faster than animations complete could cause visual artifacts or incorrect screenshots. Mitigation: the engine event system (`state-settled` event) ensures the tool waits for animations to finish before capturing.
- **Browser storage limits:** localStorage has a ~5-10MB limit; 10 transcripts of complex games could approach this. Mitigation: use IndexedDB (larger quota) or compress transcripts before storage.
- **Scope creep:** This work item touches multiple systems (persistence, events, UI automation, CLI tooling). Mitigation: break into child tasks, implement incrementally, and record additional feature ideas (video capture, multi-game support) as separate work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Cross-game generalization:** Designing the event system and replay architecture for reuse before a second game validates it may lead to premature abstraction. Mitigation: implement for Golf first, keep interfaces minimal, refactor when Beleaguered Castle or another game adds replay support.
- **Dev server dependency:** The replay tool assumes a running Vite dev server at `localhost:3000`. If the server is not running, replay will fail silently or with an unclear error. Mitigation: the replay script should check for a running server before launching Playwright and provide a clear error message with instructions to start the dev server.
- **Transcript schema drift:** If the transcript format evolves (e.g., for Beleaguered Castle), older transcripts may become incompatible. Mitigation: the transcript schema includes a `version` field; the replay tool should validate the version and fail gracefully with a clear message if the format is unsupported.

### Assumptions
- Playwright's canvas screenshot API produces sufficiently high-quality captures of the Phaser rendering for visual verification.
- The existing Golf scene's UI layout is stable enough for coordinate-based interaction (card positions, pile locations are deterministic for a given viewport size).
- The `state-settled` event pattern is sufficient for synchronizing between turns without needing frame-level precision.
- IndexedDB or localStorage provides adequate storage for 10 rolling transcripts without performance issues.
- The Vite dev server will be running when the replay tool is invoked (the tool connects to `localhost:3000`).

## Related Work

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: The first game spike. Produces the game transcripts this tool will consume. Transcript format defined in `example-games/golf/GameTranscript.ts`.
- **Game Transcript Recording (CG-0MLSPIQ1516DJNQL)** [completed]: Implemented the `TranscriptRecorder` class and transcript schema used by this tool.
- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [in-progress]: Second game spike. Will be a consumer of the replay tool and engine event system once completed.
- **Scaffold Card Game Engine (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the repository structure and tooling this tool builds on.
- **Golf browser tests** (`tests/golf/GolfInteraction.browser.test.ts`): Existing Playwright-based UI tests for the Golf scene. Demonstrates patterns for Phaser canvas interaction via Playwright that the replay tool can build on.

## Suggested Next Step

Break CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN into child work items covering: transcript persistence (auto-save + export), core engine event system, replay tool implementation, and documentation. Then begin implementation per `wl next`.


## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (39 items) and repository files for keywords: replay, transcript, screenshot, Playwright, event, persistence, browser, automation, canvas, dev tool, recording, game log. The following items have clear, direct relevance to the Game Log Visual Replay Dev Tool.

### Worklog items

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: The first game spike and a formal dependency (via `wl dep`). Produces the JSON game transcripts this tool will consume. The transcript format (version 1) and TranscriptRecorder class were built as part of this epic. The replay tool requires a working game to replay against.

- **Game Transcript Recording (CG-0MLSPIQ1516DJNQL)** [completed]: Implemented the `TranscriptRecorder` class, `GameTranscript` schema (version 1), and JSON round-trip serialization in `example-games/golf/GameTranscript.ts`. This is the direct data source the replay tool will consume. Its description explicitly references CG-0MLSN2YWY1EL17FN as a downstream consumer.

- **Phaser UI Browser Testing with Vitest (CG-0MLSUJIE30K54IUO)** [completed]: Established the Playwright + Vitest browser mode infrastructure (headless Chromium, `*.browser.test.ts` convention, viewport pinning) that the replay tool can reuse for launching and automating the Phaser game. Demonstrates patterns for accessing the game instance via `window.__PHASER_GAME__` and interacting with canvas-rendered content.

- **Investigate and fix broken Golf UI interactions (CG-0MLSW8TKZ0YHXJR2)** [completed]: Fixed click handling, turn flow, and AI execution in the Golf scene. The interaction patterns validated here (click stock pile, click grid cards, AI turn execution) are the same actions the replay tool must automate via Playwright coordinate-based clicks.

- **Core Engine Turn Sequencer (CG-0MLSPHU1C02RAGE0)** [completed]: Provides the game state management and turn sequencing foundation in `src/core-engine/`. The replay tool's engine event system (Success Criterion #4: `turn-started`, `turn-completed`, `state-settled`, etc.) will extend this module with event emission capabilities.

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [open]: The second game spike. Will be a future consumer of the replay tool and engine event system. The replay tool architecture should be game-agnostic enough to support this game once it is complete, validating the adapter pattern.

- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established repository structure, Vite/TypeScript toolchain, and module layout. The replay tool builds on this infrastructure (npm scripts, path aliases, build pipeline).

### Repository files

- **`example-games/golf/GameTranscript.ts`**: Defines the `GameTranscript`, `TurnRecord`, `BoardSnapshot`, and `CardSnapshot` TypeScript interfaces that the replay tool will parse. Also contains the `TranscriptRecorder` class. This is the primary data contract the replay tool depends on.

- **`tests/golf/GameTranscript.test.ts`**: Unit tests for transcript recording and schema validation. Demonstrates how to create, populate, and finalize transcripts programmatically — useful reference for the replay tool's transcript parsing logic.

- **`tests/golf/Integration.test.ts`**: Integration tests that run complete AI-vs-AI games and validate transcript output. Shows end-to-end transcript generation patterns and provides example transcripts the replay tool can use for testing.

- **`tests/golf/GolfInteraction.browser.test.ts`**: Playwright-based browser tests for Golf UI interactions (click handling, turn flow). Demonstrates coordinate-based Phaser canvas interaction patterns that the replay tool must replicate for driving turns via UI automation.

- **`tests/golf/GolfScene.browser.test.ts`**: Browser tests verifying Phaser game boot, rendering, and canvas presence. Shows how to launch the game in headless Chromium and access game state via `window.__PHASER_GAME__` — directly applicable to the replay tool's browser automation.

- **`example-games/golf/main.ts`**: Entry point that exposes the Phaser game instance via `window.__PHASER_GAME__` (line 13). The replay tool will use this global reference to synchronize with game state and listen for engine events.

- **`vite.config.ts`**: Configures Playwright as the Vitest browser test provider with headless Chromium and pinned viewport (900x700). The replay tool must be compatible with this configuration and may reuse the same Playwright setup for launching the game.

- **`src/core-engine/index.ts`**: Barrel file for the core engine module. Currently exports GameState, TurnSequencer, and phase management — but does not export any event emitter. The replay tool's engine event system (Success Criterion #4) will need to add event emission here.

## Summary

Source, resize, and integrate a complete 52-card SVG deck from saulspatz/SVGCards (public domain) at 140x190px into the project asset pipeline.

## User Story

As an engine developer, I want a complete set of 52 card face SVGs at the project's standard dimensions (140x190px) so that any example game can render a full deck visually without placeholder graphics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 52 individual card face SVGs exist in public/assets/cards/ at 140x190px
- Existing card back SVG is retained or replaced with one from the same set
- public/assets/CREDITS.md updated with saulspatz/SVGCards attribution (public domain)
- SVGs load correctly via this.load.svg() in a Phaser scene (verified in hello-world or golf scene)
- SVG files contain valid SVG markup (no broken XML)
- File naming convention is consistent (e.g., 2_of_clubs.svg, king_of_hearts.svg)

## Minimal Implementation

- Download saulspatz/SVGCards Vertical2 deck (https://github.com/saulspatz/SVGCards)
- Extract individual SVGs using the provided exportSVG.py script or manually from the Decks/Vertical2/svgs folder
- Resize from 210x315px to 140x190px (same 2:3 aspect ratio) via script or batch tool
- Adopt consistent naming convention matching existing assets

## Summary

Add Vitest browser mode testing with Playwright to enable automated testing of the Phaser-rendered Golf UI in a real browser environment. This addresses the broken UI that currently has no automated test coverage.

## User Story

As an engine developer, I want automated browser tests that verify the Phaser game renders correctly and responds to user interactions, so that UI regressions are caught before they reach players.

## Problem

The Golf Phaser UI (GolfScene.ts) has 674 lines of rendering and interaction code with zero automated test coverage. The UI is reported broken but there is no way to detect or prevent regressions. Phaser requires a real browser (WebGL/Canvas) and cannot run in JSDOM or happy-dom.

## Approach

- Use Vitest 3.x browser mode with `@vitest/browser` package and Playwright provider
- Configure test projects in vite.config.ts to run Node-based unit tests (`*.test.ts`) and browser-based tests (`*.browser.test.ts`) together via `npm test`
- Browser tests run in headless Chromium via Playwright
- Tests verify: canvas renders, game objects exist, basic interaction works
- Access Phaser game instance via `window.__PHASER_GAME__` for state assertions

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `@vitest/browser` and `playwright` are installed as dev dependencies
2. `vite.config.ts` uses `test.projects` to define both unit and browser test configurations
3. Browser tests use `*.browser.test.ts` naming convention
4. At least one browser test verifies the Phaser canvas renders in the game container
5. At least one browser test verifies initial game state is visible (card sprites, UI text)
6. All existing 204 unit tests continue to pass alongside new browser tests
7. `npm test` runs both unit and browser tests in a single command
8. `npm run build` continues to succeed
9. Tests run headless (no visible browser window) for CI compatibility
10. docs/DEVELOPER.md updated with browser testing section

- All 8 Golf epic features (complete)
- Vitest 3.2.4 (installed)

# Intake Brief: Help Screen with Game Rules and Instructions (CG-0MLT0PM000TQRIXT)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Add a reusable left-side help panel to the engine's UI module (`src/ui/`) that accepts an array of `{ heading, body }` content sections from each game, and integrate it into the 9-Card Golf example with rules overview, turn flow, scoring, and how-to-play instructions.

## Problem Statement

Players of Tableau Card Engine games currently have no way to learn the rules or how to play within the game itself. Rules exist only as code comments and developer documentation. A reusable, engine-level help panel is needed so that each game can surface its own rules and instructions to players without building custom UI from scratch.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** Wants to quickly reference the rules and how-to-play instructions without leaving the game.
  - *"As a player, I want to press a help button or keyboard shortcut to see the game's rules and instructions in a side panel so I can learn how to play or refresh my memory mid-game."*

- **Game developer (secondary):** Wants a ready-made, configurable help panel component they can populate with game-specific content.
  - *"As a game developer, I want to pass an array of content sections (heading + body) to a reusable help panel component so that I don't have to build help screen UI from scratch for each new game."*

## Success Criteria

1. **Reusable engine component:** A `HelpPanel` (or equivalent) class exists in `src/ui/` that accepts an array of `{ heading: string, body: string }` sections and renders them in a left-side slide-in panel.
2. **Trigger mechanisms:** The help panel can be opened via an on-screen help button (e.g. "?" icon) and a keyboard shortcut (e.g. H or ?), and dismissed via a close button, the same keyboard shortcut, or clicking outside the panel.
3. **Scrollable content:** If the rules content exceeds the panel height, the panel supports vertical scrolling with a visible scroll indicator.
4. **Percentage-based width:** The panel width is responsive, taking a percentage of the game canvas (e.g. 30-40%) rather than a fixed pixel width.
5. **Golf integration:** The 9-Card Golf example game integrates the help panel with sections covering rules overview, turn flow, scoring, and basic how-to-play instructions. The help panel is accessible during gameplay without pausing the game.

## Constraints

- **No game pausing:** The game continues running while the help panel is open. Game input behind the panel may be blocked (to prevent accidental clicks) but AI turns and animations are not frozen.
- **Engine-level component:** The `HelpPanel` must live in `src/ui/` and be importable via the `@ui/*` path alias. Game-specific content must not be hard-coded in the engine component.
- **Golf only (initial scope):** Only the 9-Card Golf game needs to integrate the help panel in this work item. Other games will adopt it later.
- **Content is not interactive:** The help panel displays static text sections. Interactive tutorials, animated demos, or step-by-step walkthroughs are out of scope.
- **Phaser 3.90.0 compatibility:** The component must work with the current Phaser version and use Phaser's built-in text rendering and input systems (no DOM overlays or external UI libraries).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass after implementation.

## Existing State

- **`src/ui/` module:** Empty stub exporting only `UI_VERSION = '0.1.0'`. No reusable UI components exist.
- **End-screen overlay in GolfScene (lines 618-674):** The only overlay-like pattern in the codebase -- a semi-transparent rectangle with text and an interactive button. Hard-coded in the scene, not extracted. This serves as a reference for how overlays can be built in Phaser.
- **Instruction text in GolfScene:** A single-line contextual instruction text at the bottom of the screen that changes per turn phase. Not a help screen.
- **Rules in code only:** `GolfRules.ts` and `GolfScoring.ts` contain complete rules as JSDoc comments and imperative code, but no player-facing text or data structure exists for rules content.
- **No keyboard shortcut handling:** The Golf game uses only mouse/pointer input. No keyboard shortcuts are implemented.

## Desired Change

- **New engine component (`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` or similar):**
  - Accepts a configuration object with an array of `{ heading: string, body: string }` content sections.
  - Renders a left-side panel that slides in/out with an animation.
  - Panel width is percentage-based (e.g. 30-40% of canvas width).
  - Includes a close button (e.g. "X" in the top-right corner of the panel).
  - Supports vertical scrolling with a scroll indicator when content overflows.
  - Provides a semi-transparent backdrop behind the panel (optional, to dim the game).

- **Help button (`src/ui/HelpButton.ts` or similar):**
  - A small on-screen button (e.g. "?" icon) that can be placed in a game scene to toggle the help panel.
  - Reusable across games.

- **Keyboard shortcut support:**
  - The help panel listens for a configurable keyboard shortcut (default: H or ?) to toggle open/close.
  - Clicking outside the panel also dismisses it.

- **Golf game integration (`example-games/golf/`):**
  - Define rules content as an array of sections (e.g. Overview, Turn Flow, Scoring, Tips).
  - Add the help button to the GolfScene.
  - Wire up the keyboard shortcut.

- **Tests:**
  - Unit tests for the HelpPanel component (content rendering, open/close state).
  - Integration verification that the Golf game's help content loads correctly.

- **Barrel exports:** Update `src/ui/index.ts` to export `HelpPanel`, `HelpButton`, and related types.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Phaser text scrolling limitations:** Phaser 3 does not have a native scrollable text container. Implementing smooth scrolling with a scroll indicator may require a masked container with drag/wheel input, adding complexity. Mitigation: research Phaser community patterns for scrollable panels before implementation; consider a crop-mask approach with pointer-drag and mouse-wheel listeners.
- **Input blocking complexity:** Blocking game input behind the panel while keeping the game running (AI turns, animations) may require careful Phaser input priority management. Mitigation: use Phaser's input hit area and depth sorting; test with active AI turns.
- **First `src/ui/` component sets precedent:** This is the first real component in the engine's UI module. Design decisions (API patterns, naming conventions, configuration approach) will influence all future UI components. Mitigation: keep the API surface minimal and well-documented; review before merging.
- **Content authoring effort underestimated:** Writing clear, concise player-facing rules text for Golf is a distinct task from building the UI component. Poor rules text undermines the feature even if the component works perfectly. Mitigation: draft rules content early and review for clarity before final integration.

### Assumptions
- Phaser 3.90.0's mask and input systems are sufficient for implementing a scrollable side panel without external libraries.
- A single keyboard shortcut (H key) is sufficient; no conflict with existing game input is expected since Golf currently uses only pointer input.
- Game-specific content will be plain text only (no rich formatting, images, or HTML). Markdown or styled text can be considered in future iterations.
- The panel does not need to persist state (e.g. scroll position) across open/close cycles.

## Related Work

- **9-Card Golf (CG-0MLSDW7YM1IWH2SB)** [completed]: The parent spike. The Golf game is the first integration target for this help screen feature.
- **Golf Phaser UI (CG-0MLSPJ9EW1WGHKLX)** [completed]: Established the Phaser scene patterns (overlays, text rendering, input handling) used in GolfScene. The help panel should follow similar patterns.
- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [open]: Future game spike that will benefit from the reusable help panel.
- **Future game spikes** (Sushi Go!, Splendor, Lost Cities, The Mind, Coloretto): All will consume the help panel component once built.
- **`src/ui/index.ts`**: Stub module that will be populated by this work item.
- **`example-games/golf/scenes/GolfScene.ts`**: Scene that will integrate the help panel.
- **`example-games/golf/GolfRules.ts`**, **`GolfScoring.ts`**: Source material for the Golf game's help content sections.

## Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog (keywords: help, panel, UI, overlay, scroll, button, keyboard, rules, instructions, Golf) and repository files. Conservative filtering applied -- only items with clear relevance to the help panel feature are included.

### Worklog items

- **Golf Phaser UI (CG-0MLSPJ9EW1WGHKLX)** [completed]: The most directly relevant prior work. GolfScene.ts (lines 618-674) contains the only overlay pattern in the codebase -- a semi-transparent rectangle with text and an interactive button for the end-of-round screen. This serves as the primary reference implementation for how to build overlay/panel UI in Phaser within this project, including depth management, text rendering, and interactive button patterns.

- **Golf Game Rules and Scoring (CG-0MLSPI9YQ083H8LO)** [completed]: Implemented the game rules (GolfRules.ts) and scoring logic (GolfScoring.ts) that contain the authoritative rule definitions as JSDoc comments and code. These files are the source material from which player-facing help content sections (rules overview, turn flow, scoring) must be derived. No player-facing text data structure exists yet -- this work item must create one.

- **Investigate and fix broken Golf UI interactions (CG-0MLSW8TKZ0YHXJR2)** [completed]: Fixed interaction handling in GolfScene (click handling, turn flow, AI execution, state transitions). Understanding these fixes is relevant because the help panel must coexist with the game's input handling -- blocking game clicks behind the panel while keeping AI turns and animations running requires awareness of the current input architecture.

- **Phaser UI Browser Testing with Vitest (CG-0MLSUJIE30K54IUO)** [completed]: Established browser-mode testing infrastructure using Vitest + Playwright. The help panel's unit and integration tests should follow the same patterns (*.browser.test.ts convention, window.__PHASER_GAME__ access for state assertions) to verify rendering and interaction in a real browser.

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [open, idea stage]: The next planned game spike. Will be the second consumer of the reusable HelpPanel component, validating that the API is truly game-agnostic. The help panel's content section interface ({ heading, body }) should be validated against this game's anticipated content needs.

- **Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)** [completed]: Established the src/ui/ module stub and the @ui/* path alias. The HelpPanel and HelpButton components must be exported from src/ui/index.ts and importable via @ui/* per the project conventions set by this work item.

### Repository files

- **`src/ui/index.ts`**: Currently an empty stub exporting only `UI_VERSION = '0.1.0'`. This is where HelpPanel, HelpButton, and related types must be exported. As the first real component added to this module, the API design here sets a precedent for all future UI components.

- **`example-games/golf/scenes/GolfScene.ts`** (676 lines): The integration target scene. The end-screen overlay (lines 618-674) demonstrates the overlay pattern (semi-transparent background rectangle, centered text, interactive button with hover states, depth management). The help panel implementation should follow this pattern but extract it into a reusable, configurable component rather than hard-coding it in the scene.

- **`example-games/golf/GolfRules.ts`**: Contains complete turn flow rules as JSDoc (draw from stock/discard, swap or discard+flip, round ending detection, initial reveal). The help content's "Turn Flow" and "How to Play" sections should be derived from these documented rules.

- **`example-games/golf/GolfScoring.ts`**: Contains scoring rules as JSDoc (A=1, 2=-2, 3-10=face, J/Q=10, K=0, column-of-three=0). The help content's "Scoring" section should be derived from this documented logic.

- **`example-games/golf/GolfGrid.ts`**: Defines the 3x3 grid model (GRID_ROWS=3, GRID_COLS=3) used by the game. Relevant context for writing the help content's rules overview section explaining the grid layout.

## Summary

Build the `HelpPanel` class in `src/ui/` that renders a left-side panel with heading/body content sections, open/close state, and percentage-based width. This is the first real component in the engine's UI module and sets the API precedent for all future UI components.

## User Story

As a game developer, I want a reusable `HelpPanel` component that accepts an array of content sections and renders them in a configurable side panel, so I don't have to build help screen UI from scratch for each new game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HelpPanel` class exists in `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` and is exported from `src/ui/index.ts`
- Constructing a HelpPanel with a sections array renders one heading and one body text block per section
- Constructor accepts a Phaser Scene and a config object: `{ sections: Array<{ heading: string, body: string }>, widthPercent?: number }`
- Panel renders as a solid background rectangle at 35% of canvas width (configurable via `widthPercent`), full height, anchored to the left edge
- Each section renders a heading (larger font) followed by body text, stacked vertically with spacing
- Panel has `open()` and `close()` methods, and an `isOpen` readonly property
- Panel starts hidden (closed state)
- Constructing a HelpPanel with an empty sections array renders the panel background with no text content (no error thrown)
- Calling `destroy()` on the HelpPanel removes all game objects from the scene (no orphaned objects)
- Unit tests verify content rendering, open/close state transitions, empty sections, and destroy cleanup
- `npm test` passes; `npm run build` succeeds

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` with a Phaser Container holding a background rectangle and text objects
- Use Phaser `Text` game objects for headings (larger fontSize) and body (smaller fontSize)

## Summary

Add polished slide-in/slide-out animation with easing to the HelpPanel open/close transitions. The panel slides from off-screen left to its final position on open, and back off-screen on close, using Phaser tweens with cubic easing curves.

## User Story

As a player, I want the help panel to slide in and out smoothly so the UI feels polished and responsive rather than jarring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Calling `open()` slides the panel from off-screen left to its final position using a Phaser tween with ease-out curve
- Calling `close()` slides the panel back off-screen left with ease-in curve
- Animation duration is configurable (default ~300ms)
- Calling `open()` while already open or `close()` while already closed is a no-op
- Calling `open()` while a close animation is in progress interrupts the close and animates to the open position without a visible position jump
- Pointer events on panel content (close button, scroll) do not fire during animation transitions
- Unit/browser test verifies animation completes and panel reaches final position

## Minimal Implementation

- Use `scene.tweens.add()` with `Phaser.Math.Easing.Cubic.Out` for open, `Cubic.In` for close
- Start panel at `x = -panelWidth`, animate to `x = 0` on open
- Track animation state to handle interruption (stop existing tween, start new one from current position)
- Disable panel interactivity during animation via a state flag

## Prototype / Experiment

Verify tween interruption (calling open during close) produces smooth reversal without visual glitches. Success = no position jump or orphaned tweens.

## Dependencies

- HelpPanel Core Component (CG-0MLTANMZ80E1GY0X)

## Deliverables

- Updated `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` with animation logic
- Animation unit/browser tests

## Summary

When content sections exceed the panel's visible height, enable vertical scrolling via mouse wheel and pointer drag, with a minimal scroll track bar indicator. Content is clipped to panel boundaries using a Phaser mask.

## User Story

As a player, I want to scroll through long help content within the panel using my mouse wheel or by dragging, so I can read all the rules even if they don't fit on one screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- If total content height exceeds panel height, scrolling is enabled automatically
- Mouse wheel scrolls content up/down within the panel bounds
- Pointer drag (click-and-drag) on the panel area scrolls content up/down
- Content is clipped to the panel boundaries using a Phaser mask (no text visible outside the panel)
- A thin vertical track bar on the right side of the panel shows relative scroll position
- Track bar updates position as the user scrolls
- If content fits within the panel, no track bar is shown and scrolling is disabled
- Scroll position resets to top each time the panel is opened
- Scrolling beyond the top boundary does not move content past the initial position (no over-scroll at top)
- Scrolling beyond the bottom boundary does not move content past the last section (no over-scroll at bottom)
- Unit/browser tests verify scroll behavior, clamping, and track bar visibility

## Minimal Implementation

- Wrap content text objects in a Phaser Container, apply a `GeometryMask` clipped to panel bounds
- Listen for `wheel` events on the scene/panel and adjust container Y offset within bounds
- Add pointer-drag input on the panel for touch/mouse drag scrolling
- Draw track bar as a thin Phaser Graphics rectangle; update its Y position proportional to scroll offset
- Calculate max scroll range from `totalContentHeight - visibleHeight`
- On `open()`, reset content container Y to 0 (top)

## Prototype / Experiment

Verify Phaser 3.90.0 `GeometryMask` works correctly for clipping a scrollable container. Success = content clips cleanly at panel top/bottom boundaries with no visual artifacts.

## Summary

When the help panel slides open, the content area is blank. Text only appears after the user scrolls. This is because the GeometryMask is drawn at the container's x position at the time of opening (which is off-screen at -panelWidth), and is never updated during the slide-in animation.

## Root Cause

In resetScroll() (called by open()), the mask is drawn at maskX = this.container.x, which is -panelWidth (off-screen). The slide-in tween animates container.x from -panelWidth to 0, but the mask rectangle is not redrawn during the animation. The mask only gets redrawn when the user scrolls (applyScroll()), which is why content appears after scrolling.

## Fix

Add an onUpdate callback to both the open and close tweens that redraws the mask at the container's current x position during each animation frame.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the help panel opens, text content is visible immediately (as the panel slides in)
2. Content remains visible throughout the entire slide-in animation
3. Content remains visible during slide-out animation
4. Scrolling still works correctly after the fix
5. npm test passes; npm run build succeeds

## Related

- Parent: Help Screen with Game Rules and Instructions (CG-0MLT0PM000TQRIXT)
- File: src/ui/HelpPanel.ts

## Summary

When the AI takes its turn, the player cannot tell what move was made. The AI should visually show which pile it draws from (stock or discard), pause to let the player see the drawn card, and then execute the swap/discard move.

## User Story

As a player, I want to see which pile the AI draws from and what card it drew before the AI makes its move, so I can follow the AI's strategy and understand what happened.

## Current Behavior

1. 'AI is thinking...' text shown for 600ms
2. AI turn executes instantly (draw + move in one call)
3. Only the card flip at the grid position is animated
4. No indication of draw source or drawn card

## Desired Behavior

1. 'AI is thinking...' text shown briefly
2. AI draws from stock or discard -- the drawn card is shown visually (like the human's showDrawnCard()) with instruction text indicating which pile was chosen
3. ~1 second pause so the player can see the drawn card
4. AI executes the swap or discard-and-flip move with the existing flip animation
5. Piles and scores refresh after the move completes

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the AI draws from stock, the instruction text says something like 'AI drew from stock'
2. When the AI draws from discard, the instruction text says 'AI drew from discard'
3. The drawn card is shown visually next to the piles (using the existing showDrawnCard pattern)
4. There is a visible pause (~1 second) between showing the drawn card and executing the move
5. After the move, the drawn card display is hidden and piles refresh normally
6. npm test passes; npm run build succeeds

# Intake Brief: Citadel variant option for Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map** | **Effort: Small** | **Risk: Low**

## Problem Statement

Classic Beleaguered Castle deals aces onto foundations before the game starts, leaving 48 cards in the tableau. The Citadel variant changes the deal so all 52 cards are dealt to the tableau with empty foundations, requiring the player to uncover and manually move aces to foundations. This feature adds the Citadel variant as a selectable option within the Beleaguered Castle game, giving players a choice of difficulty and play style.

## Users

- **Solitaire player:** Enjoys Beleaguered Castle but wants more challenge. Uncovering aces from the tableau adds strategic depth compared to the classic pre-placed-aces start.
  - *"As a Beleaguered Castle player, I want to start a Citadel game where no cards are pre-placed on foundations, so I have the extra challenge of uncovering and promoting aces myself."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pre-game variant selection:** A Citadel variant option is presented as a pre-game choice before the deal, allowing the player to choose between Classic and Citadel modes.
2. **Variant persistence:** The selected variant preference persists across page refreshes via browser storage (localStorage), matching the pattern used for difficulty/settings persistence.
3. **Citadel deal:** In Citadel mode, all 52 cards are dealt to the 8 tableau columns — no aces are pre-placed on foundations. All foundations start empty.
4. **Identical rules otherwise:** Game rules (build foundations up by suit, build tableau down regardless of suit, only top card of each column is available, empty columns accept any card, win/loss detection) remain identical to classic mode.
5. **Auto-move includes aces:** The auto-move heuristic operates on aces when they become available as the top card of a tableau column — if an ace is exposed and the corresponding foundation is empty, it is auto-moved to the foundation. Normal auto-move behavior for subsequent cards works identically to classic mode.
6. **Unit tests:** Unit tests cover the Citadel deal (all 52 cards in tableau, all foundations empty, no aces in foundations), auto-move with aces, and verify that variant selection persists correctly.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Card assets unchanged:** The existing 52-card deck (no jokers) is used. No new art assets are needed.
- **Beleaguered Castle architecture unchanged:** The variant is added within the existing Beleaguered Castle game structure. No new scenes or game entry points are needed — the variant is a game-option toggle.
- **Backward compatibility:** Classic mode remains the default and is unaffected. Existing save/load checkpoints from classic games continue to work.

## Existing State

- **Beleaguered Castle game (`example-games/beleaguered-castle/`)** is fully implemented and playable with classic deal (aces pre-placed, 48 cards in 8 columns of 6).
- **`BeleagueredCastleRules.ts`** contains `deal()`, which currently removes aces and places them on foundations before dealing remaining cards to tableau.
- **`BeleagueredCastleScene.ts`** calls `deal()` during `create()`, wired to the Phaser scene lifecycle. Options are displayed via the existing Settings panel (difficulty selector), but the variant selection should use a **pre-game popup** before dealing.
- **`SettingsPanel.ts`** provides reusable toggle/slider/difficulty selector UI patterns in a slide-in panel.
- **`SettingsStore.ts`** provides localStorage persistence helpers (difficulty, reduced-motion, end-turn keybind) — the variant selection can follow this pattern.
- **`BeleagueredCastleState.ts`** defines `BeleagueredCastleState` (foundations, tableau, seed, moveCount). The deal variant is implicit in the state (foundations empty = Citadel). No new state fields are needed for the variant itself, but the UI selection state should be persisted.
- **Save/load (`BeleagueredCastleSaveLoad.ts`)** serializes/deserializes game state via `SaveLoadStore`. Serialized state captures card positions directly, so variants are distinguished by foundation emptiness. No changes needed to save schema format.
- **Tests:** Comprehensive unit tests in `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleRules.test.ts` and browser tests for layout, overlay, and turn controller.

## Desired Change

1. **Add a Citadel deal function** to `BeleagueredCastleRules.ts` (or parameterize the existing `deal()` with a `citadel: boolean` flag) that deals all 52 cards to 8 tableau columns (4 columns of 7 cards, 4 columns of 6 cards — or another even distribution) with all foundations empty.
2. **Add a pre-game variant selection popup** before the deal animation, offering Classic and Citadel choices, with the selection persisted to localStorage.
3. **Update auto-move logic** (`findSafeAutoMoves`) to recognize that aces on top of tableau columns should be auto-moved to empty foundations. The existing rank-based safe-move heuristic should handle subsequent cards naturally after aces are placed.
4. **Wire the variant choice** through the scene lifecycle: the pre-game choice determines which `deal()` variant is called; the HUD, timer, and interactions remain unchanged.
5. **Write unit tests** for: Citadel-specific deal (all 52 cards in tableau, zero on foundations), auto-move targeting aces, and variant persistence round-trip. Update existing deal tests to be parameterized or separate.

## Related Work

- **Citadel variant option for Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV)** [this issue]: Work item being defined.
- **Beleaguered Castle (open solitaire) (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [completed]: Parent epic. Provides the full Beleaguered Castle implementation that this variant extends.
- **SettingsPanel (`src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`):** Reusable settings panel with difficulty selector pattern — useful reference for UI selection patterns, though the variant selection uses a pre-game popup.
- **SettingsStore (`src/ui/SettingsStore.ts`):** localStorage persistence pattern for difficulty/reduced-motion/end-turn-key settings — variant selection should follow the same pattern.
- **Beleaguered Castle Game Logic (CG-0MLTFCTNK10RQ41T)** [completed]: Initial implementation of `deal()`, move rules, win/loss detection — the deal function must be extended for Citadel.
- **Auto-Move to Foundations (CG-0MLTFEN5A0DG3P0M)** [completed]: Auto-move heuristic implementation — needs Citadel-aware ace promotion.
- **BeleagueredCastle Save/Load (`example-games/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleSaveLoad.ts`):** Existing serialization — should remain compatible; variant is implicit in state.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Auto-move ace promotion correctness:** The safe-move heuristic (`findSafeAutoMoves`) uses `foundationTopRank` which returns -1 for empty foundations. Code analysis (2026-08-09) shows the existing math already handles aces on empty foundations: `rankValue('A') = 0` gives `cardRank - 1 = -1`, and an empty foundation returns `-1`, so `minFoundationRank >= -1` evaluates true and aces are already eligible for auto-promotion. **Verification-first:** add the ace-promotion unit tests first; only modify `findSafeAutoMoves` if a test actually fails (e.g. mixed empty/non-empty foundation states).
- **Pre-game popup UX consistency:** The existing game has no pre-game popup (variant/options are in the Settings panel). A pre-game popup is a new UI pattern for this game and must feel cohesive with the existing overlay patterns. The popup should be dismissable and allow the player to proceed without friction.
- **Card distribution across 8 columns:** 52 cards across 8 columns creates uneven column sizes (4 columns of 6, 4 of 7 or similar). The renderer and deal animation must handle variable column heights correctly.
- **Save/load compatibility:** Existing classic-mode checkpoints should load correctly. A checkpoint saved in Citadel mode (foundations empty) should restore correctly, and the variant should be recognized on restore to use the correct deal type on new game.
- **Scope creep:** Additional variant features or refactoring opportunities may surface during implementation. Record opportunities for additional features/refactorings as work items linked to this item, rather than expanding scope.

### Assumptions
- The pre-game popup appears before the deal animation, similar to the existing resume-overlay pattern in `BeleagueredCastleScene.checkForSavedCheckpoint()`.
- The variant selection is persisted to localStorage using a key like `tce-bc-variant`, following the `SettingsStore` pattern.
- Card distribution for 52 cards across 8 columns: columns 0–3 get 7 cards each, columns 4–7 get 6 cards each (or another simple distribution). The exact distribution choice is an implementation detail.
- All foundations start completely empty in Citadel mode — unlike classic where aces occupy foundation slots from the start.
- Auto-move timing is identical to classic: `findSafeAutoMoves` runs inside `TurnController.executePlayerMove` (after each player move), not at deal time. Aces exposed by the deal will auto-move on the first player move, matching classic behaviour where the same trigger applies.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1: "How should the Citadel variant be selected? Options: (a) As a toggle/option within the existing Settings panel, (b) As a pre-game option before dealing (e.g., a popup choice at game start), (c) Some other mechanism."** — Answer (user): "b" (pre-game option before dealing). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- **Q2: "Should the variant selection persist across page refreshes (like difficulty settings via localStorage), or should it be a per-game choice?"** — Answer (user): "yes" (persist across page refreshes). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- **Q3: "For auto-move and auto-complete in Citadel mode — since foundations start empty, the current safe-move heuristic won't fire until aces are manually placed. Should auto-move/auto-complete work exactly the same as classic mode (just won't trigger until aces reach foundations), or should Citadel mode have different auto-move behavior?"** — Answer (user): "Start auto-move on aces, that is if an ace can be promoted then auto move it." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Auto-move should include ace promotion: when an ace becomes the top card of a tableau column and the corresponding foundation is empty, it should be auto-moved to the foundation. Subsequent cards follow the existing safe-move heuristic.

## Key Files

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleRules.ts` — Add Citadel deal function (all 52 cards to tableau, empty foundations) and verify/update `findSafeAutoMoves` for ace promotion from the tableau (the function is defined here and consumed by the TurnController).
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` — Add pre-game variant selection popup UI and wire variant choice.
- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` — localStorage persistence pattern for variant selection (reference; the variant key follows the same `STORAGE_KEY_*` get/set pattern).
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/help-content.json` — In-game help text; the "Setup" section describes the classic deal and must be updated to document the Citadel variant (AC 7).
- `README.md` — Root README game table row for Beleaguered Castle should mention the Citadel variant option (AC 7).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Game table / feature listing should reflect the variant option (AC 7).
- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleRules.test.ts` — Unit tests for Citadel deal, auto-move (ace promotion), and variant persistence.
- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleOverlay.browser.test.ts` — Browser tests for the pre-game variant selection popup UI (AC 1, AC 2).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB** – Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (completed)

## User Story

As a player, I want the game to correctly enforce Beleaguered Castle rules (build foundations up by suit, build tableau down regardless of suit, only top card movable, empty columns accept any card) so that every game is played correctly.

## Summary

Automatically move cards to foundations when safe to play after each player move, with compound undo support so undoing a player move also undoes all triggered auto-moves.

## User Story

As a player, I want cards to automatically move to foundations when it is clearly safe to do so, reducing tedious manual moves and making the game feel polished.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After each player move, the engine checks all tableau columns for cards safe to auto-move to foundations
- Auto-moves execute automatically with a brief animation delay between each
- Undoing a player move also undoes all auto-moves triggered by that move (compound undo via CompoundCommand)
- Auto-move chain is recorded as part of the triggering compound command in UndoRedoManager
- Auto-moves do NOT increment the player's move counter (only player-initiated moves count)
- Unit tests cover safe-move heuristic: cards that are safe and cards that are not safe to auto-move
- `npm test` passes; `npm run build` succeeds

## Open Question

The exact safe-to-auto-move heuristic needs to be defined during implementation. A conservative starting point: a card is safe to auto-move to its foundation if no tableau column contains a card of any suit that has a rank equal to the candidate card's rank minus one (i.e., no column needs this card as a potential build target). The implementer should document the chosen heuristic and test edge cases. Being too aggressive risks moving cards the player needs for tableau building; being too conservative leaves cards the player would prefer auto-moved.

## Minimal Implementation

- Implement `findSafeAutoMoves(state)` function that returns a list of cards safe to move to foundations
- Implement auto-move loop: after each player move, repeatedly call `findSafeAutoMoves()` and execute until no more safe moves exist
- Wrap player move + all triggered auto-moves in a `CompoundCommand` so undo reverses the entire chain
- Add tween animation for each auto-move (brief card flight from column to foundation)
- Ensure auto-moves do not trigger further compound nesting (flat compound)

## Dependencies

- Drag-and-Drop Card Input (CG-0MLTFDTMT0G2I0ZT): move execution pipeline
- Undo/Redo Module (CG-0MLTFC94Z00K32ZI): CompoundCommand support

## Deliverables

- Auto-move logic in game rules module
- CompoundCommand integration in scene
- Unit tests for safe-move heuristic

## User Story

As a player, I want the game to automatically complete when the remaining moves are obvious, so I do not have to tediously move cards one by one to the foundations when victory is assured.

- Auto-complete triggers when all remaining tableau cards can be played to foundations in some order

- Auto-complete plays all remaining moves with animation (cards fly to foundations in sequence)
- Player can interrupt auto-complete by pressing undo
- Auto-complete is undoable as a single compound action (CompoundCommand)
- Auto-complete does not trigger if any column has cards in non-descending order that block foundation play
