data.description:
Headline: Add a "Refresh investments" action to the Main Street investments row that lets a player pay a fixed coin cost to immediately replace the visible investments row with newly-drawn cards.

Problem statement

Players can become stuck with an investments row they don't want to purchase. Provide a UI action and game logic that lets the player buy a fresh set of investment opportunities (replace the visible investments row with newly-drawn cards) so players have an alternative to waiting for the market to naturally refill.

Users

- Primary: Players of the Main Street example game who want to refresh the investments row when current cards are unappealing or unaffordable.
  - Example user story: "As a player, when I don't like the available investment cards, I want to pay coins to redraw the investments row so I can get new options to consider this turn."
- Secondary: QA and automated tests that verify market invariants and deck accounting.

Success criteria

- A "Refresh investments" action is available in the investments row UI during the player's MarketPhase.
- When the player invokes the action and can pay the cost, exactly the visible investments row slots are replaced immediately with newly-drawn cards drawn using the same deck-selection rules as refillInvestmentsMarket (upgrades from the upgrade deck; investment events from the event deck restricted to Investment-trigger cards).
- The player is charged the configured fixed coin cost when the action is taken; coins are deducted from state.resourceBank.coins and the action is rejected if the player lacks coins.
- Removed cards are moved to their respective discard piles (not merged back into decks) and deck invariants are preserved (no duplicate ids in visible market after replacement). Add unit tests that assert correct discard/deck accounting.
- Implementation includes unit tests covering legality, execution, and deck/discard effects; the project test suite passes after changes.
- Unit tests should be added under tests/main-street/ (suggested name: refresh-investments.test.ts) to validate all behaviors and edge-cases.
- All related documentation and in-code comments (MainStreet README/market module) are updated to reflect the new action.

Constraints

- The action must use existing market/deck abstractions and follow current conventions in MainStreetMarket.ts (e.g., draw upgrades from decks.upgrade, select investment-trigger events from decks.event).
- The change must not alter end-of-turn market refill semantics (market refill processes that occur at turn boundaries should remain unchanged unless explicitly required by reviewers).
- UI affordance must only be enabled during MarketPhase; the server/game-state validation must also enforce the same timing restriction.
- Keep changes local to the Main Street example game (no engine-level API changes) unless reviewers request extraction.

Existing state

- MainStreetMarket.ts contains market logic including refillInvestmentsMarket, purchaseUpgrade, purchaseEvent, and helper functions that draw from decks.upgrade and decks.event.
- The investments row is modeled in MainStreetState.state.market.investments and is refilled at start-of-turn via refillInvestmentsMarket. Purchasing upgrade/event currently removes a card from the investments row but does not immediately refill it.
- UI rendering and click handlers live in example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts and MainStreetTurnController.ts.
- Tests exist around refill and purchase behaviour (tests/main-street/market.test.ts and related integration tests).

Desired change

- Add a market action and implementation (suggested name: refreshInvestmentsMarket or buyInvestmentOpportunities) to MainStreetMarket.ts that:
  - Exposes a legality check (canRefreshInvestments) and an execution function (refreshInvestments) that perform validation and mutate state in-place.
  - Legality: action is allowed only during MarketPhase and if state.resourceBank.coins >= FIXED_COST.
  - Execution: deduct FIXED_COST from state.resourceBank.coins; remove all visible investments row cards and push them to their discard piles; draw replacement cards using the same rules as refillInvestmentsMarket until the investments row reaches MARKET_INVESTMENT_SLOTS or decks are exhausted.
  - Return a PurchaseResult-like structure describing replaced cards and coins spent for logging.
- Wire the action into UI: add a small button in the investments row rendering that calls the existing turn controller handler (e.g., onRefreshInvestmentsClick) which calls server-side logic (or direct state mutation in single-player example) and animates the replacement.
- Add unit tests in tests/main-street to verify legality, coin deduction, correct discard handling, and that the investments row contains no duplicate ids after replacement.
- Update relevant docs and add an entry in the Main Street help content describing the new action and cost.

Related work

- example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts — market logic and refillInvestmentsMarket (primary implementation location).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts — market state shape and addLog helper used for logging mutations.
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetTurnController.ts — existing UI click handlers for purchases; will host the new click handler.
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts — investments row rendering and place to add the UI button.
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts — MARKET_INVESTMENT_* constants and card type definitions.
- tests/main-street/market.test.ts, market.integration.test.ts — existing tests to extend with refresh tests.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Cost / payment model — How should the player pay to buy new opportunities?" — Answer (user): "A: Fixed coin cost (e.g., 2 coins) per redraw." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Replacement source and handling of removed cards — When the investments row is replaced, how are the new cards drawn and what happens to the old cards?" — Answer (user): "A: Draw upgrades from the upgrade deck and events from the event deck (same as refillInvestmentsMarket). Removed cards go to their respective discard piles." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Timing and limits — When is this action allowed and are there usage limits?" — Answer (user): "A: Allowed during the player's MarketPhase only; unlimited times (subject to coins)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: scope creep — adding broad market refactor or engine-level API changes during this task could expand the work beyond a small example-game change. Mitigation: if additional extraction/refactor is desired, record as a separate follow-up work item rather than expanding this item.
- Risk: deck exhaustion and partial refill — if decks lack sufficient cards the investments row may be partially filled. Mitigation: tests must cover partial-fill behaviour and logs should record partial refill.
- Risk: duplicate id or deck accounting bugs — replacing market cards could introduce duplicate ids if discard/deck operations are mishandled. Mitigation: include tests that assert unique ids and correct deck/discard counts.

Notes and assumptions (agent inference)

- Fixed-cost value (exact coin amount) was not specified beyond the model choice. Suggested sensible default: 2 coins. Implementation should put the numeric cost in a single constant (e.g., REFRESH_INVESTMENTS_COST = 2) so maintainers can adjust easily. This default is recorded as an implementation suggestion and should be confirmed by reviewers.
- The intended UX is immediate replacement on click; tests and UI should reflect immediate replacement (not deferred to end-of-turn). If reviewers prefer a deferred refill, record as follow-up.

Draft headline to use in the work item body:
Add a "Buy new investment opportunities" action to the investments row that replaces the visible investments with newly-drawn cards for a fixed coin cost.

## Summary
Evaluate active challenges during each EndCheck phase and award bonus points for newly completed challenges.

## Player Experience
Each turn, the engine checks whether any active challenges have been met. Completed challenges are announced in the activity log and bonus points are reflected in the score.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `evaluateChallenges(state)` function runs during EndCheck (inside checkEndConditions or called before it).
- For each active challenge not yet completed: run its evaluator; if true, mark completed = true and push its ID to challengesCompleted.
- Once a challenge is marked complete, it stays complete (no revocation). Subsequent calls with a state where the condition is no longer met do not revoke completion.
- computeScore already accounts for challengesCompleted.length * CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS -- no formula change needed.
- Activity log entry added when a challenge is completed (e.g. 'Challenge completed: Foodie Row (+10 pts)').
- Evaluator does not mark a challenge complete when its condition is not met (negative case with state fixture that fails each challenge).
- Unit tests: challenge evaluation triggers correctly; score reflects bonus; completed challenges persist across turns.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add `evaluateChallenges(state: MainStreetState): void` to MainStreetChallenges.ts or MainStreetEngine.ts.
- Call it inside the EndCheck phase in MainStreetEngine.ts before checkEndConditions score calculation.
- Add activity log entries via existing addLog helper.
- Unit tests covering: no challenges -> no change; challenge met -> marked complete; already-complete challenge -> no re-evaluation side effects.

- State Integration & Setup Wiring (CG-0MMJO6GVF12SW5NQ)

## Deliverables

## Summary
Implement the 'all challenges complete' automatic win path in the EndCheck phase.

## Player Experience
If a player completes all active challenges in a run, the game ends in victory regardless of score -- rewarding strategic challenge-focused play.

## Acceptance Criteria
- If all activeChallenges are completed after evaluation, the game ends with gameResult = 'win' and endReason = 'all_challenges'.
- This win condition is checked after challenge evaluation but before the existing score-threshold check.
- Activity log entry: 'Victory: All challenges completed!'
- TOTAL_CHALLENGES is derived from activeChallenges.length (not a hardcoded constant) -- adapts to difficulty-based challenge count.
- If 0 challenges are active (edge case with count=0), the all_challenges win condition does NOT trigger (0/0 is not a win).
- Unit test: game with all challenges completed ends as win regardless of score.
- Unit test: game with some but not all challenges completed does not trigger this win condition.
- Unit test: 0 active challenges does not trigger all_challenges win.

## Minimal Implementation
- Uncomment and implement the all_challenges check in checkEndConditions in MainStreetEngine.ts.
- Wire it after evaluateChallenges runs.
- Add 3 unit tests (all complete -> win; partial -> continue; zero challenges -> no trigger).

Headline summary

Add SVG synergy icons to Main Street card art so players can instantly recognise synergy types on cards. Includes SVG assets, updates to the card generator, accessible fallbacks, and a small smoke test.

Problem statement

Players should be able to quickly recognise a business card's synergy type(s) at a glance. Currently the Main Street card SVGs and UI use textual labels and colors; adding small, consistent icons for each synergy type on the card art will make synergies more immediately scannable and improve readability on small displays.

Users

- Players: can more quickly identify synergy types on market cards, street slots, held event cards, and thumbnails.
- Designers / artists: validate visual cohesion and color mapping across the card set.
- QA: test that icons render and fall back correctly across viewport sizes and in test environments.

Success criteria

- SVG icon assets are added in public/assets/games/main-street/svg/icons/ using filenames:
  - ms-icon-food.svg
  - ms-icon-culture.svg
  - ms-icon-commerce.svg
  - ms-icon-service.svg
  - ms-icon-entertainment.svg
  Icons must be vector SVGs suitable for inclusion in card SVGs and for rasterisation at multiple sizes.
- Each generated card SVG (public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg) includes the corresponding synergy icon positioned in the lower-left (or similar unobtrusive location) at a visually consistent size (16x16 visual target; scalable).
- When the icon asset cannot be loaded in runtime environments, the renderer must display a fallback solid-color dot using the existing synergyColor mapping (see example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts). The fallback must match the same logical colour as the icon accent.
- UI smoke test: a deterministic test (unit or headless UI smoke) verifies that a sample generated card contains either an embedded <image>/<use> node for the icon or an aria-label/alt text and that if rasterised in the scene a texture key named with ms_card_* exists. (Concrete test file: tests/main-street/card-icons.smoke.test.ts or extension of existing market/render smoke tests.)
- No visual overlap: cards in Market, Street grid, Hand, and Incident queue render the icon without overlapping important text at common breakpoints (desktop and mobile). Visual regressions are validated by a manual spot-check or an updated E2E screenshot fixture.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (card generation script, asset credit if needed, and README/docs). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Icon assets must be SVG (per team preference) and added under public/assets/games/main-street/svg/icons/.
- Follow existing asset naming and generation conventions used by scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs and the card rendering pipeline (SvgDomRenderer, rasteriseSvgToTexture).
- Avoid large runtime changes to rasterisation; prefer embedding the icon in card SVG source so existing prewarm and rasterisation code picks it up.
- Keep layout conservative: icons must not change card bounding boxes or require new layout engine behaviour.

Existing state

- Card SVGs are generated by scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs into public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg; the script already writes a small synergies text label at bottom-left.
- There is a canonical synergyColor mapping used across the codebase (example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts and scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs).
- MainStreetScene supports DOM-based SVG rendering (SvgDomRenderer) and rasterisation helpers (rasteriseSvgToTexture, makeTextureKey) used when prewarming textures.
- Help panel currently lists synergy types textually (MainStreetScene.initHelpPanel) but the accepted scope for this work is "on the cards themselves" (requested by stakeholder during intake).

Desired change

- Add five SVG icon source files into public/assets/games/main-street/svg/icons/ following the naming convention above and using the existing synergyColor palette for fill/accents.
- Update scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs to insert an inline <svg> icon (or <use>/<image>) at the same coordinate area where the current synergies text is placed so generated card SVGs contain the icon.
- Ensure the generated SVG includes accessible aria-label attributes for the icon (e.g., role="img" aria-label="Food icon") and that the existing placeholder generation used by MainStreetScene is compatible.
- Add a small smoke test to tests/main-street/ verifying that a generated sample card SVG contains the expected icon element or fallback marker.
- Update docs: docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md (if necessary) and any generation script README to note the new icons and file locations.

Related work

Potentially related docs:
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts — scene-level rendering, prewarmVisibleCardTextures, SvgDomRenderer usage and initHelpPanel (evidence of where card SVGs are used).
- scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs — generator for card SVGs (place to embed icons into the card art).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts — canonical CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES, synergyColor mapping used by the generator.
- src/ui/HelpPanel.ts and src/ui/CardGameScene.ts — existing help panel and panel rendering (references for accessibility and fallback behaviour).
- docs/main-street/card-catalog.md — catalog describing synergies, useful for naming and mapping.

Potentially related work items:
- CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA: Add synergy icons to Main Street help panel (this item; we are updating it to scope icons on cards)
- CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (visual polish context)

Problem statement

When a player finishes a Main Street game and starts a new game, the Activity Log UI panel remains blank and does not display any new entries for the newly started game.

Users

- Players of the Main Street example game who rely on the activity log to see what events fired and why (playtesters, QA).  
- Developers and maintainers who rely on the activity-log tests to detect regressions in game state and UI rendering.

Repro steps (known)

1) Launch the Main Street example (`example-games/main-street`).
2) Start a new game and play until the game ends (lose or win).
3) Start a new game from the end-of-game menu.
4) Observe that the Activity Log panel remains blank (no new entries appear) despite gameplay.

Success criteria

- Manual: Starting a fresh Main Street game results in an initially empty activity log that immediately receives new entries as game events occur.  
- Automated: Add or update unit and integration tests so that a full playthrough seed (or deterministic mock) verifies activity-log entries are produced after a new-game transition. Tests must fail before the fix and pass after the fix.  
- Non‑regression: Fix does not alter activity-log behaviour in other games or break transcript persistence.  
- Code quality: Fix includes a small, reviewable code change with clear unit tests and one integration test that covers the new-game transition.

Constraints

- Scope is Main Street only (example-games/main-street). Do not make sweeping changes to the core engine unless investigation shows the bug is in shared code.  
- Preserve existing transcript persistence behaviour and avoid changing how transcripts are saved to IndexedDB or dev POST endpoints.  
- Keep changes minimal and covered by tests; prefer fixing the new-game UI/state lifecycle rather than adding global state resets.

Existing state / observations

- UI code: `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — contains activity-log panel rendering and a comment that the panel is persistent and rebuilt from `state.activityLog` (see `const entries = this.state.activityLog`).  
- State model: `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — defines `activityLog: LogEntry[]`, helper to append entries, and state cloning on save/load.  
- Related work items: several completed items implemented the activity log UI and tests. These items indicate there are unit/integration tests that assert log entry generation and UI rendering (see list below).  

Likely root causes to investigate (do not assume; verify in code)

- `MainStreetState.activityLog` is not being reset when a new game starts (old reference persists or is replaced with an empty array that UI doesn't observe).  
- The scene's activity-log UI is not being rebuilt or re-bound to the updated `state.activityLog` when a new game is created.  
- A timing/order-of-operations bug where activity-log mutations occur before the UI registers for updates.  

Desired change

1. Investigate and identify the root cause in `MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetState.ts`.
2. Implement a minimal fix so that starting a new game results in a clean activity log that receives events for the new session. Possible fixes (to be validated in code): ensure `state.activityLog` is correctly initialised for new games and/or ensure the activity-log panel rebuilds or rebinds to `state.activityLog` on new-game transition.  
3. Add unit tests for activity-log entry generation and an integration test that reproduces the repro (end game → start new game → assert new entries appear).  
4. Update or extend existing activity-log tests so the suite would have caught this regression.  

Related work

- Files
  - `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — activity log panel layout and rebuild logic; references `this.state.activityLog`.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — state model and `appendLog()` helper; initialisation and cloning behaviour.
  - `src/core-engine/TranscriptRecorder.ts`, `src/core-engine/TranscriptStore.ts` — transcript persistence helpers (referenced for non-regression checks).
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — guidance on transcripts, test fixtures, and replay tooling.

- Worklog items
  - CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 — Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI (completed): implements the visual activity log panel; review for regressions.  
  - CG-0MM8NP3MP0SW4XF7 — Render scrollable activity log panel in MainStreetScene (completed): relevant UI work.  
  - CG-0MM8NPBOT0N8TNU9 — Unit tests for activity log entry generation (completed): review and extend to cover new-game transition.  
  - CG-0MM8NOSK60H61TIW — Instrument engine functions to generate activity log entries (completed): shows where entries are created.

Acceptance tests / verification steps (to be automated where possible)

1. Unit: Test `appendLog(state, text, type)` results in `state.activityLog` having a new entry with expected fields.  
2. Integration: Automate a deterministic playthrough or mock transitions — start game, end game, start new game — assert that `state.activityLog` contains entries after the new-game starts and that the scene renders them.  
3. Manual: QA: repro the original steps in dev server and verify new entries appear in UI after starting a new game.

## Summary

Implement the runtime meta-progression system as specified in `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (Meta-Progression Spec, CG-0MMJ8S8TJ0HE9S9M). The spec is complete and the blocking dependency (Save/Load Engine Infrastructure, CG-0MMJ8S90S1P2HW74) is done. This work item covers the full implementation of the 5-tier unlock framework, campaign persistence, tier evaluation, and deck filtering.

## User Story

As a player, I want my strong single-run performances to permanently unlock new Business, Event, and Upgrade cards for future runs, so that each session rewards mastery with expanded strategic options rather than direct power.

## Scope

Implement all seven user stories from the PRD:

1. **US-1 Tier Evaluation at End of Run** -- Evaluate `resourceBank.reputation` against tier thresholds after EndCheck; unlock matching tiers.
2. **US-2 Challenge-Based Tier Unlock** -- Evaluate challenge-completion conditions as an alternative unlock path for each tier.
3. **US-3 Milestone Latch Permanence** -- Ensure unlocked tiers are never removed regardless of run outcome.
4. **US-4 Card Pool Filtering by Tier** -- Extend `createBusinessDeck`, `createEventDeck`, `createUpgradeDeck` to accept optional `unlockedCardIds` for tier-based filtering.
5. **US-5 Campaign Persistence Round-Trip** -- Upgrade schema to v2, implement v1->v2 migration, persist and restore campaign data with `milestoneHistory`.
6. **US-6 Backward-Compatible Defaults** -- All existing tests pass; deck builders without `unlockedCardIds` produce unchanged output.
7. **US-7 Milestone History Tracking** -- Append `MilestoneRecord` entries on each tier unlock.

## Key Implementation Tasks

- **Tier Definition Registry**: Create `TierDefinition` interface and `TIER_DEFINITIONS` / `ORDERED_TIER_DEFINITIONS` data structures mapping tier IDs to thresholds, challenge conditions, and card assignments (per PRD Section 4.3.5).
- **Extended Campaign Data Model**: Add `schemaVersion`, `unlockedCardIds`, `milestoneHistory` fields to `MainStreetCampaignProgress`; add `MilestoneRecord` interface (per PRD Section 3.2).
- **Schema Migration**: Bump `MAIN_STREET_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2; update serializer with v1->v2 migration (per PRD Section 4.3.2).
- **updateCampaignAfterRun()**: New function implementing post-run tier evaluation, statistics update, and persistence (per PRD Section 4.3.4).
- **Deck Filtering**: Add optional `unlockedCardIds` parameter to deck-building functions; filter templates when provided, use full pool when omitted (per PRD Section 4.3.6).
- **Game Setup Wiring**: Load campaign at game start; pass `unlockedCardIds` to deck builders (per PRD Section 4.4).
- **End-of-Run Wiring**: Call `updateCampaignAfterRun` after EndCheck phase completes.

## Files Likely Affected

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` -- Extended campaign interface
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` -- Schema v2, migration, updateCampaignAfterRun
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` -- Deck builder filtering, tier card ID constants
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` -- End-of-run wiring
- New file: `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts` -- Tier definition registry, deriveUnlockedCardIds helper

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 7 user stories from `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` Section 5 are implemented and pass their testable conditions.
2. Tier definition registry contains all 5 tiers with correct thresholds, challenge conditions, and card assignments matching the PRD.
3. Campaign schema v2 round-trips correctly through save/load (save, reload, verify all fields).
4. v1 campaign data is automatically migrated to v2 on load.
5. Deck builders with `unlockedCardIds` return correctly filtered decks; without the parameter they return the full pool.
6. Monte Carlo harness runs pass with the tier-filtered deck (seeded, deterministic).
7. All existing tests (M1 + M2 content) pass with 0 failures (`npm test`).
8. `npm run build` succeeds with no TypeScript errors.

## Dependencies

- Save/Load Engine Infrastructure (CG-0MMJ8S90S1P2HW74) -- DONE
- Meta-Progression Spec (CG-0MMJ8S8TJ0HE9S9M) -- DONE (the PRD this implements)
- Challenge System (CG-0MMJ8S8091RMCUJA) -- DONE (challenges used as tier unlock triggers)
- Expanded Card Pool (CG-0MMJ8S7LE0ZGBMEL) -- DONE (cards assigned to tiers)

## References

- PRD: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md`
- GDD Content Design: `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Section 6.2)
- Engine Capabilities Audit: CG-0MM4RAT5L12FHWKP (Save/Load gap 4.5, now resolved)

## Summary

The meta-progression backend (CG-0MMLTPXVR0F9K0JS) is fully implemented but entirely invisible to the player. The PRD data flow (Section 4.4, line 628) explicitly requires: "Display results + any newly unlocked tiers/cards." US-7 states: "As a player, I want to see a record of my milestone achievements." Neither is implemented.

## User Story

As a returning player who just finished a strong run, I want to see which new tier I unlocked and which cards were added to my pool, so that I understand why future runs offer different cards and feel motivated to keep pushing for higher tiers.

## Scope

Add meta-progression information to the existing game-over overlay and optionally the HUD. This is informational display only -- no animations, celebrations, or greyed-out card visuals (those are deferred to M4 per PRD Section 6).

### Must Have (M2 scope)
1. **Game-over overlay: Tier unlock notification** -- After score breakdown, show any newly unlocked tiers (e.g. "NEW: Tier 3 - Neighborhood unlocked!") with the trigger reason (reputation or challenge path).
2. **Game-over overlay: New cards preview** -- List the specific card names that were added to the pool by newly unlocked tiers (from `TierDefinition.newCardIds`).
3. **Game-over overlay: Current tier indicator** -- Show the player's highest unlocked tier (e.g. "Current Tier: 3 / 5 - Neighborhood").
4. **Game-over overlay: Campaign stats** -- Show total runs, total wins, win rate, highest score, persistent reputation below the score breakdown.

### Nice to Have (can be deferred)
5. **HUD tier badge** -- Small tier indicator in the HUD (e.g. "T3" or tier name) so the player knows their tier during gameplay.
6. **Milestone history panel** -- Accessible from game-over overlay or a menu, showing the full milestone history with timestamps and trigger details.
7. **Progress toward next tier** -- Show how close the player is to the next tier threshold (reputation needed or challenge conditions).

## Implementation Approach

### Key Constraint
`updateCampaignProgress()` (line 394-399) is async fire-and-forget, called before `showGameOverOverlay()` (line 425-426). To display newly unlocked tiers, we need to capture the "before" state of `campaign.unlockedTiers` before calling `updateCampaignAfterRun()`, then diff against the "after" state.

### Suggested Approach
1. In `endTurn()`, before calling `updateCampaignProgress()`, snapshot `[...this.campaign.unlockedTiers]`.
2. Make `updateCampaignProgress()` return (or await) the updated campaign.
3. Compute `newlyUnlockedTiers = afterTiers.filter(t => !beforeTiers.includes(t))`.
4. Pass `newlyUnlockedTiers` and the updated `campaign` to `showGameOverOverlay()`.
5. In the overlay, render the new sections after the challenge details and before the difficulty selector.

### Files Likely Affected
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` -- `endTurn()`, `showGameOverOverlay()`, `updateCampaignProgress()`
- Possibly `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts` -- Helper to map tier IDs to display names/card names

### Data Available
- `this.campaign` -- Full `MainStreetCampaignProgress` (mutated in place by `updateCampaignAfterRun`)
- `TIER_DEFINITIONS[tierId]` -- Has `.name`, `.newCardIds`, `.cumulativeCardIds`
- Card template names can be looked up from deck builders or a new lookup helper

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a run that unlocks one or more tiers, the game-over overlay clearly displays which tiers were newly unlocked and which cards were added.
2. After any completed run, the game-over overlay shows the player's current highest tier.
3. Campaign statistics (total runs, wins, win rate, highest score) are visible on the game-over overlay.
4. When no new tier is unlocked, the tier unlock section is not shown (no empty/confusing UI).
5. The overlay panel height adjusts dynamically to accommodate the new sections.
6. All existing tests pass (`npm test`), `npm run build` succeeds.
7. New tests verify that the campaign data passed to the overlay is correct (unit tests for the tier diff logic).

## References

- PRD: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` Section 4.4 (data flow), US-7 (milestone history)
- Backend implementation: CG-0MMLTPXVR0F9K0JS (completed)
- Game-over overlay: `MainStreetScene.ts:1486-1607`
- Campaign update flow: `MainStreetScene.ts:394-399, 413-439`

## Summary

In MainStreetScene.endTurn(), before calling updateCampaignProgress(), snapshot the current campaign.unlockedTiers array. After the campaign is updated (in place by updateCampaignAfterRun), compute the set of newly unlocked tier IDs by diffing the before and after states. Pass this information to showGameOverOverlay().

## Key Constraint

updateCampaignAfterRun() mutates the campaign object in place. Since updateCampaignProgress() is fire-and-forget async but the mutation happens synchronously within the Promise body, we need to either: (a) make updateCampaignProgress() awaitable, or (b) snapshot before and read after the synchronous mutation (which happens inside the .then() of the async call -- so this won't work). The safest approach is to await updateCampaignAfterRun() or restructure the flow.

## Suggested Approach

1. Snapshot `[...this.campaign.unlockedTiers]` before calling updateCampaignProgress().
2. Change updateCampaignProgress() to return the Promise from updateCampaignAfterRun().
3. Await it in endTurn() (or use .then()) before calling showGameOverOverlay().
4. Compute newlyUnlockedTiers = campaign.unlockedTiers.filter(t => !snapshotBefore.includes(t)).
5. Pass newlyUnlockedTiers to showGameOverOverlay().

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Newly unlocked tier IDs are correctly computed after each run.
2. When no new tiers are unlocked the list is empty.
3. The overlay receives the newly unlocked tier IDs and the updated campaign.
4. All existing tests pass. npm run build succeeds.

## Sections to Add

1. **Tier Unlock Notification** -- Only shown when newlyUnlockedTiers is non-empty. For each newly unlocked tier: 'NEW: Tier N - TierName unlocked!' with the trigger reason (reputation threshold or challenge path). Use green color for emphasis.

## Summary

When playing Main Street in Easy mode, the player cannot purchase cards in the first round. The UI rejects the action saying the player is in the 'day start' phase. If the player clicks 'End Turn', the overlay displays 'Processing end of turn...' but never completes — the game hangs permanently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Main Street from the game selector.
2. Select Easy difficulty.
3. Start a new game.
4. Attempt to buy a card from the market in round 1.
5. Observe: purchase is rejected (day start phase error).
6. Click 'End Turn'.
7. Observe: 'Processing end of turn...' appears but the game never advances.

## Expected Behaviour

- The player should be able to buy cards during the market phase in round 1.
- Clicking 'End Turn' should process the turn and advance to the next day (or trigger game-over if conditions are met).

## Actual Behaviour

- Buying is blocked with a phase mismatch error.
- End Turn hangs indefinitely on 'Processing end of turn...'.

## Impact

This is a critical issue: Easy mode is completely unplayable. Players cannot progress past the first turn.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In Easy mode, the first round enters the market phase correctly and allows card purchases.
2. Clicking 'End Turn' in Easy mode processes the turn and advances the game.
3. All existing tests pass. npm run build succeeds.
4. A new or updated test confirms Easy mode round-1 market phase is reachable.

data.description:
## Problem

In `MainStreetScene.loadCampaignAndSetup()` (line 370-394), the async campaign load replaces `this.state` with a fresh state in `DayStart` phase AFTER `create()` has already called `startDayPhase()` which transitioned the original state to `MarketPhase`. The async callback only calls `this.refreshAll()` instead of `this.startDayPhase()`, leaving the engine in `DayStart` while the UI shows market phase.

## Fix

Replace `this.refreshAll()` at line 388 with `this.startDayPhase()` so the new state is properly transitioned from DayStart to MarketPhase.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When async campaign load replaces the state, `startDayPhase()` is called instead of just `refreshAll()`
2. After the fix, `state.phase` is `MarketPhase` when the UI shows market controls
3. All existing tests pass
data.title: Fix async campaign load race condition in MainStreetScene

data.description:
## Problem

`endTurn()` in MainStreetScene sets `uiPhase = 'animating'` and instruction text to 'Processing end of turn...' BEFORE calling `processEndOfTurn(state)`. If `processEndOfTurn` throws (e.g. due to phase mismatch), the function aborts without ever calling the delayed callback that would advance the game or show results. The UI stays permanently stuck showing 'Processing end of turn...'.

## Fix

Wrap the `processEndOfTurn(this.state)` call in a try/catch. On error, reset `uiPhase` to `'market'`, show an error message, and call `refreshAll()` so the player can recover.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. If `processEndOfTurn` throws, the game does not hang
2. The player sees an error message and can still interact with the game
3. All existing tests pass
data.title: Add defensive try/catch in endTurn to prevent permanent hang

Problem statement
-----------------
Extend the Main Street Monte Carlo harness so it can run and evaluate the project AI strategies (greedy + random) at scale, produce JSON and CSV metrics, and gate CI with a configurable win‑rate guardrail. This will let designers and engineers validate economy and difficulty balance deterministically across many seeded runs.

Users
-----
- Designers: validate economic balance and difficulty targets using repeatable Monte Carlo results.
- Engineers: run automated stability checks and performance regressions in CI and locally.
- QA: reproduce failing seeds and verify fixes.

User stories
- As a designer, I can run 200 seeded Monte Carlo runs with the greedy and random AI and see win rate and key metrics in JSON and CSV so I can validate balance changes.
- As an engineer, I can invoke `npm run monte-carlo -- --strategy <name> --seeds <n> --maxTurns <n>` locally or in CI and have the pipeline fail if win rate falls outside the guardrail.
- As QA, I can repro a single failing seed and inspect the run transcript/metrics to diagnose issues.

Success criteria
----------------
- MonteCarlo harness accepts `--strategy` (default `greedy`), `--seeds` (default 200), and `--maxTurns` (default 25).  
- Output artifacts: a JSON file containing `MonteCarloMetrics` and a CSV export of runs; both written to the `--out` path when provided.  
- CI guardrail: a test that fails the build when greedy strategy win rate on Medium falls outside 20–80%.  
- Strategies wired: `greedy` and `random` strategies are discoverable and selectable by name by the harness.  
- Existing Monte Carlo and integration tests remain green after changes.

Constraints
-----------
- Deterministic RNG/seed handling must be preserved so runs are reproducible.  
- Keep run-time reasonable in CI; default seeds=200 and maxTurns=25 are accepted unless changed.  
- Do not alter game mechanics as part of this task; only add harness wiring, CLI flags, and CI guardrail.

Existing state
--------------
- Current harness: `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` implements runMonteCarlo and CSV exporter; `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` is a thin runner.  
- Tests: `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` and related integration tests exist and exercise the harness.  
- AI strategies: Random and Greedy strategies are implemented elsewhere in the Main Street example (per repo search and work-item references).  
- Worklog item: CG-0MMN8V9UU0MF2GHK already exists and is staged to `idea` and `in-progress`.

Desired change
--------------
- Extend `RunMonteCarloOptions`/`MonteCarloStrategy` to include strategy names for `greedy` and `random` (if not already present).  
- Update `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and npm script `monte-carlo` to accept `--strategy`, `--seeds`, `--maxTurns`, and `--out`.  
- Wire harness to import and call the corresponding AI strategy implementation via a name->factory map.  
- Add a CI test that executes the harness (with defaults) and fails the build when the greedy win rate falls outside 20–80%.  
- Ensure outputs (JSON + CSV) are produced and linked as job artifacts for debugging.

Related work
------------
Potentially related docs
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts — current harness implementation and CSV exporter.  
- scripts/monte-carlo.ts — CLI runner that invokes the harness.  
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts — AI strategy implementations and strategy notes.  
- tests/main-street/monte-carlo-balance.test.ts — existing Monte Carlo balance test that will need to remain green.

Potentially related work items
- Main Street M3: Monte Carlo Harness Extension for AI Strategies (CG-0MMN8V9UU0MF2GHK) — this intake (open, high).  
- Main Street M3: Random AI Strategy (CG-0MMN8UKE10G7GASW) — Random strategy implementation (completed).  
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 3 -- AI, Hints, and Undo System (CG-0MM4REQ4C01X8C08) — parent PRD work item with AI milestone context (in-progress).  
- Tests, Playtests & Monte Carlo Harness (CG-0MMJ8S9FI0E0Q9JP) — prior harness/test work (completed).

Notes / decisions captured from intake
-------------------------------
- Defaults confirmed: seeds=200, maxTurns=25, default strategy=`greedy`.  
- CI guardrail behavior: treat guardrail as a hard CI failure when win rate is outside 20–80% (requested).  
- Strategy availability: Random and Greedy strategies are present and will be imported into the harness by name.

Open questions
--------------
1) Where should the CI job be defined/placed (existing `ci/` workflow or a new workflow)? Suggested default: add to existing main CI workflow as a separate job that runs the harness and uploads artifacts.  
2) Are there required artifact retention or naming conventions for the JSON/CSV output in CI? Suggested default: `results/main-street-monte-carlo-<strategy>-<timestamp>.json|csv` in job artifacts.  
3) Should the guardrail test be parameterized per environment (e.g., wider thresholds in ephemeral branches)? Suggested default: keep guardrail strict in main branch CI only.

Please review this draft and provide any clarifications or edits. If this looks correct, approve and I will proceed to finalize the intake and update the Worklog item description.

Headline: Main Street M3: Undo/Redo System

Problem statement

Implement a robust Undo/Redo system for Main Street by wrapping all player market actions in Command objects and integrating with the engine UndoRedoManager, plus UI controls and tests so players can undo/redo market actions and developers can reproduce and validate behavior.

Users

- Players: want to undo accidental buys or experiment with placements (user story examples: undo last buy, redo after undo, compound action undo for buy+upgrade).
- Developers / QA: need deterministic undo/redo behavior for testing and Monte Carlo balance harnesses that exercise full action flows.

Success criteria

- Undo reverses last market action and fully restores all affected state (streetGrid, resourceBank, market slots, heldEvent, appliedUpgrades, activityLog).
- Redo re-applies an undone action; executing a new action after undo clears the redo stack.
- Compound actions (buy+upgrade) undo as a single step via CompoundCommand.
- Undo/Redo UI buttons are visible in MarketPhase and enable/disable correctly based on stack state; Undo stack clears on end-of-turn.
- Unit and integration tests covering single-action undo, compound undo, redo, empty-stack no-op, stack clear on end-of-turn; all tests pass and build succeeds.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Use the existing UndoRedoManager, Command, and CompoundCommand from src/core-engine/UndoRedoManager.ts; avoid engine API changes where possible.
- Undo stack must be per-game (scene/state) and cleared at end-of-turn (no cross-turn undo).
- Actions executed during resolution phases (Income/Incident/EndCheck) are not undoable.
- Hint and AI systems should record undo/hint events in the transcript; transcripts must remain backwards-compatible.

# Intake Draft: Parameterize Monte Carlo CI guardrail and runtime (CG-0MMP0Q8051WJTSWT)

Headline
Make the Monte Carlo CI guardrail and harness runtime configurable so PRs run quickly while main branch retains strict, full-seed checks.

Problem statement
The current Monte Carlo guardrail is hard-coded (seed counts and win-rate thresholds) and runs as part of the full test suite. Large fixed runs slow PR feedback, increase CI cost, and prevent per-environment tuning of thresholds.

Users
- Developers making PRs to the repository: want fast, predictable CI feedback without expensive Monte Carlo runs on each PR.
- Release/maintainers running main branch checks: want strict, full-seed Monte Carlo runs to catch regressions before merging.

User stories
- As a contributor, I get fast PR feedback because the Monte Carlo guardrail uses a reduced seed count for PRs.
- As a maintainer, I ensure main branch runs the full Monte Carlo harness with stricter thresholds.
- As a developer running local checks, I can override seeds and thresholds via environment variables to reproduce CI conditions.

Success criteria
- Configurable via env vars: `MONTE_SEEDS`, `MONTE_MIN_WIN_RATE`, `MONTE_MAX_WIN_RATE` with sensible defaults.
- PR CI uses reduced seeds (default: 20) and main branch uses full seeds (default: 200); tests assert using the effective configuration.
- Deterministic behavior preserved: seed handling remains reproducible when seeds are provided.
- Documentation updated in `docs/main-street/*` and `DEVELOPER.md` describing the env vars and recommended PR vs main values.

Constraints

# Core Card Animations - Intake Brief

Implement core card animations (deal, move/place, discard) for Main Street and ensure animation helpers are reusable engine components.

## Users
- Players: Receive visual feedback for card actions (dealing cards, placing them on the street, discarding used cards), making gameplay easier to follow and more satisfying.
- Game developers: Reuse modular card animation helpers from the engine without reimplementing animation logic for each new game.

## User stories
- As a player, I want to see cards animate when they are dealt so I can easily track which card entered my hand.
- As a player, I want to see cards animate when placed on my street so I can confirm the action succeeded.
- As a player, I want to see cards animate when discarded so I understand they are no longer in play.
- As a developer, I want reusable animation helpers in the engine so I can add animations to any game with minimal code.

## Success criteria
1. Deal animation: When a card is added to the player's hand, a deal animation plays; GameEventEmitter fires a 'card:dealt' event on completion.
2. Move/place animation: When a card is placed on the street, a move animation plays; state transitions happen after animation completes; a 'card:placed' event fires.
3. Discard animation: When a card is discarded, a discard animation removes it visually; a 'card:discarded' event fires with the card ID.
4. Reusability: Animation helpers are in src/ui/ and exported via the engine's public API (src/ui/index.ts).
5. Testability: Unit tests or browser tests verify callbacks fire and state is correct after animations complete.
6. Documentation: Animation timings and usage examples are documented in docs/ or README.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Use existing GameEventEmitter (src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts) for event emissions - do not create new callback mechanisms.
- Follow animation timing guidelines in docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md (Section 4) but adjust as needed for good feel.
- Put animation helpers in src/ui/ (engine) not in example-games/.
- Keep engine and public APIs unchanged where possible; prefer extending over modifying existing interfaces.
- Accessibility: Animation should respect reduced-motion settings if present.

## Existing state
- Core engine provides moveGameObject.ts (positional tween helper) and flipCard.ts (card flip animation) in src/ui/.
- Main Street scene renders cards via refreshPlayerHand() in scenes/MainStreetScene.ts.
- Commands in MainStreetCommands.ts handle game actions but currently have no visual animation.
- GameEventEmitter exists in src/core-engine/ for event handling.

## Desired change
- Create card-specific animation helpers in src/ui/ (e.g., dealCard.ts, placeCard.ts, discardCard.ts) that:
  - Accept a Phaser scene and card sprite
  - Use appropriate easing and duration from UX guidelines
  - Emit events via GameEventEmitter on completion
  - Handle reduced-motion accessibility
- Integrate animations into Main Street scene command handlers
- Add tests for animation callbacks and state consistency
- Document animation helpers and timings

## Related work
- Parent: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY)
- Existing: src/ui/moveGameObject.ts - reusable positional tween helper (can be reused)
- Existing: src/ui/flipCard.ts - card flip animation (reference for card animations)
- Existing: src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts - event emission system to use
- Existing: docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md - animation timing guidelines
- Related: MainStreetScene.ts - where animations will be integrated

## Risks & assumptions
- **Risk**: Scope creep — temptation to add more animations (card flip, hover effects, etc.) beyond the three core animations.
  - **Mitigation**: If additional animations are needed, create separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding scope.
- **Risk**: Animation timing may not "feel right" on first implementation — requires iteration.
  - **Mitigation**: Use existing UX doc as starting point; allow implementer to adjust for good feel; document final timings.
- **Assumption**: GameEventEmitter is already integrated into the Main Street scene and can be used for event emission.

---

## Related work (automated report)
- **Parent**: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY) — Parent epic for M4; this item is a child task.
- **Prior art**: Add card/noble movement animations to SplendorScene (CG-0MM4RIKWT0EKGP0P) — Completed work for Splendor; likely similar implementation pattern.
- **Code reference**: src/ui/moveGameObject.ts — Reusable positional tween helper; used as foundation for deal/place animations.
- **Code reference**: src/ui/flipCard.ts — Card flip animation; reference for card-specific animation patterns.
- **Code reference**: src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts — Event emission system to use for animation callbacks.
- **Design doc**: docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md — Section 4 contains animation timing guidelines.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The acceptance criteria mentions callbacks - should these be event emissions that external code can subscribe to (using the existing GameEventEmitter), or should they be Promise-based awaitables, or both?" — Answer (user): "Use existing GameEventEmitter". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "For animation timings, should I follow the guidelines from docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md (Section 4: Animation and Juice) or use custom timings?" — Answer (user): "Follow the doc but feel free to adjust". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The deliverable mentions 'animation helpers in example-games/main-street/animations.ts' - is that the intended location, or would you prefer them in the scenes directory or exported from the engine?" — Answer (user): "From engine". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Problem statement

Event and scene transition animations (coin/reputation pop and simple enter/exit scene transitions) are missing or placeholder in Main Street. Players and QA need consistent, accessible, and testable animations to improve feedback and enable polished thumbnails and play sessions.

Users

- Players: receive clearer feedback when income/reputation changes and when scenes transition; improved perceived responsiveness and polish.
- QA/Producer: get reproducible visual behavior for playtests and thumbnail generation.
- Developers: need small, reusable animation helpers that are easy to test and toggleable (reduced motion, mute).

User stories

- As a player, I want a short "coin" or "reputation" pop animation when my resources change so I can immediately perceive the effect of economic actions.
- As a producer, I want scene enter/exit transitions so recorded replays and thumbnails do not show abrupt visual jumps.
- As a developer, I want small, well-documented animation helpers (pop, fade/slide transitions) that can be reused across scenes.

Success criteria

- A coin/reputation pop animation plays when income or reputation changes and completes within 1500ms without blocking game logic.
- Animations are implemented using SVG placeholder assets (if final art is not yet available) and accept final art formats without API changes.
- Unit or smoke tests verify animation trigger and completion (e.g., animation promise resolves or tween complete callback called) for both pop and transition animations.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Use SVG placeholders for art; final assets will be delivered later and must be swappable without code changes.
- Provide accessibility support: reduced-motion toggle must disable non-essential animations and transitions.
- Keep engine/public APIs unchanged; implement helpers as scene-level utilities or small engine adapters.
- Avoid heavy runtime allocations; animations should be lightweight and not degrade Monte Carlo or headless test runs.

Existing state

- Parent PRD M4 (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY) calls for event animations and transitions as part of visual polish.
- Some placeholder visuals and scripts for thumbnail generation exist (scripts/generate-thumbnail.ts); no formal animation helpers are present in the codebase for coin/reputation pops or scene transitions.
- Work item CG-0MO4LWX1T003I2LP currently exists with a short description and minimal acceptance criteria.

Desired change

- Implement two small, reusable animation helpers:
  1) popTextOrIcon(target, options): a compact pop + fade animation usable for coin/reputation changes and other small toasts.
  2) sceneTransition(scene, direction|type, options): simple enter/exit transitions (fade, slide) wired into scene lifecycle hooks.
- Wire pop helper into income and reputation change handlers so events trigger the animation without changing game logic flow.
- Add smoke/unit tests that run headlessly to assert that animations are triggered and complete (check callback or promise resolution), ensuring they don't hang headless runs.
- Document usage in docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md and add short README examples in the code folder.

Related work

- Parent: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY) — PRD that lists event animations, transition animations, accessibility requirements, and thumbnail pipeline; M4 is the parent milestone for this work.
- SVG Placeholder Assets (CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4) — existing work item that added SVG placeholders; relevant as an asset source for placeholders used by these animations.
- Core Card Animations (CG-0MO4LWWWC006HSNZ) — related animation helpers (deal/move/discard) that can provide patterns and reuse opportunities.
- docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md — visual and audio direction reference; includes animation timing guidance and accessibility notes.
- scripts/generate-thumbnail.ts — existing thumbnail tooling which benefits from smoother scene transitions for reproducible thumbnails.

Related work (automated report)

- CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY (Main Street: PRD Milestone 4) — Parent PRD: outlines event animations, transitions, reduced-motion accessibility, and thumbnail pipeline requirements. This intake should align with the M4 success criteria and use SVG placeholders where final assets are missing.
- CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4 (SVG Placeholder Assets) — Provides SVG placeholders used by early visual work; reuse these placeholders for pop and transition visuals to avoid blocking on final art.
- CG-0MO4LWWWC006HSNZ (Core Card Animations) — Existing animation implementations (deal/move/discard) that can be used as a template for implementation patterns and utility functions.
- docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md — Design guidance for animation timing, easing, and accessibility (reduced motion). Use timing targets (300–600ms for pops) from this document.
- scripts/generate-thumbnail.ts — Thumbnail generation tooling benefits from predictable transitions; ensure transitions are deterministic and can be disabled for headless thumbnail runs.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Are SVG placeholders acceptable for this work if final art is not available?" — Answer (agent inference + parent PRD): "Yes. Use SVG placeholders and ensure final assets can be swapped in without code changes." Source: parent PRD (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY). Final: yes.
- Q: "Should animations be disabled by default for headless runs and CI?" — Answer (agent inference): "Animations should either be no-op in headless test mode or expose hooks/promises that allow tests to wait for completion without rendering frames; provide a reduced-motion toggle and a headless-friendly flag." Source: existing project practice and Test constraints. Final: yes.
- No interactive clarifying questions were asked of the user during this intake.

Headline: Generate and integrate permissively-licensed SFX and a background loop for Main Street; wire them into SoundManager and expose mute/volume controls (CG-0MO4LWX76002HM2Q)

Problem statement

A small set of permissively-licensed sound effects (SFX) and a background loop are required for the Main Street game (Milestone 4). These assets should be generated or sourced, registered with the engine's SoundManager, wired to scene events, and exposed in the SettingsPanel as volume and mute controls so players can control audio.

Users

- Players of Main Street and other example games who expect audio feedback.
- Developers who need a reproducible asset generation pipeline and a stable audio API to write and test scene-level audio triggers.

Success criteria

- A minimal set of 5 short permissive SFX (deal, place, discard, coin-pop, click) plus one loop are present under public/assets/games/main-street/audio/ with licensing notes in public/assets/CREDITS.md.
- SoundManager is used (or extended) to register these SFX and scenes call SoundManager.play() via existing event-to-sound mappings.
- SettingsPanel exposes working mute toggle and volume slider that persist preferences and affect playback. Unit tests cover SoundManager behavior including mute and volume persistence and that muted prevents playback.
- All related documentation (CREDITS.md, docs/main-street/*.md, README snippets) updated to reflect the new assets and usage.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

Constraints

- Audio files must be permissively-licensed (CC0, MIT, or equivalent). If any file requires attribution, add entries to public/assets/CREDITS.md.
- Files should be added under public/assets/games/main-street/audio/ (create directories as needed) and kept small (individual SFX < 200KB where reasonable) to avoid large repo bloat.
- Implementation must reuse the existing SoundManager API (no breaking changes to its public contract). Scenes should register logical keys via SoundManager.register().
- Tests must mock the SoundPlayer contract; do not require integration-level audio playback in unit tests.
- Persistence of volume/mute should use the existing StorageLike/localStorage approach; handle missing storage gracefully (tests already assume this).
- Work must not change CI or publishing pipelines; any large media additions that would inflate the repo should be proposed as a separate follow-up work item.


Existing state

- The core engine already includes a Phaser-agnostic SoundManager (src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts) with volume/mute, persistence, and connectToEvents mapping.
- UI SettingsPanel (src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts) already implements mute toggle and volume slider wired to SoundManager.
- Tests exist for SoundManager and SettingsPanel and expect a SoundPlayer DI contract.
- Scripts for generating SFX (scripts/generate-sfx.mjs and variants) already exist and can be used as a starting point.

Desired change

- Source or generate the SFX (prefer CC0/MIT) and commit them to public/assets/games/main-street/audio/.
- Update CREDITS.md with licensing and attribution notes for any included audio files.
- Ensure scenes (MainStreetScene and relevant example scenes) preload and register the new SFX keys and map events to logical sound keys via SoundManager.register() and connectToEvents().
- Ensure SettingsPanel and SoundManager behavior remain consistent and covered by unit tests. Add tests to assert that playback does not occur when muted and that volume is persisted.

Related work

Potentially related docs:
- public/assets/CREDITS.md — asset attributions and current audio entries; update this file with any new attributions. (file path)
- docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md — Main Street audio direction, recommended SFX types and music mood. (file path)
- docs/the-build/engine-capabilities-audit.md — documents SoundManager and SettingsPanel contracts used by this work. (file path)

Potentially related work items:
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY) — parent milestone for this audio work; consider marking this item as a child if appropriate.
- Accessibility toggles & settings UI (CG-0MO4LWXCK007PDCC) — ensures audio controls are exposed and persistent for accessibility.
- Source CC0 audio assets (CG-0MLUGZZIR1YA0GTL) — prior work that sourced CC0 audio; reuse approach and sources.

# Intake Draft: Unify card dimensions across UI (CG-0MO4NFMY4005DK66)

Problem statement

Currently different UI areas use different card aspect ratios and pixel sizes (for example: canonical art 140×190px portrait, market card slot 140×80 landscape, street slot 105×110 square). This causes inconsistent visual scale, asset duplication, and makes it hard for developers and QA to author and validate placeholder art. We need a small scoped initiative to standardise the canonical card dimensions, define rules for derived thumbnails, and provide a migration plan so scenes render consistently without visual distortion.

Users

- Developers building or replacing art assets for example games (Main Street, The Mind, Lost Cities).
- QA engineers running headless/browser tests that assert scene preload and visual layout.
- Designers who need clear guidance on which asset sizes to provide.

Example user stories

- As a developer, I want a single canonical card art size so I can author SVGs once and derive thumbnails programmatically.
- As QA, I want scenes to render without stretched or squashed cards so tests and screenshots reliably reflect intended visuals.
- As a designer, I want the asset spec documented so exported art matches engine expectations.

Success criteria

- A canonical card art orientation and pixel size is chosen and documented (recommended: portrait 140×190) in the work item.
- Mapping of existing UI slots (market, street, queue, hand) to derived thumbnail sizes or aspect-preserving rendering rules is documented.
- A small prototype is committed that: loads the canonical SVG, renders it into market and street slots without visual distortion (preserve aspect ratio), and includes unit/browser tests that validate preload and presence of textures.
- A child work item is created under CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4 to convert street layout adjacency rules to a grid (distance-based adjacency) and linked to the parent asset pipeline item.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs (docs/main-street/*).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Keep the initial scope small: pick a canonical orientation and produce a migration/proposal + small prototype. Full UI refactor or sweeping game-rule changes are out-of-scope for this item.
- Prefer non-destructive changes: initial UI behaviour should be preserved unless explicitly changed by child work items.
- Use permissively-licensed or in-repo authored placeholder SVGs only.
- Do not commit large raster assets; prefer SVGs and small, derived thumbnails to avoid CI bloat.

Existing state

- Canonical card generation scripts (scripts/generate-mind-cards.ts) use 140×190px as a source art size for The Mind cards.
- Scenes and UI constants currently use a mix of sizes: example-games/main-street uses MARKET_CARD_W = 140, MARKET_CARD_H = 80; SLOT_W = 105, SLOT_H = 110. Shared runtime defaults (src/ui/constants.ts) set small runtime CARD_W = 48, CARD_H = 65 used for layout helpers.
- An in-progress work item for SVG Placeholder Assets exists: CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4.

Desired change

- Decide on a canonical in-repo card art size (portrait 140×190 recommended) and document the choice.
- Define a mapping table that lists each UI slot type (market card, street slot, incident queue, hand) and the recommended handling: either a derived thumbnail size or an aspect-preserving rendering rule (fit-inside vs fill-and-crop).
- Implement a small prototype change in MainStreetScene (or shared helper) to load a canonical SVG and render it into market and street slots while preserving aspect ratio, plus tests to assert textures are preloaded and display sizes are applied.
- Create a child work item to implement a grid-based street adjacency system (distance-based adjacency) and link it to parent CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4. The child should be scoped for design + implementation and have its own acceptance criteria.
- Update docs: docs/main-street/* and public/assets/CREDITS.md with asset guidance and regeneration notes.

UI / Responsiveness decision

- Target responsive layouts, with 1280×720 (desktop) as the primary reference resolution. Implement layout rules that adapt to narrower viewports, but ensure the desktop layout reproduces the intended spacing and sizing at 1280×720.

Related work

Potentially related docs:
- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-1.md — PRD with asset expectations for Main Street.
- scripts/generate-mind-cards.ts — example generator that uses 140×190 source size.
- docs/DEVELOPER.md — asset placement and guidelines.

Potentially related work items:
- SVG Placeholder Assets (CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4) — parent asset work item (in-progress).
- Card Asset Pipeline (CG-0MLSPHIDD19PBDOZ) — pipeline and card asset standardization.
- Minimal Responsive UI (Walking Skeleton) (CG-0MM7IABRS0YJ6M3N) — earlier UI layout guidance.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Scope creep if the item attempts a full UI refactor. Mitigation: limit this item to proposal + small prototype; create follow-up work items for bulk changes.
- Risk: Visual regressions in other example games when switching rendering helpers. Mitigation: keep changes in shared helper functions guarded and add tests to catch regressions.
- Assumption: Existing canonical art (140×190) is acceptable as the single source of truth and thumbnails can be derived programmatically.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Canonical card orientation: portrait (140×190) or landscape?" — Answer (user): "Keep portrait 140x190 as recommended." Source: user reply. Final: portrait 140×190.
- Q: "Street layout behaviour: make street two rows of 5 cards — visual-only or should adjacency rules change?" — Answer (user): "For now keep synergy rules the same. However, create a child work item under CG-0MO4LWWK90006QB4 that will modify the rules to create a grid system for cards in which synergy rules use distance between cells." Source: user reply. Final: visual-only for this item; child work item created for adjacency rule change.
- Q: "UI constraints / responsiveness: desktop-only or responsive mobile?" — Answer (user): "Responsive with 1280x720 as the target resolution." Source: user reply. Final: responsive with 1280x720 primary reference.

Draft notes

- The immediate goal is to standardise asset expectations and provide a safe, incremental migration path that preserves game behaviour. The grid-adjacency rules are intentionally delegated to a child work item to keep this item small and actionable.

Problem statement

Main Street currently stores street cards in a 10-slot array but adjacency/synergy still behaves like a linear strip. The scene now renders a 2x5 board, so adjacency should be distance-based on that grid.

Users

- Players: expect nearby cards on the 2x5 board to synergize consistently with visual layout.
- Designers/QA: need deterministic, testable adjacency that matches board geometry.
- Developers: need reusable mapping helpers from slot index to grid cell and distance-based neighbor calculation.

Success criteria

1. Adjacency uses 2x5 grid coordinates (5 columns x 2 rows) instead of linear neighbors.
2. Default synergy range (range=1) counts orthogonal neighbors by Manhattan distance (up/down/left/right), no diagonals.
3. Extended range from upgrades (`synergyRangeBonus`) expands Manhattan radius correctly.
4. Existing APIs remain stable for callers (`neighbors`, `computeSynergyBonus`, `computeBusinessIncome`, `computeIncome`, `applyIncome`).
5. Unit tests cover edge/corner/middle cells, range extension, and asymmetry when only one business has upgraded range.
6. Main Street regression suite passes (`npm test` and `npm run build`).
7. Documentation explains the grid-distance adjacency model and migration notes for future balancing.

Constraints

- Keep the `streetGrid` storage shape as a 10-slot array for compatibility.
- Preserve deterministic behavior and avoid randomization changes.
- Do not introduce breaking changes to scene or transcript formats.

Implementation approach

- Implement index<->cell mapping helpers inside `MainStreetAdjacency.ts`.
- Recompute `neighbors(index, range)` from Manhattan distance over 2x5 coordinates.
- Update adjacency tests in `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts` to match the new geometry.
- Update docs (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-4.md`) with the grid-distance rule.

Related work

- Parent milestone: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY)
- Discovered from: Unify card dimensions across UI (CG-0MO4NFMY4005DK66)

# Intake Draft: Main Street layout update for canonical card sizes and 2x5 street (CG-0MO4SXRMY007LEA9)

## Problem statement
Main Street's current screen layout does not reliably use the defined card sizing guidance while also accommodating the full 10-slot street in a readable layout. We need a responsive UI re-layout that keeps gameplay rules unchanged, uses canonical card sizing rules, and displays the street as 2 rows of 5 without overlap.

## Users
- Players of Main Street on desktop and narrower viewports.
- Developers maintaining `MainStreetScene` layout constants and rendering behavior.
- QA validating layout stability and visual non-overlap.

Example user stories:
- As a player, I want all major play zones visible and readable without overlapping elements so that turns are easy to understand.
- As a player, I want the street shown as 2x5 so card placement is easier to scan.
- As a developer, I want layout rules aligned to defined card-size guidance so future UI updates stay consistent.

## Success criteria
- Street grid renders as exactly 2 rows of 5 slots (10 total) in Main Street at runtime.
- Layout changes remain UI-only: no rule or adjacency mechanic changes are introduced.
- Action controls in the bottom-right are compacted enough to move the player hand area to the bottom and create vertical space for lower sections.
- The full Main Street layout is responsive (desktop + narrow/mobile) with no overlapping of major zones (market, incident queue, street, hand, action area, instruction text).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must keep Main Street game rules unchanged for this item (layout-only scope).
- Must use the defined card dimension guidance (canonical portrait card size and aspect-preserving rendering behavior from docs).
- Street must remain 10 total slots and be rendered as 2x5 (user-confirmed after typo clarification).

## Desired change
- Refactor Main Street scene layout constants/placement logic so the street is displayed as 2 rows of 5 slots.

Headline

Ensure purchased investment events animate into and materialize in the left-hand held-event slot and remain fully visible across desktop and narrow/mobile viewports.

Problem statement

When the player purchases an investment (held event) in Main Street, the purchased card sometimes appears on the right side of the screen and may render outside the visible viewport. It should instead materialize in the dedicated held-event slot on the left side of the screen (where the "No held event" label appears), and remain within visible bounds across responsive breakpoints.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Fixing layout might inadvertently change interactive hit areas or conflict with svgDom vs canvas rendering. Mitigation: keep changes limited to coordinate calculation and container anchoring; add unit tests to cover computeLayout/getHandCardCenter behaviors.
- Risk: Headless/browser tests may flake if animations rely on wall-clock timing. Mitigation: use promise-based transfer completion hooks (tween onComplete) or short-circuit animations in headless mode and assert completion via resolved promises.
- Risk: Scope creep — deeper UI refactors may be tempting. Mitigation: record further improvements as separate follow-up work items and keep this item focused on placement/animation destination and tests.
- Assumption: The game logic that chooses which card becomes the held-event is correct and must not be changed by this work. If that assumption is false, the agent will record an open question.

Users

- Players: receive clear, consistent feedback when buying investment events and avoid seeing UI elements rendered offscreen.
- QA/Producers: get reproducible visual behavior for automated browser tests and thumbnail generation.
- Developers: need a small, well-scoped fix to layout/placement logic so transfer animations and final materialization target the correct hand coordinates without changing game logic.

User stories

- As a player, when I buy an investment event it should animate into the held-event slot on the left and appear there after the transfer completes.
- As a QA engineer, I want an automated browser test that buys an investment and asserts the event only appears in the hand after the transfer animation completes and is within viewport bounds.
- As a developer, I want clear, minimal changes that correct hand placement and include unit/browser tests so the fix is maintainable.

Success criteria

1. When a player purchases an investment event, the transfer animation targets the left hand slot (getHandCardCenter()) and the state.heldEvent is materialized only after the transfer completes; automated browser tests assert this.
2. The held-event card is always fully within the visible viewport bounds for the supported responsive breakpoints (desktop and narrow/mobile). Automated tests verify positions at desktop (1280x720) and a narrow/mobile dimension (900x1100 or similar).
3. Unit tests cover position computation (getHandCardCenter(), drawHeldEventCard() behaviour) for representative layout metrics.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (code comments and example-games/main-street/scenes/README.md or docs where applicable).
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Do not change game logic that determines which card becomes the held-event; only change the UI placement/animation target and related rendering logic.
- Keep the fix lightweight and deterministic (avoid adding heavy runtime allocations or non-deterministic layout strategies that could break headless tests).
- Respect existing reduced-motion and headless test flags: animations can be skipped or short-circuited in headless test environments, but the test must still be able to verify transfer completion via promises or tween callbacks.
- Preserve compatibility with DOM-based SVG rendering (svgDom) and the canvas fallback path.

Existing state

- The MainStreetScene computes layout metrics (computeLayout()) and exposes getHandCardCenter(), drawHeldEventCard(), and requestCardTexture()/svgDom usage. The animateTransferFromMarket() helper currently uses getHandCardCenter() as the destination for event purchases.
- Tests: tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts already contains transfer animation assertions (materialization after ~1700ms) that can be extended or used as a template.
- Current observed bug: purchased events are rendered on the right side of the screen and may spill offscreen in some viewports.

Desired change

- Verify and, if necessary, fix the following code paths so the transfer destination and final rendering use the left hand slot coordinates:
  - getHandCardCenter(): confirm it returns the left hand slot coordinates for all breakpoints.
  - drawHeldEventCard(): ensure container position/anchor aligns the held card to the left slot and respects displayWidth/displayHeight.
  - Any responsive layout offsets or container parenting that could cause the held card to be positioned relative to an unexpected origin (e.g., wrong container x/y) should be corrected.

  - Browser test that purchases an investment, asserts state.heldEvent is null until transfer completes, asserts the held card's on-screen position is within viewport bounds after completion (desktop and narrow mobile). Use existing MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts patterns.
  - Unit tests for getHandCardCenter() and drawHeldEventCard() outputs given mock layout metrics.
- Update docs/README or inline code comments to document the hand slot coordinates and responsive behaviour.

Related work (automated report)

Relevant functions: computeLayout(), getHandCardCenter(), drawHeldEventCard(), and animateTransferFromMarket() which determine where transfer animations target and where the held-event ultimately appears.
