Headline summary

Fix the test workflow so it no longer mutates or removes tracked Main Street SVG source assets under `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards`. The change should remove the destructive behavior at its source and preserve normal test/build validation.

## Problem statement

Running `npm test` currently invokes a `pretest` command that writes to the Main Street SVG source tree, which has previously led to tracked card SVG asset loss in the working tree. Test workflows must not mutate tracked source assets.

## Users

- Developers running local test workflows need test commands to be safe and non-destructive.
- Maintainers/reviewers need confidence that validation commands do not damage source-controlled assets.
- Main Street feature teams need stable card SVG source files for rendering and animation work.

User stories

- As a developer, I want to run `npm test` without risking deletion or mutation of tracked assets.
- As a maintainer, I want test scripts to operate only on safe paths so source files are never unintentionally touched.
- As a Main Street contributor, I want SVG source assets to remain stable across test/build runs.

## Success criteria

1. The specific destructive path is identified and documented: `package.json` `pretest` currently runs `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree public/assets/games/main-street/svg || true`.
2. Test workflow scripts are changed so running `npm test` does not target or mutate tracked source SVG directories used for Main Street card assets.
3. `npm test` completes successfully after the fix with no tracked changes under `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards` attributable to the test workflow.
4. `npm run build` completes successfully after the fix.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to fixing the current destructive behavior for Main Street SVG assets (no broad cross-project guardrail expansion in this item).
- Keep the existing developer workflow simple; avoid introducing unnecessary new checks per user direction.
- Preserve compatibility with existing Main Street asset generation and loading paths.

## Existing state

- `package.json` defines `pretest` as `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree public/assets/games/main-street/svg || true`.
- Main Street generated SVG cards are written under `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards` by `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- A prior recovery item, `Restore deleted main-street SVG card assets (CG-0MOALGGK7008UINX)`, restored removed assets after an earlier incident.

## Desired change

- Remove or replace the script behavior that writes to the tracked Main Street SVG source path during test setup.
- Ensure test-time cleanup/restoration (if still needed) operates only on safe, non-source, generated/transient paths.
- Update docs to clearly distinguish source asset directories from generated/transient outputs involved in workflows.

Scope change: Use ToneForge (tf) outputs directly — do NOT implement synthesis internals in this repo.

Updated Goal:
- Remove runtime sound synthesis implementation from the repository. Instead, call into ToneForge-generated code/artifacts (the same API surface the tf CLI produces) at runtime. The project will rely on tf for all synthesis features; this repo acts as a thin integration layer only.

What to do (updated acceptance criteria):
1) Remove or avoid adding any engine-internal synthesis implementation (no SynthPlayer or bespoke Tone.js synthesis code).
2) Add a small runtime integration adapter that delegates to the tf-generated module exported by the ToneForge CLI. This adapter should only:
   - import (or dynamically load) the tf-generated JS module produced by the tf CLI,
   - provide thin mapping from logical sound keys to tf factory names/descriptors, and
   - expose simple play/stop/setVolume/setMute delegations to the tf module (no synth logic).
3) Include a package.json script (scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh or npm run tf:generate) and docs describing how to run the tf CLI to regenerate the synth module (docs/the-build/audio.md).
4) Update SoundManager to accept synth-mapped keys that call the integration adapter which in turn calls tf exports. The SoundManager should not replicate synthesis logic.
5) Remove any previously-added synthesis prototype code from the repo (if present) or mark it for deletion.
6) Add example wiring in MainStreetScene to call the tf-backed adapter (ms-move-loop, ms-place, etc.) and document the expected tf export names.
7) Keep all existing WAV asset playback functionality intact as a fallback.

Notes / constraints:
- The tf-generated module format/version determines the adapter implementation; the spike must inspect tf output and adapt the thin adapter accordingly.
- The project must include clear developer docs for installing the tf CLI (global or project-local) and for regenerating synths.
- We will not check in or duplicate ToneForge synthesis code; only the tf-generated JS module (if required by build policy) or a small shim that imports it. Prefer keeping the generated module out of source control if team policy prefers artifacts be generated as part of the build; provide script and instructions either way.

Risk: external tooling dependency (tf) and runtime dependency on Tone.js. Mitigation: clearly document install/run steps and fallback to WAV assets when tf/Tone.js is not available.

Estimated effort: spike 0.5-1 day to implement the thin adapter + docs; full integration 2-3 days to wire examples and tests after confirming tf export format.

Problem statement

Clicking market cards currently opens action menus but does not leave a persistent visual selection state; players can lose track of which card they selected when the modal is open or after brief interactions. This causes confusion and reduces discoverability of click-to-act behaviour.

Users

- Primary: Players of Feudalism and other example games that use a market UI.
  - As a player, when I click a market card I want a clear persistent visual indicator so I can tell which card I selected while the action modal is open or until I cancel.
- Secondary: QA and playtesters who need reliable visual feedback during testing.

Success criteria

- A visible, persistent selection marker is applied to a clicked market card across all scenes that render clickable card containers (feudalism, main-street, and other market-like UIs).
- The selection visual is a green 2px stroke outline plus a slight scale-up (approx. 1.04x) that is distinct from the existing hover state (yellow stroke + scale). The hover state remains yellow and functions as before.
- The selection clears when the player clicks any non-card area (including background, UI buttons, or other containers) or when the scene closes the action modal; clicking a different card moves selection to that card.
- Automated UI/browser tests validate selection persistence: at least one browser test asserts that after pointerdown on a market card the DOM/scene shows the selection outline and that it clears on a non-card click.
- All related documentation (code comments, README, relevant game docs) is updated. Full project test suite passes with new changes.

Constraints

- Visual change must be implemented conservatively using existing rendering APIs (Phaser GameObjects: rectangle stroke style, container scaling, or tint) so it has minimal cross-scene impact.
- Avoid coupling selection logic to a single scene; implement a small reusable helper (UI utility) that can be consumed by market renderers.
- Do not change persisted game state or turn logic; this is a purely UI/UX enhancement.
- Keep behaviour consistent with existing input handling (preserve current pointerover/pointerout animations and event ordering).

Existing state

- FeudalismScene.createMarketCard() makes each card's background rectangle interactive and responds to pointerdown/pointerover/pointerout. Hover shows strokeStyle(2, 0xffdd44) and container scale(1.05).
- MainStreet and other games render market-like UIs with similar patterns (market containers, deck backs, flying-card animations).
- BeleagueredCastleScene implements click-to-move selection using a SELECTION_TINT, showValidDropHighlights(), selectColumn()/deselectColumn() and emits 'card-selected'/'card-deselected' events — a good precedent for selection visuals and event practices.
- GameEventEmitter includes event types for 'card-selected' and 'card-deselected' that can be used if telemetry/events are desired.

Desired change

- Add a small, reusable UI selection helper (e.g., ui/selection.ts or src/ui/selection.ts) that provides an API to attach a persistent selection state to a Phaser container or GameObject.
  - API: attachSelection(container: Phaser.GameObjects.Container | Phaser.GameObjects.GameObject, options?) -> returns controller with select()/deselect()/isSelected(); optionally emits events or calls callbacks.
- Update FeudalismScene.createMarketCard() to attach the selection helper to the card container and set pointerdown to toggle/select using the helper instead of only opening the action menu.
- Ensure hover styling remains unchanged; selected state applies green 2px stroke + scale(1.04).
- Wire selection clear on global pointerdown for non-card areas (scene.input.on('pointerdown', ...)) using the helper so clicks anywhere not hitting a selected card will deselect.
- Apply the same helper in other market-like scenes (MainStreetScene, any other scenes with createMarketCard-style renderers) to get consistent UX.

Related work

- example-games/feudalism/scenes/FeudalismScene.ts — Market rendering and card interactivity. (Used to find createMarketCard, refreshMarket, onMarketCardClick handlers.)
- example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts — Click-to-move selection implementation and selection tint constants. (Used as precedent for selection visuals and event usage.)
- src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts — Defines 'card-selected'/'card-deselected' events and payload shapes. (Reference for event naming and telemetry.)
- Worklog: Highlight for selected card (CG-0MOJ44AXO006HFAS) — existing work item; updated to intake/in-progress prior to drafting.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope — which scenes should get this selection highlight?" — Answer (user): "C" (All scenes that show clickable cards). Agent research/evidence: Reviewed FeudalismScene.ts and other market usages (MainStreet scene tests and market helpers). Final: yes.
- Q: "Visual treatment — how should a selected market card look?" — Answer (user): "B" (Add a green stroke outline (2px) + slight scale up (1.04); keep hover yellow). Agent inference/evidence: Matched to existing hover styles in FeudalismScene.ts and selection precedent in BeleagueredCastleScene.ts. Final: yes.
- Q: "Selection lifetime / behavior — when should the highlight be cleared?" — Answer (user): "C" (Clear on any non-card click). Agent inference/evidence: Will implement scene-level pointerdown handler to clear selection when click target is not a market card. Final: yes.

Implementation notes / suggested tasks (non-exhaustive)

- Implement src/ui/selection.ts with minimal Phaser-agnostic helpers.
- Update FeudalismScene.createMarketCard() to attach selection controller and update pointerdown flow: select then open action menu; selection persists until deselected.
- Add small unit/browser test: MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts or a FeudalismScene browser test to assert selection appears and clears on non-card click.
- Update code comments and docs where market card rendering is described.

Headline

Add a Difficulty selector to the Settings panel that lists the engine DifficultyPresets (Easy/Medium/Hard), persists the player's preference across sessions, and applies to newly started games only.

Problem statement

Players can currently select Main Street difficulty from the Game Over screen but cannot set it from the Settings panel. We need a SettingsPanel difficulty selector so players can set (and persist) their preferred difficulty outside the Game Over flow.

Users

- Players (casual and returning): want to set a preferred difficulty before starting a game.
- Designers / QA: need an easily-accessible UI to test runs at different difficulty presets.
- Engine developers: need a simple, reusable API-level mechanism so games can read the selected difficulty from a shared settings store.

Example user stories

- As a player, I can choose Easy/Medium/Hard from the Settings panel so that new games start at my preferred difficulty.
- As a designer, I can change the difficulty in Settings and run a new game to validate balance quickly.

Success criteria

- The Settings panel displays a difficulty selector with the same difficulty names used by DifficultyPresets (Easy, Medium, Hard).
- Changing difficulty in Settings persists across browser sessions and affects subsequently started games.
- Changing difficulty shows a short tooltip: "Difficulty applies to new games only" and does not modify an in-progress game.
- Unit tests cover the SettingsPanel difficulty UI and the mapping to the engine DifficultyPresets API, including persistence behaviour.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (code comments, README, relevant docs).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- The change should reuse the existing DifficultyPresets API and the SettingsPanel/SettingsButton UI rather than introducing a new settings subsystem.
- Difficulty changes must be safe for games that read difficulty at startup; do not attempt to mutate an active game state mid-run.
- Persisted settings should be stored using the same persistence mechanism used by SettingsPanel (localStorage or existing settings store) to avoid duplicating state layers.
- Keep the UI compact — a single-line selector or segmented control is preferred to avoid major layout changes.

Existing state

- SettingsPanel exists at src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts and presently handles mute/volume and reduced motion. It is created by CardGameScene via initSettingsPanel().
- DifficultyPresets generic API exists under src/core-engine/DifficultyPresets.ts and Main Street presets are defined at example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts.
- Example scenes (e.g., example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts) currently read selectedDifficulty when setting up a new game and default to 'Medium'.
- There are tests asserting difficulty preset names and behaviour (tests/main-street/difficulty-presets.test.ts).

Desired change

- Add a difficulty selector control to SettingsPanel that lists available difficulty names from the DifficultyPresets registry.
- Hook the selector to the existing settings persistence mechanism and expose a getter that engine/game setup code can read when creating a new game.
- Add unit tests for the SettingsPanel integration and update example game scenes or setup code to read the persisted preference when starting games.
- Update documentation and any relevant tests to reflect the new behaviour.

Related work

- CG-0MOJ5CPYP001IGD8 — Add difficulty setting to settings page (this item; updated to stage=idea, status=in-progress)
- CG-0MMJ8S87N06Q5GP1 — Difficulty Presets (Easy/Medium/Hard) — completed: Engine-level generic presets API extraction.
- CG-0MMJ9O4K403TOIWA — Tests: Difficulty Presets — completed: tests validating preset names and lookup behaviour.
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts — concrete Main Street presets and DIFFICULTY_NAMES list.
- src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts — existing SettingsPanel implementation to be updated.
- src/ui/SettingsButton.ts — settings toggle button.
- tests/ui/SettingsPanel.test.ts — unit tests for SettingsPanel; update to include difficulty selector tests.

Find-related report

The repository and worklog search found additional related items that may inform implementation or testing:
- CG-0MO4LWXCK007PDCC — Accessibility toggles & settings UI (open): overlaps in accessibility-related settings and toggles that SettingsPanel must co-exist with.
- CG-0MLUH07HP1QKGS1Y — Settings Panel with mute toggle and volume slider (completed): historical work adding settings features; useful for persistence API pattern.
- CG-0MM041HC70G1UFSH — Fix top-line UI overlap with menu button and settings/help icons (completed): contains UI layout fixes to avoid overlap with SettingsButton.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Settings persistence mechanism differs between example games; mitigation: reuse SettingsPanel's existing persistence API and add an adapter if needed.
- Risk: UI layout regresses on small screens; mitigation: use a compact control and test in scenes that include the SettingsPanel.
- Risk: Changing difficulty mid-run could cause confusing behaviour if applied incorrectly; mitigation: make selector apply only to new games and show an explanatory tooltip.
- Assumption: DifficultyPresets registry is stable and exposes the canonical set of names (Easy/Medium/Hard) for all example games.
- Scope creep mitigation: Any additional features (per-game overrides, dynamic mid-run difficulty) discovered during implementation will be recorded as separate work items instead of expanding this item.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the SettingsPanel difficulty selector be: A) Global (applies to all example games using DifficultyPresets), B) Per-game, C) Game-selector-level?" — Answer (user): "A" (Global). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should the selected difficulty be persisted across sessions (localStorage / saved settings)?" — Answer (user): "Yes". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Which of the following should be true when changing difficulty in SettingsPanel? Apply immediately to newly started games only; Update any open game in-progress; Show a tooltip/confirmation that the change affects new games only." — Answer (user): "Apply immediately, show a tooltip" (i.e., changes apply to new games only and UI shows tooltip). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Notes / evidence

- Search of repository shows SettingsPanel at src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts and DifficultyPresets at src/core-engine/DifficultyPresets.ts. Example usage in example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts and scene initialization in example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts.

Problem statement

Double the number of distinct card types available in the Main Street card catalog to increase gameplay variety and support richer deck-building and meta-progression choices. Use the PRD Appendix A and the existing card catalog as the source of truth for current content and design constraints.

Users

- Players: benefit from increased variety, replayability, and new strategic choices.
- Game designers: need a larger card pool to design varied scenarios and progression.
- QA / Playtesters: require deterministic smoke tests and balance checks to validate new cards.

Example user stories

- As a player, I want more unique cards so that successive runs feel different and present new strategies.
- As a designer, I want at least twice the number of card types to enable more distinct archetypes and synergies.
- As a tester, I want automated deck-generation and balance smoke tests to detect regressions introduced by new cards.

Success criteria

- The total number of distinct card types in the Main Street catalog is increased to at least 2× the current count (i.e., >= 2 * current_count). (Measurable: compare counts in docs/main-street/card-catalog.md before/after.)
- New cards are integrated into runtime deck/market generation and appear in game runs without code changes to deck-loading logic.
- Automated tests added/updated: unit tests for card registration and deck generation, plus at least one balance smoke test (monte-carlo or similar) that runs successfully in CI locally. (Measurable: new/updated tests in tests/main-street/ and green CI/local runs.)
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including docs/main-street/card-catalog.md, PRD Appendix A (if applicable), code comments, and README entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Scope limited to the Main Street card catalog (docs/main-street/). Changes should not proactively expand other example-games unless explicitly requested.
- Use existing programmatic asset pipeline (generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs) and SVG templates for new cards; no finalized artist assets are required to complete this work.
- Maintain backwards-compatible card API and deck-loading interfaces; avoid breaking changes to existing gameplay unless necessary and justified.
- Keep churn manageable: prefer programmatic creation and template reuse over bespoke per-card art or bespoke code for each card.

Existing state

- The current Main Street card catalog and tiers are documented in docs/main-street/card-catalog.md and PRD Appendix A in docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md.
- Repo contains tooling and examples: generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs, card-system module, SVG templates, and supporting tests.
- Relevant prior work items and design documents exist (see Related work).

Desired change

- Add a set of new card definitions (data-driven JSON/TS entries) sufficient to double the distinct card count.
- Extend the card-generator templates and run the SVG generator to produce placeholder art for new cards.
- Update deck/market generation to include new cards where appropriate, and add playtest/balance smoke tests.
- Update docs and PRD references to include the new cards and any adjustments to numbers.

Related work

- docs/main-street/card-catalog.md — Main Street: Card Catalog (current catalog and tiering). Path: docs/main-street/card-catalog.md
- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md — PRD Milestone 2 (includes Appendix A: Card Catalog by Tier). Path: docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md

Headline

Deliver Main Street Milestone 5: implement tutorial/onboarding, Game Selector integration, Help/Rules panel, and onboarding flow described in docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md. Optional statistics tracking decision deferred (OPEN QUESTION).

---

Problem statement

Main Street lacks a first-time player onboarding experience integrated with the shared Game Selector, persistent tutorial state, and an always-available Help/Rules panel. This gap increases onboarding friction for new players and makes it difficult for them to learn the core loop without external documentation.

Users

- New players: need a guided, action-gated tutorial to learn core mechanics (example story: "As a new player, I want a guided first run so I can learn the game in <15 minutes").
- Returning players: need replayable tutorial and Help panel to refresh mechanics.
- Producers/QA: need deterministic tutorial state for automated tests and scene integration.

Success criteria

- SC-1: On first launch the app shows a tutorial offer modal with Start/Skip and Start begins the scripted tutorial (AC-1.1..AC-1.5 from PRD).
- SC-2: Tutorial progression enforces action gates per the script and persists a completion flag to local storage; replayable from menu.
- SC-3: Main Street appears in the Game Selector with correct metadata and launches MainStreetScene; returning to selector preserves registry state.
- SC-4: Help/Rules panel accessible during gameplay with required sections and <=8 lines per section.
- SC-5: Full project test suite passes; specific tutorial, selector integration, and persistence tests are added and green.
- SC-6: Documentation updated: code comments, README, and docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md reflect final behaviour.

Constraints

- Implement using existing shared Game Selector and save/load conventions (localStorage keys suggested in PRD).
- Tutorial must be disable-able for replay/test harness via explicit config flag.
- Keep copy in English only for this milestone; accessibility: respect reduced-motion, 1280x720 and narrow view layouts, keyboard/controller nav.
- Do not change core game mechanics or card economy in this milestone.

Existing state

- PRD exists at docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md and defines tutorial script, states, schemas, and acceptance criteria.
- Related work includes prior Main Street milestones (milestone 1-4), Game Selector and shared renderer components, and existing tests that reference Main Street scenes.

Desired change

Decision on optional statistics tracking is deferred and documented as an open question.

data.description:
Implement and extract top-priority engine components from Main Street into shared engine modules (P1: MarketOfferEngine, EconomyLedger, ActionCommands). This work item will include full implementation, tests, migration updates, and documentation; the developer may determine the exact subset and implementation sequencing but must document selection decisions and create follow-up work items for any deferred components.

Problem statement

Main Street contains valuable, reusable gameplay systems implemented inside example-games/main-street. These systems should be extracted into shared engine modules under src/* with well-defined TypeScript public APIs, unit and integration tests, and migration notes so future games can reuse them without copying game-specific code.

Users

- Engine architects and maintainers: need reusable, well-documented components to reduce duplication across games.
- Game developers: want stable APIs and examples so they can adopt engine components with minimal friction.
- QA and Producers: need migration plans and tests to ensure refactors do not regress Main Street behavior.

User stories

- As an engine architect, I want Main Street’s proven gameplay components extracted into engine modules so I can reuse them in later games.
- As a game developer, I want TypeScript interfaces and example code so I can adopt extracted components quickly.
- As QA, I want unit and integration tests plus a migration checklist so regressions are caught before merges.

Acceptance Criteria (Success Criteria)

1. Implementation: The top-priority P1 components (MarketOfferEngine, EconomyLedger, ActionCommands) are extracted into src/* with exported TypeScript public APIs, usage examples, and unit tests. If the implementer chooses a subset, the PR must include a short decision note listing which P1 components were implemented, which were deferred, and a created follow-up work item for each deferred component.

2. Integration: example-games/main-street is updated to consume the extracted components (imports only). The game behavior is preserved as validated by integration tests or end-to-end smoke checks comparing key game flows.

3. Tests & validation: Unit tests exist for each extracted component covering core behaviors (buy/refill for MarketOfferEngine, resource delta and ledger invariants for EconomyLedger, command do/undo semantics for ActionCommands). The work branch passes: npm run build and npm test locally; the PR contains test run logs or CI-green evidence.

4. Documentation & migration: A migration.md or README section is included documenting file moves, public API usage examples, migration steps for Main Street, and any deprecation notes. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

5. Quality gates: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. Lint/TypeScript strictness (tsc) must be preserved; no new TypeScript errors may be introduced.

Constraints

- Preserve external behavior of Main Street; breaking changes must be minimized and clearly documented with migration notes.
- Maintain TypeScript strictness and existing path aliases.
- Any API-breaking changes must include deprecation guidance and migration steps.
- Licenses for assets and third-party code must remain permissive (MIT/Apache/CC0).
- Follow repository workflow: implement on a feature branch, run build → test → commit, push to dev as described in AGENTS.md.

Existing state

- PRD and design work for Milestone 6 exist at docs/main-street/prd-milestone-6.md (component inventory, API drafts, migration plan sketches).
- Candidate source files in example-games/main-street/: MainStreetMarket.ts, MainStreetEngine.ts, MainStreetCommands.ts, MainStreetHint.ts, MainStreetSaveLoad.ts, MainStreetTranscript.ts, MainStreetAdjacency.ts.
- Reusable foundations already in repo: src/core-engine/SpatialRules.ts, TranscriptRecorderBase, UndoRedoManager, SaveLoad/TranscriptStore, and UI helpers under src/ui/.

Desired change

- Extract and implement the P1 engine components into src/ (MarketOfferEngine, EconomyLedger, ActionCommands) with TypeScript public APIs, unit tests, and documentation. Update example-games/main-street to import and use these modules without behavioral changes. Create follow-up work items for any deferred extractions (P2/P3).

Related work (manual & automated seeds)

- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-6.md — PRD: component inventory, TypeScript API drafts, migration plan, verification checklist (seed for this work).
- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md — AI / Hint / Undo system and transcript hooks referenced by Milestone 6.
- docs/core-engine/spatial-rules.md — existing spatial/grid primitives to re-use rather than re-implement.
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts — Market engine (extraction candidate P1).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts — Core game logic (contains economy and orchestration code; candidate for refactor).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts — Action/command adapters (extraction candidate P1).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetHint.ts — Hint scoring harness (P2 candidate).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts — save/load adapters (P2 candidate).
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts — transcript mapping (P2 candidate).
- Related work items (worklog):
  - Main Street (epic) — CG-0MM4R9UJF1DGI0ZF
  - Main Street: PRD Milestone 6 -- Engine Component Extraction and Refactoring — CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC (PRD created; contains OPEN QUESTION about scope which is resolved by this intake)
  - Migrate Main Street — CG-0MOZNY43I0029F7C

Related work (automated report)

data.description:
Problem statement

When cards are automatically promoted from a tableau column to the top row in the Beleaguered Castle scene, there is currently no visual movement animation to show the transfer. Players can miss what happened during auto-moves. This work will add a clear, consistent animation (and SFX) for auto-promoted cards so the board updates are visually traceable and the UX matches hand-played moves.

Users

- Casual players: Want to visually follow what the game is doing so the board state feels comprehensible and satisfying.
- Playtesters / QA: Need deterministic animations to validate transcripts and to avoid flaky visual tests.

Example user stories

- As a player, when the game auto-promotes a card from a column to the top row, I can watch the card move so I understand the change.
- As a QA engineer, I can run the Beleaguered Castle automated browser tests and see animations complete before assertions run.

Success criteria

1. Single-card auto-promotes animate with a smooth movement from source position to target top-row position, using existing UI animation helpers where appropriate.
2. When multiple cards are auto-promoted in one event, animations run sequentially with a short stagger between starts (default stagger: 100ms) and complete within the scene's animation timing constants (ANIM_DURATION in Beleaguered Castle constants).
3. A suitable SFX is played for each promoted card using existing SFX_KEYS (SFX_KEYS.CARD_TO_FOUNDATION or SFX_KEYS.AUTO_COMPLETE_CARD) and should be toggleable by existing settings (obey scene/global SFX enabled flag).
4. All new behavior is covered by automated tests (unit or browser tests) that assert animations are started and that the scene emits or waits for the existing "animation-complete" semantics before state-settled transitions.
5. All related documentation is updated (code comments, Beleaguered Castle README/help content, and any relevant docs). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Use existing animation helpers in src/ui where possible (moveGameObject, placeCard, etc.) rather than inventing a new low-level tweening approach.
- Respect Beleaguered Castle timing constants (example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleConstants.ts) and the scene's transcript/turn-controller flow so that animations do not desynchronize game logic or transcript recording.
- Keep changes localized to the Beleaguered Castle scene/renderer/turn-controller or to a narrowly-scoped animator helper in src/ui if reuse is clearly beneficial.
- Do not alter game rules or state transitions; animations are purely visual and must not change move application logic.

Existing state

- The game rules compute auto-promote moves (BeleagueredCastleRules.findSafeAutoMoves / getAutoCompleteMoves) and the TurnController applies moves; however, the renderer/path that applies auto-moves to the board does not animate promoted cards to the top row currently.
- There is precedent in the repo for similar work: items implementing card/noble movement animations and SFX hooks, and an open work item CG-0MM2DD29P0GRV6M4 that targets foundation auto-move animation and sound in Beleaguered Castle.
- Animation helpers and constants exist in src/ui (moveGameObject, placeCard, dealCard, etc.) and example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes contain renderer and turn-controller code responsible for visual updates.

Desired change

- Implement an animation path for auto-promoted cards in Beleaguered Castle that:
  - Uses existing ui helpers where possible.
  - Plays the configured SFX per card movement.
  - Runs sequentially when multiple cards are moved, with a 100ms start-stagger by default.
  - Ensures the scene's transcript/timing semantics are preserved (i.e., the TurnController waits for animations to complete when appropriate).
- Add tests that assert animation invocation and completion hooks are respected and update relevant documentation/help content.

Related work (automated report)

- CG-0MM2DD29P0GRV6M4 — "Animate and play sound for auto-moved cards to foundation in Beleaguered Castle" (open): Directly related; targets the same feature space (auto-moves → foundation/top row) and should be linked as potentially duplicate or sibling. Source: Worklog search.
- CG-0MO4LWWWC006HSNZ — "Core Card Animations" (completed): Contains shared animation patterns and helpers that may be re-used or referenced when implementing this feature. Source: Worklog search.
- CG-0MP0B5190004IVC9 — "Extract MainStreetAnimator" (completed): Example of extracting animator functionality into a reusable object; useful precedent for extracting a Beleaguered-specific animator or reusing a small animator helper.
- example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts: Handles creation and refresh of card visuals in the scene; a primary integration point for applying animations.
- example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleTurnController.ts: Orchestrates move execution, auto-complete, and transcript recording; changes here must preserve transcript semantics.
- example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleConstants.ts: Contains ANIM_DURATION, AUTO_COMPLETE_DELAY, and SFX_KEYS used by the scene; implementation must use these constants.
- src/ui/moveGameObject.ts (and placeCard.ts / dealCard.ts): Reusable animation helpers that should be preferred.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this work the same as CG-0MM2DD29P0GRV6M4 and should be merged/treated as the same item?" — Answer (user): "A" (Yes — merge / mark duplicate and continue work on the existing item CG-0MM2DD29P0GRV6M4). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "How should multiple auto-promoted cards be shown?" — Answer (user): "A" (Sequential: animate one card at a time with a short stagger (default: 100ms between starts)). Source: interactive reply. Final: Sequential with 100ms stagger.
- Q: "Should a sound play when a card auto-moves to the top row/foundation?" — Answer (user): "A" (Yes — use existing SFX_KEYS.CARD_TO_FOUNDATION / AUTO_COMPLETE_CARD as appropriate). Source: interactive reply. Final: Yes, use existing SFX keys.

Research & evidence summary

- Commands executed during intake: `wl show CG-0MOYCJXN4009W3VD --json`, `wl search animate --json`, `rg` over the repository to locate Beleaguered Castle scene files and animation helpers. Key files inspected: example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts, BeleagueredCastleTurnController.ts, BeleagueredCastleConstants.ts, src/ui/index.ts and animation helpers.

Notes on idempotence

- This draft includes the Appendix and Related work report. Re-running the intake will reuse the same work item id (CG-0MOYCJXN4009W3VD) and will not duplicate Appendix entries; existing Appendix entries should be updated rather than re-appended if repeated.

Problem statement

The Sushi Go! example game's SVG icon assets are rendering as solid black squares in the in-browser game, preventing players from seeing the intended icons (nigiri, maki, tempura, etc.) and degrading the UI.

Users

- Players (developers and playtesters) using the local dev server (npm run dev) to run Sushi Go!.
  - As a developer running the game locally, I need the sushi icon graphics to render as intended so I can verify gameplay and visuals.
  - As a playtester, I need the visual icons to be visible so I can understand card types at a glance.

Success criteria

- Reproduce the black-square rendering locally (npm run dev) and capture a failing screenshot.
- Identify root cause (assets, loader, texture handling, bundler/Vite/Phaser config or browser rendering) and document it in the work item.
- Implement fix so that locally served Sushi Go renders SVG icons correctly in Chromium and Firefox (dev server).
- Add a regression test or playwright screenshot test that loads the Sushi Go scene in replay mode and verifies at least one icon's pixel area is not a solid single color (or compares to a golden screenshot).
- Update docs: public/assets/sushi-go/STYLE.md and public/assets/CREDITS.md if any asset changes are needed; update SushiGoScene preload comments if loader behavior changes.
- All project tests pass (npm test) and the fix is covered by a test validating UI rendering as described above.

Constraints

- Prefer minimal changes: identify whether the issue is caused by asset content (SVG markup), Phaser's SVG loader behavior, or Vite static asset handling. Avoid wholesale changes to asset formats unless required for browser compatibility.
- Keep compatibility with existing build pipeline (Vite dev server, production build) and with the engine's asset loading helpers (this.load.svg(...)).
- Do not change game visuals unnecessarily; preserve original SVG vector art and styling where possible.

Existing state

- Example scene (example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts) preloads icons with this.load.svg(key, `assets/sushi-go/${fn}`) and creates images with this.add.image(...).
- SVG files exist in public/assets/sushi-go/, and individual files (e.g., icon-nigiri-salmon.svg) look like valid SVGs with fill and stroke attributes.
- The issue is reported for local dev server only (user selected A). The user marked cause as unknown (C) and asked the agent to run Playwright to capture console/log evidence if needed.

Desired change

- Diagnose root cause and implement minimal corrective change (asset fix, loader configuration tweak, or build/serve config) so SVGs render correctly.
- Add an automated Playwright / screenshot test to prevent regression.
- Update related docs if asset regeneration or export scripts are updated.

Related work (manual discovery)

- example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts — Preloads SVGs and renders them with this.add.image(); primary code paths to inspect.
- public/assets/sushi-go/icon-*.svg — The SVG files; inspect for problematic markup (e.g., missing xmlns, use of <foreignObject>, unsupported filters, or CSS relying on external fonts).
- public/assets/sushi-go/STYLE.md — Document describing SVG style and export steps; includes suggested export command using tools/export-sushi-icons.js.
- public/assets/CREDITS.md — Mentions public/assets/sushi-go/icon-*.svg (asset attribution).
- tests/sushi-go-icons.test.ts — Tests referencing the sushi-go icons directory (useful for verifying presence and filenames).

Related work (automated report)

- Worklog item: SVG in Sushi Go have gone (CG-0MOYCWCCX002Q0GW) — current intake target.
- Files: public/assets/sushi-go/ (icon-*.svg) — the actual assets that fail to render; inspected and appear to contain valid SVG shapes.
- File: example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts — uses Phaser's this.load.svg and this.add.image; relevant for loader/texture usage.
- File: public/assets/sushi-go/STYLE.md — documents expected SVG authoring/export; may contain hints if assets were recently regenerated.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where are you seeing the black squares?" — Answer (user): "A" (Local dev server). Final: yes.
  - Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "When did this start happening?" — Answer (user): "C" (Recently but unknown cause). Final: yes.
  - Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Do you have browser console errors or a screenshot (esp. any CORS or MIME-type warnings)?" — Answer (user): "C - you can do this yourself with playwright" (user asked agent to run Playwright). Final: yes.
  - Source: interactive reply.

Notes / Observations

- The SushiGoScene code checks this.textures.exists(iconKey) before adding image; ensure textures are actually created by the loader and not substituted by fallback rectangle/sprite.
- Common causes to investigate:
  1) Vite dev server serving SVGs with incorrect MIME-type or transformed in a way that Phaser's SVG loader cannot parse.
  2) Phaser's svg loader or the browser rasterization producing a black rect when internal SVG uses currentColor or CSS variables not supported when inlined as images.
  3) SVG contains unsupported features (external CSS, fonts, <filter> with cross-origin resources) that cause missing rendering.
  4) The texture is present but its pixels are black due to fill/stroke attributes being inherited incorrectly when the SVG lacks explicit fill colors.

Open questions

- Confirm whether the issue reproduces in both Chromium-based and Firefox browsers.
- If Playwright capture shows console errors (CORS/MIME or SVG parsing), record them here and link to the failing screenshot.

-- end of intake draft

data.description:
# Extract SVG & card rendering into shared engine helpers and migrate Sushi Go

Problem statement

Sushi Go currently uses Phaser's this.load.svg(...) and in-scene rendering, while Main Street implements DPR-aware rasterisation (SvgTextureHelpers) and a DOM-based SVG renderer (SvgDomRenderer) under example-games. There is no centralized, engine-level SVG/card rendering helper in src/ that can be reused across example games. Extracting the rasterisation and DOM SVG techniques into a shared core-engine module and migrating Sushi Go to use them will unify rendering, reduce duplication, and make SVG rendering more robust across browsers and DPRs.

Users

- Developers maintaining example games and engine modules.
  - As a developer, I want a single, well-documented API for rasterising SVGs and rendering card art so I can reuse it in multiple example games.
  - As an integrator, I want Sushi Go to render icons consistently across browsers without ad-hoc workarounds.
- QA / CI: Playwright tests that validate rendering will benefit from consistent rendering behavior.

Success criteria

- A shared SVG rendering helper module is added to src/ (e.g., src/ui/SvgHelpers.ts) exposing rasteriseSvgToTexture, makeTextureKey, getOrCreateTexture, and a DOM renderer wrapper or adapter.
- SushiGoScene is migrated to use the new shared helpers (either rasterisation to size-specific textures or DOM renderer fallback) instead of calling this.load.svg directly.
- All existing unit and browser tests pass locally (npm test) and the Sushi Go browser rendering test (SushiGoIcons.browser.test.ts) shows non-solid icon pixels.
- Docs updated: README or docs/DEVELOPER.md and public/assets/sushi-go/STYLE.md updated with guidance for asset authors.
- A small compatibility adapter is provided so existing code that uses templateKeyForCard or previous texture keys continues to work.
- A lightweight Playwright browser test is added that renders a small set of representative sample cards using the new core-engine helpers, asserts that textures/images are created and are not solid-colour, and captures a screenshot (golden or pixel-sample) suitable for CI. The test should be fast and deterministic (seed RNG where applicable) and live under the tests/ or tests/playwright/ area.

Constraints

- Keep changes minimal and backward compatible for existing games: prefer adding a shared helper and an adapter rather than rewriting all game assets.
- Ensure DPR-aware rasterisation to produce crisp textures on HiDPI displays.
- Avoid introducing large runtime performance penalties; generate textures lazily or on-demand as done in Main Street.

Problem statement

Migrate the Hello World example scene to use the centralized core-engine SVG helpers (SvgHelpers) so SVG assets are rasterised and managed consistently with other example games. The migration should adopt lazy generation of textures and may change asset keys / the public API used by the scene.

Users

- Developers maintaining example-games and engine contributors who need a canonical example of using SvgHelpers.
- CI / test runners that verify example scenes boot and rasterisation works via automated browser smoke tests.

User stories

- As an engine developer, I want HelloWorldScene to use the shared SvgHelpers so that SVG rasterisation and texture caching are consistent across example games.
- As a test author, I want an automated smoke test that asserts the scene boots and created textures are available when the scene is shown.

Success criteria

1. HelloWorldScene no longer calls this.load.svg in preload; instead it uses core-engine SvgHelpers (getOrCreateTexture / rasteriseSvgToTexture) following lazy generation semantics.
2. The scene compiles and boots in the browser; a new automated browser smoke test asserts the scene boots and the two card textures are available (either ready.sync or their promise resolves).
3. Any public API/key changes are documented and the HelloWorldScene code is updated accordingly; the example runs without runtime console errors.
4. All related documentation (code comments, README, docs/DEVELOPER.md) is updated to reflect the migration and recommended usage patterns.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

Constraints

- Migration should be shallow: do not refactor unrelated scene logic or introduce broad API surface changes beyond what is necessary for lazy SVG rasterisation.
- Avoid DOM renderer fallbacks; use the canonical rasteriseSvgToTexture / getOrCreateTexture flow from src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts.
- The change must be small and low-risk to keep CI stable; the Hello World example should remain a minimal proof of concept.

Existing state

- example-games/hello-world/scenes/HelloWorldScene.ts currently calls this.load.svg('ace_of_spades', 'assets/cards/ace_of_spades.svg', {...}) and this.load.svg('card_back', 'assets/cards/card_back.svg', {...}) in preload and then references texture keys directly in create.
- src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts exposes makeTextureKey, rasteriseSvgToTexture, getOrCreateTexture and scene validity helpers (markSceneValid / markSceneInvalid).
- Related migrations (Sushi Go, The Mind, Lost Cities) and docs exist and can be used as references.

Desired change

- Replace the HelloWorldScene preload usage with a lazy-rasterisation approach that either:
  - Uses getOrCreateTexture(scene, templateId, svgText, width, height) and awaits the returned promise when necessary, or
  - Calls rasteriseSvgToTexture with an explicit key if synchronous texture creation is required in create.
- If template ids or texture keys are changed, update any scene references and add short migration notes in docs/DEVELOPER.md and the example README.
- Ensure markSceneValid(this) is called at an appropriate lifecycle point to allow SvgHelpers to operate safely.
- Add a browser smoke test under tests/hello-world validating that HelloWorldScene boots and the two textures are available / their promises resolve.

Related work

- CG-0MOZN33JW004XILY — Migrate lost-cities SVG usage to core-engine SvgHelpers (open) — similar per-scene migration.
- CG-0MOZNY9O0008NEKT — Scan & Create Migrations (completed) — script that scanned example-games for svg loads.

- CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV — Migrate the-mind SVG usage to core-engine SvgHelpers (completed) — example migration reference.
- CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89 — SVG, Texture & Tooltip Helpers (open) — broader helpers that may be referenced.
- CG-0MOZNYCLW008H4K4 — Docs & Migration Guide (completed) — documentation to update with migration notes.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Migration policy: should the HelloWorld scene use a \"shallow, behaviour-preserving\" migration (preload SVGs via fetch + synchronous await so textures are ready before create, matching current preload behaviour), or can it use \"lazy generation\" (defer rasterisation to first use via getOrCreateTexture and accept that textures may be generated asynchronously at runtime)?" — Answer (user): "B" (Lazy generation). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Backwards compatibility: do you want to keep the same asset keys ('ace_of_spades', 'card_back') and scene code that refers to those keys (i.e., replace internal loading mechanism only), or is changing the public API / keys acceptable?" — Answer (user): "B" (Change keys / API acceptable). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Tests & verification: For acceptance, should we add a small browser smoke test validating that HelloWorldScene boots and the two textures exist (or render) when the scene is shown, or is a manual visual test sufficient?" — Answer (user): "A" (Add automated browser smoke test asserting texture existence and scene boots). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Related worklog items were discovered via wl search for "svg". Final: yes.

OPEN QUESTIONS

- If template ids or texture key naming conventions change, should we adopt the exact makeTextureKey(templateId, width, height, dpr) pattern for exported keys in example code, or provide a thin adapter that maintains the old keys? (OPEN QUESTION directed to repo maintainers: affects compatibility and clarity of example.)

# Migrate lost-cities SVG usage to core-engine SvgHelpers

## Problem statement

`LostCitiesScene.ts` preloads 121 SVGs via `scene.load.svg()`, duplicating rasterisation logic that should go through the shared `SvgHelpers` pipeline. Migrate to lazy rasterisation (`getOrCreateTexture`/`rasteriseSvgToTexture`), following the pattern established by the hello-world and The Mind migrations.

## Users

- **Engine maintainers** — benefit from a single shared SVG rasterisation path for correctness, caching, and DPR-aware texture generation.
- **Game authors (Lost Cities)** — want no visual or functional regressions in card rendering after the migration; cards should render correctly in both full-size and discard-size variants.
- **QA/CI** — deterministic tests and headless integration checks that verify textures are available when needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LostCitiesScene.ts` no longer calls `this.load.svg()` in `preload()`; uses `SvgHelpers` (`getOrCreateTexture`/`rasteriseSvgToTexture`) with lazy generation and `markSceneValid(this)`.

2. All card textures (5 colors × 12 cards + back — both full-size and discard variants) are available across browser and headless environments; no missing-texture errors during normal gameplay.

3. Focused unit tests (e.g., `tests/lost-cities/texture-helpers.test.ts`) cover inline helper functions for key generation, SVG text caching, and `getOrCreateTexture`-based retrieval for at least one full-size card, one discard-size card, and the card back.

4. Existing Lost Cities tests pass; any API-driven test updates are minimal and documented.

5. Code comments and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` updated to reflect the migration and lazy rasterisation policy.

6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

7. All related documentation is updated to reflect changes, including code comments, README, and relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Shallow migration**: do not refactor unrelated scene logic, rendering, or game mechanics. The only change is to replace the SVG loading mechanism.
- **Inline approach**: helper functions for texture key generation and lazy rasterisation are placed directly in the relevant files (e.g., `LostCitiesScene.ts` and/or `LostCitiesRenderer.ts`), not in a separate adapter module.
- **Lazy rasterisation**: textures are created on first use via `getOrCreateTexture`; do not eagerly rasterise all 121 SVGs during preload.
- **Avoid DOM renderer fallbacks**: use the canonical `rasteriseSvgToTexture`/`getOrCreateTexture` flow from `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`.
- **Compatibility**: preserve the `cardAssetKey()` and `compactAssetKey()` functions so that existing card display logic continues to work; update texture key references in `LostCitiesRenderer.ts` to resolve DPR-aware keys via the inline helpers.
- **Asset keys may change**: DPR-aware texture keys (e.g., `ms_card_lc-blue-2_95x130@2`) will differ from the current template IDs (`lc-blue-2`); callers that rely on raw texture key strings must be updated accordingly.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: The migration could expand beyond SVG loading into broader refactoring of Lost Cities rendering or scene logic. *Mitigation: explicitly limit changes to SVG loading/renderer texture key updates; record opportunities for additional refactoring as separate work items linked to this one.*
- **Visual regression risk**: DPR-aware texture keys or rasterisation quality changes could cause cards to render at incorrect sizes or with visual artifacts. *Mitigation: focused tests asserting key generation and at least one browser smoke test verifying texture availability; manual visual check recommended before closing.*
- **Merge conflict risk with CG-0MPDWZ8OI0021TSQ**: The related "Port lost-cities to use shared HandView & PileView" work item may touch overlapping files and create merge conflicts. *Mitigation: coordinate implementation order; if conflicts arise, rebase one branch onto the other.*
- **Performance risk**: Lazy rasterisation of 121 SVGs on first use may cause visible texture-pop during gameplay. *Mitigation: SvgHelpers caches in-flight and completed textures; textures remain cached for the scene lifetime. If pop is noticeable, pre-rasterise a subset (e.g., card back and common ranks) eagerly while deferring the rest.*
- **Assumption: SvgHelpers API is stable**: The `getOrCreateTexture` and `makeTextureKey` signatures used in prior migrations remain unchanged. If the API has evolved, migration will need to adapt. *Low probability based on recent commits.*

## Existing state

- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` preloads 121 SVGs via 5 `this.load.svg()` call blocks:
  - Full-size cards (lines ~84-98): 60 card faces + 1 back at `CARD_W=95, CARD_H=130`
  - Discard-size cards (lines ~103-119): 60 card faces (with `-sm` suffix) at `DISCARD_CARD_W=57, DISCARD_CARD_H=78`
- `example-games/lost-cities/LostCitiesCards.ts` provides `cardAssetKey()` and `compactAssetKey()` which return template IDs like `lc-blue-2` and `lc-blue-2-sm`.
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts` uses `this.scene.add.image(x, y, cardAssetKey(card))` and `CARD_BACK_KEY` to create card sprites — these texture key references need updating for DPR-aware keys.
- `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` provides `fetchSvgText`, `makeTextureKey`, `rasteriseSvgToTexture`, `getOrCreateTexture`, `markSceneValid`, and `markSceneInvalid`.
- SVG assets live under `public/assets/cards/lost-cities/` (121 files).
- Prior migrations (hello-world CG-0MOZN33BH001UF1L, The Mind CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV) followed the same pattern and serve as references.

## Desired change

1. **Remove `this.load.svg()` calls** from `LostCitiesScene.preload()` and replace with `markSceneValid(this)`.
2. **Add inline helper functions** in `LostCitiesScene.ts` (or a co-located helper file) that:
   - Fetch SVG text (or cache it from preload-file reads)
   - Wrap `getOrCreateTexture` for full-size and discard-size card textures
   - Provide stable texture key lookup that translates template IDs to DPR-aware keys
3. **Update `LostCitiesRenderer.ts`** to use the inline helpers instead of raw `cardAssetKey()` / `CARD_BACK_KEY` strings when creating card sprites.
4. **Add focused tests** (e.g., `tests/lost-cities/texture-helpers.test.ts`) verifying key generation, caching semantics, and texture retrieval for a representative card sample.
5. **Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md`** with a short migration note.

## Related work

- **CG-0MOZNXU4Y0043NR3 — Shared SVG Helpers** (completed) — created `SvgHelpers` API (`src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`) being migrated to.
- **CG-0MOZN33BH001UF1L — Migrate hello-world SVG usage to SvgHelpers** (completed) — first per-scene migration; established the pattern with browser smoke test.
- **CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV — Migrate the-mind SVG usage to SvgHelpers** (completed) — The Mind migration epic; established lazy rasterisation with adapter pattern.
- **CG-0MP12H40Q003Y7OU — Implement migration: MindCardRenderer -> SvgHelpers** (completed) — detailed child epic with MindCardTextureAdapter and focused tests.
- **CG-0MPAVIGJ5004YBLZ — Scan: find other scene.load.svg usage and schedule migrations** (completed) — scan that identified the 5 SVG load blocks in LostCitiesScene.ts.
- **CG-0MPAZX4KL002MXNX — Duplicate of this item** (closed as duplicate).
- **CG-0MPDWZ8OI0021TSQ — Port lost-cities to use shared HandView & PileView** (open) — related refactoring for Lost Cities that may touch overlapping files (LostCitiesScene.ts, LostCitiesRenderer.ts); coordinate implementation order to avoid merge conflicts.
- **CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I — Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components** (epic, open) — broader effort that includes lost-cities as one of its targets; may create additional changes to the same files.
- **`src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`** — the shared SVG rasterisation helpers.
- **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`** — developer guidance (contains SVG rendering & migration section from prior migrations).

## Related work (automated report)

A conservative search of Worklog and repository files identified the following items with clear relevance to this SVG migration:

- **CG-0MOZN33BH001UF1L — Migrate hello-world SVG usage to SvgHelpers** (completed) — Most directly comparable migration. It replaced 2 `scene.load.svg()` calls with lazy rasterisation via `getOrCreateTexture`, added a browser smoke test, and followed the "shallow migration" constraint. The implementation pattern (remove load.svg → markSceneValid → inline helper → update texture keys in renderer → add focused tests) should be replicated here with the larger Lost Cities card set.
- **CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV — Migrate the-mind SVG usage to SvgHelpers** (completed) — The Mind migration epic. Established the lazy rasterisation policy documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`. Its child CG-0MP12H40Q003Y7OU contains the most detailed implementation reference, including a MindCardTextureAdapter (though this item uses an inline approach instead of a separate adapter).
- **CG-0MP12H40Q003Y7OU — Implement migration: MindCardRenderer -> SvgHelpers** (completed) — Contains the detailed implementation pattern: replacing `scene.load.svg` with `markSceneValid(this)` in preload, using `getOrCreateTexture` for lazy rasterisation, and updating callers to use DPR-aware texture keys. Also includes the Node/test preload path that populates an SVG text cache for headless testing — a pattern this migration should follow.
- **CG-0MOZNXU4Y0043NR3 — Shared SVG Helpers** (completed) — Created the SvgHelpers API (`src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`) that this migration targets. Understanding the API surface (`makeTextureKey`, `getOrCreateTexture`, `rasteriseSvgToTexture`, `markSceneValid`, `markSceneInvalid`, `fetchSvgText`) is essential.
- **CG-0MPAVIGJ5004YBLZ — Scan: find other scene.load.svg usage and schedule migrations** (completed) — The scan that precisely identified the 5 SVG load blocks in `LostCitiesScene.ts` (lines 84, 91, 97, 106, 113 in the version scanned). Confirms no other files in lost-cities use `scene.load.svg`.
- **`example-games/the-mind/MindCardRenderer.ts`** — Reference file showing the complete migration pattern: preload changes, svgTextCache for headless tests, markSceneValid, and ensureMindCardTexture wrapping getOrCreateTexture.
- **`tests/the-mind/mind-card-renderer.test.ts`** and **`tests/the-mind/headless.test.ts`** — Reference test files showing unit and headless integration test patterns for migrated SVG rendering.
- **CG-0MPDWZ8OI0021TSQ — Port lost-cities to use shared HandView & PileView** (open) — Targets the same `LostCitiesScene.ts` and `LostCitiesRenderer.ts` files. If worked on concurrently, will create merge conflicts. Recommend completing this SVG migration first or coordinating branch strategy.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "How should the migration handle texture key adapters — create a separate `LostCitiesTextureAdapter.ts` (The Mind pattern) or inline the helpers directly in the scene/renderer files?" — Answer (user): "Inline" (no separate adapter module). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "What testing approach should be used — primarily update existing tests, or add new focused tests?" — Answer (user): "Add focused tests" (e.g., `tests/lost-cities/texture-helpers.test.ts`). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "There are two work items with the same title and GitHub issue #586 — CG-0MOZN33JW004XILY (May 10) and CG-0MPAZX4KL002MXNX (May 18). How should the duplicate be handled?" — Answer (user): "Proceed as recommended" — closed CG-0MPAZX4KL002MXNX as duplicate of CG-0MOZN33JW004XILY. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Research notes (agent inference): inspected `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` (121 SVG loads in 5 blocks), `example-games/lost-cities/LostCitiesCards.ts` (cardAssetKey/compactAssetKey functions), `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts` (uses raw texture keys), `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` (API surface). Reviewed completed migrations for hello-world and The Mind to confirm patterns. Related worklog items discovered via `wl search`.

data.description:
Problem statement

Intermittent browser test runtime failure: a TypeError "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'resolution')" originating in Phaser rendering during MainStreetScene browser tests. The failure is intermittent and causes npm test to exit non-zero.

Users

- Developers running the test suite (local and CI) who need reliable, non-flaky tests.
- QA engineers and release managers relying on automated tests to gate changes.

Example user stories

- As a developer, I want npm test to complete without intermittent runtime errors so I can confidently validate changes locally and in CI.
- As a QA engineer, I want the browser tests to be deterministic so regressions are easier to triage.

Success criteria

- Reproduce the error deterministically or clearly characterize the conditions that cause the flake (viewport, timing, asset loading sequence, environment). Measurable: documented repro steps or an automated harness that reproduces the failure.  
- Identify the root cause or causes that lead to texture resolution being null when accessed in the Phaser rendering path and produce a short technical note describing the root cause.  
- Implement a durable fix so that the rendering path no longer attempts to read resolution from a null texture under normal test runs. Measurable: code change merged with tests or guards.  
- Add short-term defensive guard(s) if necessary to prevent unhandled exceptions while the root cause is addressed. Measurable: npm test runs to completion in repeated local runs (e.g., 50 consecutive runs without the unhandled error) or equivalent automated check.  
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.  
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Tests run under Vitest in a headless/DOM environment; Phaser v4 RC is used in the project. Any fix must be compatible with our current Phaser and test harness versions.  
- Avoid large refactors unless a small, targeted change cannot resolve the root cause.  
- Preserve existing game behaviour and visual fidelity; defensive guards must not hide real rendering regressions.

Existing state

- Work item CG-0MOZQNA6T008GNW9 records the failing error and has initial acceptance criteria: reproduce/characterize, guard/fix null texture resolution, ensure npm test completes.  
- Failure observed in tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts where a transfer animation test runs; stack from Vitest indicates reading `resolution` of null.  
- Related items and experiments exist that touch SVG loading, shared SVG helpers, and earlier RCA experiments (see Related work below).

Desired change

- Reproduce the failure reliably or narrow down the exact triggering conditions (timing, viewport, DPR, asset type, loader path).  
- Instrument the renderer/texture-loading code to capture diagnostics when texture objects are null where resolution is expected.  
- Implement the durable fix (root-cause patch) that ensures textures are present before their resolution is read, or otherwise adjusts the load/render sequencing.  
- If the durable fix will take time, add a conservative defensive guard to prevent an unhandled exception and add a follow-up work item to complete the root-cause fix if necessary.

Related work (manual discovery)

- Root-Cause Analysis & Isolation Experiments — CG-0MOYKQNR6000KIJN
  Short: Completed experiments exploring hypotheses (Vite transform, Phaser loader, SVG markup, WebGL rasterization) and may contain lab-notebook evidence relevant to reproduction and fixes.

- SVG in Sushi Go have gone — CG-0MOYCWCCX002Q0GW
  Short: Investigated SVG loading and rasterization regressions; includes notes about Vite/SVG interactions and Phaser's SVG handling which may be relevant to null texture resolution.

- Shared SVG Helpers — CG-0MOZNXU4Y0043NR3
  Short: Extracted SVG handling into shared helpers; includes unit tests and integration demos that may show differences in texture creation/registration.

- Extract SVG & card rendering into shared engine helpers and migrate Sushi Go — CG-0MOZMT7G80090Y6S
  Short: Migration work that consolidated rendering paths; relevant for shared code paths that touch texture creation and DPR scaling.

- Add Playwright debug scripts for Sushi Go SVG rendering — CG-0MOZRJJKZ002SIN8
  Short: References that this intermittent Phaser resolution null error blocks some debug flows; contains Playwright scripts useful for reproduction.

- Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio — CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY
  Short: High-level visual polish guidance and integration notes for Main Street, may provide context about expected rendering behaviour.

Related repo docs/paths

- tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts — Test that surfaced the error.  
- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-4.md — Mentions the test and visual polish requirements.

Related work (automated report)

Related work (automated report):
- The worklog search for Phaser-related items returned multiple items likely relevant to rendering, SVG handling, and prior RCA experiments. These items were reviewed conservatively and included when they showed clear overlap with texture/asset loading, SVG rasterization, or test flakiness. See the manual list above for the high-confidence, hand-selected items.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where/how is the failure reproducible?" — Answer (user): "this was identified with local test run, but it is not clear under what conditions it occures". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Fix approach preference?" — Answer (user): "B" (Investigate and fix the root cause so texture is always present when accessed). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Any known recent changes or suspects?" — Answer (user): "B" (No / unknown — agent should proceed to reproduce and instrument). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Notes on idempotence

- This draft appends findings and related work conservatively and is intended to be updated in-place when the intake command is re-run. The Appendix records clarifying Q/A entries and will be updated rather than duplicated on subsequent runs.

Draft prepared for review.

## Summary
Beleaguered Castle can incorrectly end as a loss immediately after an early move even though the position still has productive continuations.

## User story
As a player, I want the game to continue whenever productive play still exists, so I am not incorrectly forced into a loss.

## Scope
- Investigate why game-end logic in `checkGameEnd()` can declare a loss while meaningful play remains.
- Add regression coverage for a concrete reproducible state.
- Fix the root cause.
- Include a small UX text improvement so end-state messaging is precise.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A failing test (added first) reproduces a false game-over scenario.
2. The root cause is fixed and the new regression test passes.
3. Existing Beleaguered Castle tests continue to pass.
4. No-moves overlay text is improved for clarity.
5. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

data.description:
Bug: In Feudalism, the tick marks used to indicate which tokens are selected to take during a turn remain visible after the turn ends.

User story:
As a player finishing my turn in Feudalism,
I want token-selection tick marks to clear automatically,
so that the next turn starts with a clean, accurate board state.

Expected behavior:
- When a turn ends, all token-selection tick indicators are cleared.
- The next turn should not show stale selections from the previous turn.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Ending a turn clears all token-selection tick marks in Feudalism.
2. Starting the next turn does not display previous turn tick marks.
3. Automated tests cover this regression and fail before the fix, pass after the fix.
4. Existing tests continue to pass.
data.title: Feudalism: Clear token-selection tick marks at end of turn

data.description:
Bug: In Feudalism, game end winner resolution currently favors the player who finishes first instead of the player with the highest influence.

User story:
As a player at end game,
I want the winner to be determined by highest influence,
so that final results match Feudalism scoring rules rather than turn order.

Expected behavior:
- At game end, the winner is the player with the greatest influence.
- Reaching the finish threshold first should not automatically win if another player ends with more influence.

Acceptance criteria:
1. End-game winner selection in Feudalism uses highest influence.
2. A player who triggered game end can still lose if another player has higher influence when game ends.
3. Regression tests fail before fix and pass after fix.
4. Existing tests continue to pass.
data.title: Feudalism: Determine winner by highest influence at game end (not first to finish)

Draft headline

Audit and extract reusable components from example-games into src/*; create child work items for the top-3 logical components and implement migrations with tests.

Problem statement

Inspect the repository's example-games/ modules to identify duplicated code and extract reusable components into src/* so shared functionality is implemented once, tested, and consumed by multiple games.

Users

- Engine maintainers and contributors who will benefit from reduced duplication, faster fixes, and lower maintenance cost.
- Example-game authors who will have simpler game code, stable shared APIs, and clearer migration paths.

User stories

- As an engine maintainer, I want shared helpers (rendering, input, save/load, timers) in src/* so fixes and improvements apply to all games without duplicated patches.
- As a game author, I want example-games to import stable core APIs so I can write smaller scene files and focus on game rules rather than boilerplate.

Success criteria

- SC-1: A triage report listing extraction candidates across example-games ranked by impact (high/medium/low) exists and is attached to the work item.
- SC-2: At least the top-3 extraction candidates are implemented as child work items (one child per logical component) with reproduction steps and tests specified.
- SC-3: Each extraction child includes unit tests that validate behaviour and at least one browser integration test demonstrating the migrated component works in one example game.
- SC-4: Example-games continue to build and tests referencing example-games pass after migrations (either via adapters or updated imports in the same PRs), and the full project test suite passes.
- SC-5: All related documentation (code comments, README, docs/*) is updated to reflect the new location and usage of extracted components.

Constraints

- Must not introduce runtime regressions: the extraction must be covered by unit and browser integration tests before merging.
- Preserve deterministic behaviour of game logic; where API changes are required for unification, make those changes in coordinated PR(s) that update example-games imports and tests (per stakeholder choice: allow renames in the same PRs).
- Avoid large, multi-purpose refactors in the same PR as a basic extraction; if scope grows, create follow-up work items and mark them as dependencies.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Scope creep — extraction work may reveal larger design opportunities. Mitigation: record additional features/refactors as separate, linked work items and keep this epic focused on the top-ranked candidates.
- Risk: Breaking changes — migrating code may introduce API changes that break example-games or tests. Mitigation: per stakeholder choice B, coordinated PRs that update example-games imports and tests are acceptable; ensure each migration includes tests and a short migration guide.
- Risk: Test coverage gaps — some behaviours may lack unit tests in example-games. Mitigation: require unit tests and at least one browser integration test for each migrated component; add test-only adapters where needed to preserve behaviour.
- Assumption: Completed Main Street extraction examples give valid patterns and tests that can be reused.

Existing state

- There are multiple completed extraction work items and PRs for Main Street and other games that serve as examples (see Related work). Several game modules already contain "Design Notes for M6 Extraction" comments indicating intended extraction points.
- The work item CG-0MP1244W1000R3E5 is in-progress at stage=idea and already assigned to Map.

Desired change

- Produce a ranked triage of reusable components across example-games, create an epic child work item for each top-ranked logical component (Renderer, InputHandler, SaveLoad/Transcript, Timer/ChallengeSystem, SVG rasterisation, Tooltip/UI helpers), implement extractions with tests and minimal adapter shims, and update example-games to consume the new src/* modules.

Related work

- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-6.md — Migration plan and file-level extraction notes for Main Street (recommended first target). Useful for planning the Main Street -> src/* migrations and contains acceptance criteria for M6.
